articleTitle: Drone Detection and Classification Based on Radar Cross Section Signatures
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, we show how drone detection and classification can be enabled by leveraging a database of radar cross section (RCS) signatures. First, we present a set of measurement results of the RCS of a carbon fiber drone model at 28 GHz. The measurements were performed in an anechoic chamber and provide essential information about the RCS signature of the specific drone. Then, we assess the RCS-based detection probability and the range error by running simulations in urban environments. The drones were positioned at different distances, from 30m to 90m, and the RCS signatures used for the detection and classification were obtained experimentally.

articleTitle: Link-Level and System-Level Simulation of 300 GHz wireless Backhaul Links
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: One of the goal of the EU-Japan joint project ThoR is to demonstrate the feasibility of the IEEE Standard 802.15.3d-2017 for backhaul/fronthaul links. This will be done in a realistic deployment scenario using both system-level and link-level simulations integrated in the same tool. Based on the system-level simulations, a wireless backhaul network for a given ultra-dense mobile network is automatically planned and analyzed. Exemplary links are then simulated using the link-level simulations. Preliminary results of both simulations are presented from a scenario in Hanover, Germany and showing the achievability of >100 Gbit/s data rate fully considering the current IEEE Std 802.15.3d-2017.

articleTitle: HAPS propagation loss model for urban and suburban environments
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: High-Altitude Platform Station (HAPS), which provides communication services from an altitude of 20 km via an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV), is attracting much attention as a new mobile communications platform for ultra-wide coverage areas and disaster-resilient networks. A HAPS can provide mobile communications services directly to smartphones. In order to design efficient cell configurations for HAPS-based services, we need a radio wave propagation model that takes into consideration factors such as terrain, vegetation, urban areas, suburban areas, and building entry loss. In this paper, we focus on the propagation loss at high elevation angles in urban and suburban areas. We measure and clarify the propagation loss characteristics at high elevation angles in urban and suburban areas and propose a new model based on the current clutter loss model.

articleTitle: Broadband RCS Reduction for Fabry-Perot Antenna with enhanced Bandwidth Using Polarization Conversion Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A Fabry-Perot (FP) antenna with enhanced bandwidth and wideband RCS reduction based on polarization conversion metasurface (PCM) is presented in this paper. The wide impedance bandwidth benefits from the two parasitic mushroom-shaped patches loaded on the radiating edges of source antenna to excite a new resonant mode (quasi-TM30 mode), and high gain-bandwidth is also achieved by using an irregular ground plane. The PCM units are arranged in chessboard configuration to form a superstrate, which is placed on the antenna to obtain good scattering characteristics.

articleTitle: Digitally Tunable Frequency Selective Surface for a Physical Layer Security System in the 5 GHz Wi-Fi Band
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, a digitally tunable Frequency Selec-tive Surface (FSS) for use in Physical Layer Security (PLS) systems is presented. The design of a unit cell is described, which is optimized by simulations for the frequency range of 5 GHz indoor Wi-Fi. Based on the developed unit cell, a prototype with 64 binary switchable elements is set up. The performance of the surface is demonstrated by measurements.

articleTitle: Radar-Based Automatic Detection of Sleep Apnea Using Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Early diagnosis of sleep-apnea-related breathing problems helps to avoid the increased risk they can cause. In this study, we performed simultaneous radar measurements and polysomnography on patients with sleep apnea. A support vector machine algorithm was applied to the radar data to automatically detect sleep apnea events. Support vector machine parameters were optimized using the relationship between the radar and polysomnography data. The support vector machine was found to be effective in noncontact detection of central/mixed sleep apnea events using radar data. The proposed approach achieved an accuracy of 79.5%, a recall of 71.2%, and a precision of 71.2%.

articleTitle: Automatic Planning of 300-GHz-Band Wireless Backhaul Link Deployment in Metropolitan Area
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes an algorithm for automatic planning of 300-GHz-band wireless backhaul link deployment. The algorithm consists of two steps; Selecting the pair of adjacent cells that can get a line of sight, and Deployment of base stations. We succeeded in the automatic planning of 300-GHz-band backhaul link in Shinjuku, Japan by using this algorithm. We conducted radio wave propagation simulation of the wireless backhaul links, and showed that SNR of 99.5 % of the wireless backhaul links deployed by using this algorithm exceeds the standard demand SNR for 100-Gbit/s data transmission even when the rain rate is 100 mm/hr.

articleTitle: Radio Propagation Prediction Using Neural Network and Building Occupancy Estimation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a radio propagation prediction method using machine learning and building occupancy estimation. There have been learning-based researches using aerial photographs and building occupancy images as spatial information. However, the availability of building occupancy images is often limited to urban areas. We assume the situation that only the aerial photographs are available and aim to improve radio propagation prediction accuracy by estimating building occupancy images from the given aerial photographs.

articleTitle: Polarization-Insensitive Dual-Band Frequency Selective Rasorber based on Concentric SRRs
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band frequency selective rasorber (FSR) has been presented based on concentric split ring resonator geometry. The proposed design comprises a top lossy layer and a bottom lossless layer separated by a quarter-wavelength thick air spacer. Theoretical analysis of the structure exhibits an overall absorption band ranging from 2.2 to 9.0 GHz (with a fractional bandwidth of 121.43%), whereas two discrete passbands appear at 3.54 and 9.0 GHz having insertion loss of 0.7 and 1 dB, respectively. In addition, the proposed topology is polarization-insensitive and angularly stable unlike the existing multi-band FSR geometries. The physical insights behind the absorption and transmission mechanism have also been explained by analyzing the surface current distribution of the structure.

articleTitle: A W-Band Corporate-Fed Hollow-Waveguide Slot Array Antenna by Glass Micromachining
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a W-band 16×16-element corporate-fed air-filled waveguide slot array antenna by glass micromachining technology. This antenna is constructed by laminating five layers of glass wafers. Each layer is innovatively fabricated by through glass via (TGV) technology. It is realized by using a laser-induced deep etching process, and has been applied initially to the advanced packaging field. According to the wet-etching process, a taper angle of 10° is taken into account during the design of glass wafers. In addition to the antenna's electromagnetic analysis, its mechanical and thermal characteristics are also simulated and analyzed to ensure the success of glass wafer bonding. As the experimental results, the antenna gain of 30.3 dBi at the center frequency 94 GHz, and the bandwidth of 13.3% for the antenna gain higher than 30 dBi are achieved in the W-band.

articleTitle: Conformal High Gain Aperture Antenna Based on Leaky-Wave Array for CubeSat Communication
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A high gain aperture antenna implemented by an array of leaky-wave antennas (LWAs) is proposed in this paper. The proposed array element (AE) is designed in a substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) with low profile, simple feeding and suitable dimension of 98.6×16×1.575 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> for the 1U CubeSat. The AE radiates in the direction of -45° with gain of 15.2 dBi at 28 GHz. By combining the radiation of such two AEs which are perpendicularly located at one corner of the CubeSat, a sum beam with gain of 17.4 dBi pointing at the diagonal direction is achieved. Because of the uniform amplitude and linear phase front of the leaky waves, the amplitude and phase front of the aperture antennas are uniform and linear too, leading to the high gain. A prototype of the AE is manufactured and tested to validate the proposed scenario and simulation results. The proposed aperture antennas is in low profile and conformal to the surface of the CubeSat.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of Optically Transparent Dual-Polarized Reflectarray with Suppressed Sidelobe Level
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An optically transparent reflectarray with upper sidelobe level (SLL) suppression is proposed for the fifth generation (5G) wireless communications in this paper. A unit cell of the reflectarray is composed of a crossed-dipole element to realize dual-polarized operation. In order to validate the improvement of upper SLL, a 45 degree-beam-steering reflectarray, comprising 20 × 10 elements, operating at 28 GHz for quasi-millimeter-wave applications is designed and investigated experimentally. Experimental results demonstrate that the worst value of all upper SLL in radiation pattern of the reflectarray is reduced by about 10 dB as compared to that in previous design.

articleTitle: Measured Performance of High Gain Dielectric Lens Antenna in 300 GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A dielectric lens antenna was designed at 270 GHz to achieve high gain performance. A plano-convex lens was designed using the geometrical optics theory. For primary radiators, a pyramidal horn antenna was proposed which can easily control the beamwidth to illuminate the lens with uniformity. The measured gain was 25.7 dBi at 270 GHz, and the measured half-power beamwidth (HPBW) was 7.4 degree.

articleTitle: Circular antenna arrangement for LOS-MIMO transmission independent for the transmission distance using a genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method that does not affect the transmission/reception distance and does not reduce channel capacity in circular array-type line-of-sight multiple-input-multiple-output (LoS-MIMO) transmission. In LoS-MIMO transmission, an optimum antenna element spacing is present depending on the transmission distance, but the transmission efficiency drops significantly, except for a certain transmission/reception distance. In this paper, the constraint condition of a circular array is provided in consideration of the implementation of the antenna arrangement. Subsequently, the optimum element arrangement of the antenna that does not depend on the transmission/reception distance and does not reduce the channel capacity in LoS-MIMO transmission is derived using a genetic algorithm, and its effect is clarified.

articleTitle: 2-D DOA Estimation for Coprime Cubic Array: A Cross-correlation Tensor Perspective
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a cross-correlation coarray tensor-based 2-D direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation method for coprime cubic array (CCA) is proposed. Since the CCA received signals characterized by two coprime tensors cannot be collectively shaped as a single tensor to operate auto-correlation, the cross-correlation is introduced to calculate the coarray tensor statistics of CCA. A Nyquist-matched 4-D coarray tensor is then obtained for 2-D DOA estimation, where the designed structured tensorization is applied without spatial smoothing. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Propagation Loss Model of Human Body Shielding in HAPS Communications
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: High-Altitude Platform Station (HAPS), which provides communications services from an altitude of 20 km via an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) is attracting much attention as a new mobile communications platform for ultra-wide coverage areas and disaster-resilient networks. HAPS can provide mobile communications services directly to smartphones. To offer mobile communications services directly to smartphones, a propagation loss model of human shielding that can consider elevation angles in various environments is required. In this paper, we propose a propagation loss model of human body shielding in HAPS communications.

articleTitle: Measurement of Glass Complex Permittivity at 200-500 GHz for THz Propagation Simulation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Terahertz (THz) band wireless link is promising candidate for the 6G mobile communication standard. However, there are a few experimental data on the reflectance and transmittance characteristics of building materials, such as glass, at the 300GHz band, which is necessary for THz-band radio wave propagation simulation. In this paper, we measured the complex permittivity of glasses at 200-500 GHz by using terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) and vector network analyzer (VNA), and compared these results. We conducted 300-GHz-band outdoor radio wave propagation simulation by using the measured complex permittivity of the glass.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Characteristics for NN and CNN in Path Loss Prediction
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In path loss prediction, recently machine learning approaches such as the convolutional neural network (CNN) have been attracting interest. Various models have been proposed that estimate the path loss characteristics by automatically extracting parameters from satellite photographs of buildings and so on. However, at present neither the estimation tendency nor the characteristics of the path loss estimation using NN and CNN are sufficiently clear. In this paper, we propose a CNN model constructed using the same concept as the NN model and evaluate the differences and tendencies of the RMS error.

articleTitle: Complex Permittivity Evaluation of Building Materials at 200-500 GHz Using THz-TDS
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In 6G mobile communication, 300-GHz-band terahertz (THz) system is a promising candidate for achieving ultra-high-speed wireless communication. However, the experimental data on the reflectance and transmittance of building materials at 300GHz were insufficient. In this paper, we employed terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) spectroscopy to obtain the complex permittivity of building materials, glass, concrete, and granite at 200-500 GHz in order to calculate the reflectance and transmittance of building materials. In THz-TDS spectroscopy, the effect of multiple reflections was removed by time-gating the acquired waveform. We conducted 300-GHz-band indoor propagation simulation by using the calculated complex permittivity of building materials.

articleTitle: High Gain Low Sidelobe Multibeam Shaped Lens Antenna at 24 GHz for Wind Profile Radar
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Wind profile radar system needs multibeam antenna with high gain, low sidelobe and dual-polarization to detect turbulence. An electronically beam-switching shaped dielectric lens with these features at 24 GHz for wind profile radar is presented in this paper. This lens antenna includes coma-correction zoning dielectric lens, 2*2 corrugated horn feed array, microstrip-to-waveguide transducer, and beam-switching control circuit. This multibeam lens antenna system can realize beam deflection of ±10° and dual-polarization with the maximum gain of 31 dBi and the sidelobe of -25 dBi.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Circularly Polarized Microstrip Antenna with Short-Ended Microstrip Line Perturbations
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a new configuration of a reconfigurable circularly polarized microstrip antenna employing switchable short-ended microstrip line perturbations. Diodes are integrated between the radiating patch element and perturbation segments for switchable function. Since simple short-ended microstrip lines are used as perturbations, simple structure with no additional bias networks is realized. Circular polarization switching capability between RHCP and LHCP is obtained by changing the switching voltage to the diodes. In this paper, the performance of the proposed antenna is discussed by simulated and experimental results.

articleTitle: Coarray-Based Pattern Synthesis for Minimum Hole Arrays
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents an approach to pattern synthesis based on the difference coarray of minimum hole arrays (MHAs), based on the relations between the weights on the physical array and the virtual weights on the difference coarray. From these relations, some virtual weights are selected as design variables. The remaining virtual weights and the weights on the physical array are then determined by these design variables. Numerical examples show that, if these design variables are samples of a Kaiser window, the proposed approach can achieve smaller beamwidth or lower sidelobe levels than some existing weight designs for the MHA.

articleTitle: Effective Use of Ka-band Based on Antenna and Radio Wave Propagation for Mobile Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: As the demand for Internet connection on ships and aircraft increases, the development of high-speed mobile communication technology using High-Throughput-Satellites (HTS) is underway. In Japan, an engineering test satellite named ETS-9 is being developed to establish the next-generation HTS technologies. In parallel with the development of the ETS-9, we have started the research and development of the ground communication systems to improve the frequency utilization efficiency while making full use of the functions of ETS-9. This paper gives an overview of the research and development of antenna systems to achieve the use of Ka-band efficiency.

articleTitle: Radar Modeling Experiment Using Vector Network Analyzer
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Radar modeling is an important method in the radar experiment. Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) as equipment that used for measuring the Scattering parameter of radio frequency (RF) Circuit can be applied to develop a radar model that is used in a certain radar experiment. The basic concept of radar modeling using VNA is discussed in this paper. The radar modeling sample and its result are also provided. Radar modeling using VNA provides flexibility in developing a radar experiment for many radar topologies and detection cases. The VNA-based radar model provides a good representation of the radar system that is studied.

articleTitle: SAR Target Recognition With Limited Samples Based on Meta Knowledge Transferring Using Relation Network
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a synthetic aperture radar (SAR) target recognition method based on meta knowledge transferring with relation comparison. Firstly, the meta knowledge is obtained based on a relation network by learning a distance metric from simulated data. Then, we retrain the network on the limited real SAR target samples to realize the meta knowledge transferring. Different from the conventional methods based on feature transferring, the meta knowledge learned from simulated data using relation network enables the model to adapt to the recognition task of real SAR data quickly, which is called “learning to learn”. Under the condition of limited training samples, the experimental results on MSTAR dataset verify the advantages of the proposed method compared with the conventional convolutional neural network (CNN)-based method.

articleTitle: A Circularly Polarized Cavity-Backed Stacked Patch Antenna for Wide-Angle Beam Scanning Millimeter-Wave Phased Array
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents design and measurement of a circularly polarized cavity-backed patch antenna for a low- profile active electronically scanned array with a beam- scanning capability over a wide angle. The proposed antenna comprises upper patches, a spacer, and pin-fed lower patches to achieve low axial ratio across a wide angle of view and high efficiency. Each component is bonded without any screws, which enhances the manufacturability of the antenna and prevents degradation of the radiation pattern. A 16-element array is fabricated and measured. The measured pattern for co-polarization agrees well with the simulated one, and scan loss is approximately 5.5 dB in the ± 70 ° directions. In addition, low axial ratio of approximately 4.5 dB is obtained even in the ±70 ° directions.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Band-Notched Absorber for Wideband RCS Reduction
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a polarization-insensitive miniaturized band-notched absorber with a wide operating bandwidth. The proposed geometry is comprised of a resistive top layer, band-reflective middle layer, and a ground plane, separated from one another by air spacers. The structure exhibits an operational bandwidth of 132.7% where absorption band is spread across the frequency ranges of 2.48-5.23 GHz and 7.68-12.26 GHz, whereas a band-notch response is obtained in between the absorption bands. The proposed topology is also angularly stable upto 45<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup> for both TE and TM polarizations. In addition, the overall footprint of the unit cell geometry is very small having lateral dimensions of 0.08λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub> × 0.08λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub> and thickness of 0.085λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub>, where λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub> corresponds to the lowest absorption frequency. The prototype of the structure has been fabricated as well as experimentally verified.

articleTitle: Proposal of Time Domain Near-Field Measurement System for 5G Antenna System
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a far-field estimation system at 28 GHz that does not require a reference signal input to the Antenna Under Test (AUT) by measuring an antenna system in the near-field and in the time domain.

articleTitle: Scattering Effect up to 100 GHz Band for 6G
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper clarifies frequency dependency of scattering effects from the building rough surface up to the 100 GHz band for 6G. From the measurements, it is found that the scattering are diffused as the frequency increases. Based on these results, we modeled scattering using directive scattering model and confirmed that the frequency dependency of the scattering can be predicted by changing the beam width of the directive scattering model according to the frequency.

articleTitle: Emulating Rician distributed channels in a hybrid chamber for OTA measurements
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: It has been shown by means of simulations that the rich isotropic multipath and the random line-of-sight channels and other Rician channels in-between can be successfully generated in the same over-the-air hybrid measurement chamber without the use of additional static or moving scatterers.

articleTitle: Interdigital and Multi-Via Structures for Mushroom-Type Metasurface Reflectors
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the novel patch element shapes with the interdigital and multi-via structures of a mushroom-type metasurface reflector are proposed. The interdigital structure provides a wide reflection phase range by changing the depth of the interdigital fingers. In addition, the multi-via structure provides the reflection phases near +180°. These structures have low polarization dependent properties. The desired reflection angles and sharp far field patterns of the reflected beams were obtained in the simulation results.

articleTitle: Quantitative Evaluation of the Decoupling Principle Between Two PIFAs by Using CMA
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In the previous study, we have proposed a novel decoupling method that does not require the adjustment of the original antennas by using parasitic elements (PEs), but the decoupling principle of the proposed method is not quantitatively evaluated. In this study, the usefulness of Characteristic Mode Analysis is utilized to quantitatively evaluate the decoupling principle of proposed method. The results show that inner product between the currents of port#1 and port#2 after using PEs is close to zero compared to that of before using PEs. In other words, PEs make these currents orthogonal to each other for decoupling.

articleTitle: Multi-Laptop-Antenna Designs for 2.4/5/6 GHz WLAN and 5G NR77/78/79 Operation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Two sets of the two-antenna systems in laptop computers are proposed. The first set comprises two WLAN antennas, each of which is fed by a coupling loop and having a conjoined, central T strip. The design is capable of new 6 GHz operation in addition to the current 2.4 and 5 GHz WLAN bands. The second set of the designs is a two-5G-NR-antenna system, covering the 3.3-5.0 GHz wideband and decoupled using the same loop shared by the feeding monopoles.

articleTitle: Design of Glass-Integrated Grid Antenna Using CMA for Multiband Indoor Network
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Integrate the antenna with the inherent glass structure of the buildings is a method of optimising the deployment of indoor base station. A triple-band glass-integrated grid antenna for indoor communications is presented in this paper. The antenna consists of three concentric square grid structures and is integrated into glass. With the help of characteristic modes analysis (CMA), three optimum operating modes are obtained and excited with single feeding, each resonant frequency can be tuned independently. To demonstrate the concept, a design for GSM at 1.8 GHz, WLAN at 2.4 GHz and low-frequency band for 5G at 3.5 GHz is provided.

articleTitle: Four-port DRA Array for MIMO Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A four-port MIMO antenna array comprising of four rectangular dielectric blocks (DBs) is presented. The -10 dB impedance bandwidth of the antenna is from 5.45 GHz to 6.05 GHz. The isolation between the antenna elements is enhanced by placing vertical metal plates between them and found to be greater than 20 dB with an inter-element spacing of 0.081 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">h</sub> (λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">h</sub>, = highest operating wavelength). The maximum gain of the antenna is noted to be 4.09 dBi with an envelope correlation coefficient ≤ 0.0044 in its entire bandwidth.

articleTitle: Verification of Underwater Position Estimation Using Received Power Profile Through Pseudo-Scale Model
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method based on the received power profile for diver position estimation in shallow sea using electromagnetic waves, and verify it by pseudo-scale model experiments. In our verification, we extract three regions in the sea where divers may exist based on the information of the diver's depth and the 1 dB margin of the received power, and examine the position estimation method to select the overlapping region.

articleTitle: Circularly-Polarized CTS Array Antenna for SatCom applications
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a circularly-polarized continuous transverse stub(CTS) array antenna for space applications. The radiating structure consists of open-ended parallel plate waveguides(PPW), supporting the propagation of the transverse electromagnetic(TEM) and first transverse electric(TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>) modes. Such modes are orthogonally-polarized in the PPW cross-section and, if properly excited, can generate circular polarization(CP). The antenna radiating section consists of 32 long slots, parallel-fed by a quasi-optical system through a PPW-based corporate feed network(CFN) and an electric field rotator. The proposed antenna is matched in the 27.5-31GHz band while scanning up to +-20° in elevation, with an axial ratio(AR) below 3dB.

articleTitle: Energy harvesting by applying Multi-Sector Yagi-Uda Rectenna
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes novel energy harvesting method using multi-sector Yagi-Uda antenna for wireless power transfer. The proposed structure applies the waveguide principle of the Yagi-Uda antenna. That is, the non-feeding element close to the power feeding element, which is the power transmitting unit, acts as a power receiving unit to light the LED, and at the same time, it acts as a director to transmit power to the next element. In this research, we propose to arrange this Yagi-Uda array in sectors around the wave source, which is the power transmission section, with the aim of further expanding the range of radio waves. The wireless power transmission efficiency obtained by each of the waveguide elements constituting the sector-arranged Yagi-Uda array from the feeding element was calculated from the S para obtained by the electromagnetic field simulation. Based on this result, it was clarified by experiments that an array composed of 3 elements each was arranged in 3 sectors around the wave source and all LEDs were lit.

articleTitle: Measurement of a microstrip antenna array fed by longitudinal slots on a narrow wall of the rectangular waveguide with standing-wave excitation for linear polarization perpendicular to the axis
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents measurement of a microstrip antenna array fed by longitudinal slots on a narrow wall of the rectangular waveguide with standing wave excitation for linear polarization perpendicular to the axis. A dual-ring microstrip antenna with a circumference of 5 wavelengths excited by the longitudinal slot on the narrow wall of the waveguide with a dielectric substrate is used as an element of the proposed array for grating lobe suppression due to the longitudinal slots arrayed at a spacing of one guided wavelength. In this paper, a prototype array consisting of the dual-ring microstrip antennas fed by three longitudinal slots on the narrow wall of the rectangular waveguide with standing-wave excitation is designed and fabricated. The measured results are agreed with the simulated ones obtained by HFSS. The measured radiation pattern reveals that grading lobes due to the longitudinal slots are well reduced by the proposed array. Validity of the design of the proposed array is confirmed by the measurement.

articleTitle: Measurement and analysis of arrival angle at MS in High Elevation Environment
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: HAPS which provides communication services from an altitude of 20 km via a UAV is being considered as a new mobile communications platform for an ultra-wide coverage areas and disaster-resilient networks. In order for HAPS to provide mobile communication services to smartphones, it is important to clarify the arrival angle profile in the high elevation environment. This paper present measured results and analyses of the radio arrival angle profile of the mobile station for the incoming wave from a helicopter in flight.

articleTitle: Recent Designs to Achieving Wideband MIMO Antenna for 5G NR Sub-6GHz Smartphone Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recently, many wideband MIMO antenna designs for smartphone applications have been reported to cover the 5G NR (new radio) band n77 (3300-4200 MHz), n78 (3300-3800 MHz), and n79 (4400-5000 MHz), in addition to WLAN 5GHz band (5150-5825 MHz). In this Invited Talk, the various design techniques to attain wide impedance bandwidth and good isolation will be addressed explicitly. Furthermore, two novel wide bandwidth 8-antenna array for 5G smartphone that can exhibit good 10-dB impedance bandwidth covering the 5G NR band n77/78/79 are presented and discussed as well.

articleTitle: A Microstrip-Line Gunn Oscillator Loaded Active Integrated Array Antenna Using Inclined Patches for Polarization Switching Function
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A polarization agile active integrated array antenna (AIAA), consisting of a microstrip-line Gunn oscillator loaded with dual-polarized array antenna is proposed for spatial modulation systems. By consolidating two single-pole single-throw (SPST) switches in the orthogonal feed lines, the dual-polarized array antenna is excited by either one of the feed lines to generate ±45° polarizations. The measured results validate the concept with an EIRP of +9.8 dBm, DC-to-RF efficiency of 0.32%, and around 10-dB cross polarization suppression.

articleTitle: Effectiveness of the virtual massive MIMO in 5G with OFDM
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In fifth generation (5G) and later systems (B5G/6G), the use of massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) with numerous antennas at the base station has drawn significant attention. However, the hardware scale of this method increases as the number of antennas increase. To solve this problem, we propose a technique to realize a virtual massive MIMO (VM-MIMO), with a single receiver. In this study, we show the effectiveness of the VM-MIMO in a 5G environment using orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) by computer simulation based on ray trace calculations.

articleTitle: Channel Capacity Estimation of 4 × 4 MIMO Antenna by Machine Learning, Considering SNR, Power Imbalance, and Correlation Coefficient
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study aimed to develop an accurate method for estimation of the channel capacity of 4 × 4 MIMO antenna systems by using a neural network. First, the channel capacity of an omnidirectional array antenna was calculated using the Monte Carlo method by changing the incident-wave signal-to-noise power ratio, power difference between the array elements, and correlation coefficient between the MIMO channels. Second, a neural network was used to evaluate the causal relation between the channel capacity and these parameters. The channel capacity predicted by the trained neural network matched well with the ones calculated using the Monte Carlo method.

articleTitle: High-Frequency Performance Improvement of LPDA for EMC/EMI Measurements
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A log-periodic dipole array with improved high-frequency performances for EMC/EMI measurements is proposed in this paper. In the proposed design, a saw-toothed shaped feed line is implemented. This modified feed arrangement allows dipole elements to be placed in the same horizontal plane, effectively suppressing the generation of the undesired vertical component electric field. The proposed LPDA offers on average VSWR of 1.49:1, a gain of 6.7 dBi, an FBR of 23.4 dB, an XPI of 26 dB, and E-plane HPBW of 63.6°.

articleTitle: Joint MIMO and Frequency Diverse Array for Suppressing Mainlobe Interferences
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper jointly exploits multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) increased degrees-of-freedom and frequency diverse array (FDA) range-dependent beampattern to suppress mainlobe interferences. The interferences caused by deceptive or false targets are separated firstly in the range dimension with blocking matrix method, and then the true target is estimated with the eigen-projection matrix preprocessing. All proposed methods are verified by simulation results.

articleTitle: SIW Cavity-Fed Filtenna Arrays for 5G Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, two kinds of millimeter wave (mmWave) substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity-fed filtenna arrays for 5G applications are presented. As a result, a four-order band-pass filtering response is achieved. For demonstration, filtenna array prototypes were fabricated and measured. These prototypes cover the 5G millimeter wave band (24.25 - 29.5 GHz) with measured average gains of 8.2 dBi with 22 dB out-of-band suppression. The proposed antennas are good candidates for 5G mmWave communication.

articleTitle: A Design of Multi-band Mushroom-type EBG Structure with Multi-layer Configuration
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We have proposed a compact multiband mushroom-type electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structure with multilayer configurations. The proposed EBG structure constitutes a large mushroom structure with smaller mushroom structures inside it. The proposed dual-band EBG structure has the dual bandgaps of f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>-1.5f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> and 3.2f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>-3.6f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. The size of the dual-band EBG unit cell is less than 70% of that of the conventional dual-stacked EBG unit cell.

articleTitle: LCMV Beamforming for Conformal Arrays Using Software Defined Radio
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A general Linearly Constrained Minimum Variance (LCMV) beamformer for antenna arrays on conformal surfaces using software defined radio (SDR) is presented. The demonstrator consists of an antenna array with four 2.4 GHz patches on different conformal surfaces and the USRP 2955 SDR. With the calculated LCMV weights, beams and nulls in the radiation pattern are realized for different conformal surfaces. Various scenarios are tested and good agreement between simulation and measurement is observed. The demonstrated LCMV beamforming can easily be applied to larger arrays and to arrays on other conformal surfaces.

articleTitle: 390-W 85-kHz band rapid wireless charging UAV and its inductive power transfer charging port with frustum shape
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper reports a rapid wireless charging UAV and its inductive charging port in 85-kHz band. The unique frustum structure, which is made of FRP, of the charging port enables a light-weight power receive equipment without a ferrite block in UAV, high mutual inductance between coils, prevention of misalignment of the coils. The measured receive dc power and current of batteries is 390 W and 8.46 A, respectively. The result and a successful test flight of the test UAV show a great potential of the proposed UAV and wireless charging port to realize rapid charging for large size UAVs.

articleTitle: Source Location Estimation via Compressed Sensing using UAVs
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Herein, a new source location estimation method the iterative shrinkage-thresholding algorithm (ISTA), which is a compressed sensing method, and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) is presented. By using the source location information of the primary system, secondary use of the unused vacant frequencies is possible. The proposed source location estimation method utilizes a virtual array using UAVs; however the estimation took considerable time. Therefore, we evaluate the effect of the source location estimation method using a small number of antennas by ISTA and clarify this effect.

articleTitle: Ray tracing: techniques, applications and prospect
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Ray tracing models have been used since the beginning of the nineties for both field prediction and channel simulation in mobile radio systems. Since then, ray tracing has undergone tremendous progress in terms of algorithm efficiency and application capabilities. Some of the most recent frontiers in RT progress are described in this paper. The development of fast algorithms and their real-time use inside smart wireless systems to improve performance will probably revolutionize the panorama of deterministic propagation modelling in the future.

articleTitle: Design Strategy on Medical Wearable Antenna for Tumor Detection
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Cancer is currently one of the deadliest problems in this world and every year the case always increases. There are many methods that can be used for tumor and cancer imaging. There are many requests for new approaches that are reliable, cost-effective, wearable, and convenient for the human body. The technique used is CPW and Microstrip line. For the breast, the flexible 4x4 array antenna microwave is used for human breast tumor detection. The purpose used flexible material is easy to bend and more easily adapted to media or wearable applications. The proposed frequency of antenna is working between 3.1 - 4.8 GHz in single antenna, and 5 - 9 GHz in array position.

articleTitle: Acceleration of DOA-TOA Simultaneous Estimation by Matrix Based Compressed Sensing with Zero Bin Removal
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper propose an acceleration method of Compressed Sensing by both Kronecker product and zero element removal in estimation of both DOA and TOA. Numerical results show that the calculation time is greatly reduced is by proposed method.

articleTitle: PSO-aided ILA Methodology for Hemispherical Beam Coverage and Scan Loss Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes an accurate and efficient integrated lens antenna (ILA) concept and design methodology for extraordinary beam coverage and scan loss mitigation at millimeter-wave spectrum. The geometry of the proposed ILA consists of inhomogeneous curvatures and internal center offset, where multiple parameters have high order and non-linear relations. Relying entirely on conventional full-wave simulation becomes realistically unviable. Based on geometrical optics, twodimensional ray tracing model calculates refractions on the arbitrarily-curved boundaries. The preliminary geometry of the proposed ILA is determined by a novel particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm, significantly enhancing the entire efficiency of the design procedure. With the integration of 8×16 phased array antenna, the devised ILA exceeds the conventional beam scanning limitations by 93%, achieving a main beam scanning range of 174 and scan loss of 2.2 dB for both vertical and horizontal polarizations and broad operational bandwidth. This method is estimated to alleviate the mmWave 5G antenna CAPEX (capital expenditure) by more than 50%.

articleTitle: Single-Layer Antenna with Dual-Band for 5G Millimeter-Wave System
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A dual-band antenna is proposed for the 5G millimeter-wave system. The proposed structure consists of two metallic layers and one dielectric substrate including a U-slot patch with additional slots. Dual-band characteristic is produced using slotted patch method. For proposed antenna, an impedance bandwidth (S11< -10 dB) of 5.3 GHz (18.9 %) and 3.3 GHz (8.7 %) is achieved with the average gain of 8.9 dB and 8.6 dB at 28 GHz and 38 GHz, respectively. The radiation patterns and realized gain of the proposed antenna are also presented.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Millimeter-Wave Radio Tomographic Imaging (RTI) based Indoor Localization
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In recent years, IoT and AI technologies have been developing rapidly. To utilize these technologies in home environment, it is important to capture and visualize environmental information in a house. This study developed an indoor positioning method using multi-path radio tomography imaging (RTI) based on millimeter-wave (mm-wave) radio systems such as 5G mobile and IEEE 802.11ad/ay WiGig which currently attract a great deal of attention. The extensive performance evaluation via computer simulation should be needed for the system design and optimal installation because the localization performance largely depends on various system conditions. This paper clarified the relationship between the performance and the setup conditions such as the size of the target environment and the placement of anchor nodes which are most important system parameters.

articleTitle: EMI Reduction Techniques from 100 kW Wireless Charging Systems for Heavy-Duty Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) is a useful technology for vehicle charging. Transfer power above 100 kW is needed for rapid charging of heavy-duty vehicles such as electric buses. One of the issues of WPT systems is electromagnetic interference that affects radio services. Limits of radiated disturbances from WPT systems are specified in CISPR 11 and the Radio Act of Japan. In this study, a 100-kW-class WPT system was constructed with the aim of reducing the radiated magnetic field strength. Opposite-phase transfer and frequency hopping spread spectrum were implemented to reduce the fundamental frequency. Low-pass filters were applied to decrease the harmonic frequency. A 10-m anechoic chamber was used to measure the radiated magnetic field strength of this WPT system. The results confirmed the compatibility of the three proposed techniques. The radiated magnetic field strength of the constructed WPT system was below the limit set by the Radio Act of Japan.

articleTitle: Focal Region Ray Tracing of Dual Spherical Reflector Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: 5G mobile communications require multibeam base station antenna to operate at millimeter frequency band. Therefore, dual spherical antenna is promising for 5G application. As for achieving high gain, optimum antenna configuration should be found out. In this paper, the focal region ray tracing method is developed. Firstly, analytical equations for the focal region ray tracing are clarified. The key equation of determining the caustic position is then solved by MATLAB program. In addition, some ray tracing results are shown to ensure the usefulness of the developed ray tracing method.

articleTitle: A Patch Antenna Array With a Rotatable Polarization Plane for Ku-Band Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A Ku-band linear array that can change the main- beam direction and the polarization plane electronically is presented. The radiating elements are dual circularly polarized (CP) patch antennas, and the main-beam direction and the polarization angle of the resultant linearly polarized (LP) wave are controlled by changing only the excitation phases. Experimental results of the beam steering and polarization plane control are presented.

articleTitle: Experimental Reflection Characteristics of 253 GHz in a Small Closed-room
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the experimental reflection characteristics based on measurements in a small closed-room at 253 GHz. The reflection coefficients of interior construction materials such as concrete, wood, and metal are firstly investigated. As a result of measuring the power distribution of multipath signals reflected in a small closed-room and comparing them with the ray-tracing simulation results, we observed that multipath signals reflected more than once were distributed in various angles.

articleTitle: 2-Element Slot Antenna Array Based on Substrate Integrated Waveguide at Q-band
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A 2-element slot antenna array based on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) for MIMO communication systems is proposed in this paper. The antenna array contains two separated SIW slot antennas. To obtain high isolation which means low correlation and is important for MIMO systems, the two separated slot antennas are arranged in orthogonal polarization directions. For each SIW slot antenna, there exist two radiating slots whose distance is 1.5λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub> (λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub> represent the waveguide wavelength in the SIW transmission line). Proposed 2-element antenna array is fabricated and measured to verify the validity at Q-band, which shows good agreement between testing results and simulations.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Enhancement of Microstrip Patch Antenna Using Slits for 5G Mobile Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The design and simulation of a microstrip patch antenna for 5G mobile networks is presented in this paper. The antenna operates at the Local Multipoint Distribution Service band having a center frequency at 28 GHz. The antenna was designed on a Rogers RT Duroid 5880 of height 0.5mm and a dielectric constant of 2.2. Slits were introduced unto the patch to enhance the bandwidth, gain of the antenna. Simulation results obtained showed a return loss of –23.6 dB, with a wide bandwidth of 1.23 GHz and a gain of 6.35 dB which makes it suitable for deployment in 5G applications.

articleTitle: Low-cost fixed-site ground station system for receiving NOAA-19 satellite
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a design and builds of a low-cost fixed-site ground station to receive NOAA-19 APT weather satellite at 137.1 MHz. In a power link budget calculation, signals from NOAA satellites to the receiver of the ground station can be obtained with a margin of 26 dB at an elevation angle of 20 degrees. As a result of testing, the proposed ground station can receive the NOAA-19 to APT satellite images and displayed in real-time throughout the airspace of the station.

articleTitle: An Improved Method in Graph Coloring Algorithm for Interference Coordination in Cluster-wise Ultra-dense RAN
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In our previous study, we proposed a Restricted Color Number (RCN) algorithm based on graph coloring for interference coordination in cluster-wise distributed MU-MIMO in ultra-dense RAN. In this algorithm, we applied Delaunay Triangulation to help decide the interference relationship, which is different from the common-used threshold setting method. In this paper, we will discuss about the advantages of the Delaunay Triangulation method over the threshold method in graph coloring algorithm for interference coordination.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Circularly Polarized Microstrip Antenna for BDS Application
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A dual-band circularly polarized (CP) microstrip antenna for BeiDou Navigation Satellite System (BDS) is presented. A circular patch with notches and a ring slot with notches are used for upper and lower band radiators respectively. Meanwhile, the circular patch acts as a coupling patch to feed the ring slot radiator. A quarter wavelength transformer and branch impedance adapter are introduced for impedance matching. The measured and simulated results show good CP radiation at 1618 MHz and 2452 MHz. The gains of the proposed antenna are 7.91 dBi and 5.24 dBi at the upper band and the lower band respectively.

articleTitle: Broadband SIW Slot Antenna for Millimeter Wave Application
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband SIW slot antenna for millimeter frequency band is designed. The method of etching irregular rectangular grooves on the top of the integrated waveguide of the substrate and loading short-circuit pins realizes the broadband of the antenna and improves the gain of the antenna. Grounded coplanar waveguide(GCPW) feeding to obtain better matching; the working frequency band of the antenna is 20-26.8GHz, the relative bandwidth is 28.3%, and the antenna gain is 10.1dB. For the traditional slot antenna, the slot antenna based on the substrate integrated waveguide(SIW) designed in this paper has a wider impedance bandwidth and can be used in millimeter wave communications.

articleTitle: A Beam Forming Antenna Based on Earth Shape for Micro-satellites
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a new wide-beam bifilar helix antenna with earth coverage beam for satellite communication. Former helix antennas for micro-satellites are focused on narrow-beam high-gain purpose and hard to realize the desired beam pattern within a wide angle range, making them unsuitable for earth coverage applications. This novel antenna realizes the uniform illumination of the earth's surface with miniaturized structure. (The earth coverage radiation pattern is obtained within the beamwidth of θ in the range of ±56°). According to the calculation, the antenna is modeled and simulated. The simulation results show good agreement.

articleTitle: Helical antennas in 920-MHz band for wireless sensor nodes under the ground
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this study, the radiation characteristics of the 920-MHz band helical antennas in free space and in the ground were analyzed and compared. Some lobes and nulls appeared in the underground case and the radiation toward the air from the underground was weakened as a whole compared to the case in free space. Based on the result, a wall was added to the ground conductor plate of the antenna, and the space between the helix and the ground was filled with a dielectric material. As a result, the radiated waves were almost uniformly toward the air, and the radiation was strengthened. This antenna is useful when connecting sensors underground that measures environmental data to a wireless network. By installing the antenna in the ground together with sensor nodes, measurement is possible without interfering with farm work.

articleTitle: A Quad-Polarization Agile Microstrip Antenna with Diode Loaded Cross Slot and Microstrip Line
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper describes a novel microstrip patch antenna with switchable four polarizations. The proposed antenna consists of a patch antenna embedded with four PIN diodes in cross-slot shape and four microstrip lines (MSL) are connected at the four corners of the patch. By switching the state of the PIN diodes, the sense of rotation of the electric fields in circular polarization (CP) can be reconfigured. Moreover, with the aid of the half-wavelength shorted MSL and four extra diodes, the proposed antenna can switch linear polarization (LP). The concept is validated by the simulation and found to be feasible. The simulated 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth is around 1% for both RHCP and LHCP.

articleTitle: Accuracy Improvement of Human Motion Recognition with MW-FMCW Radar Using CNN
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Human Motion Recognition (HMR) using radar has been expected to be applied to human monitoring. Radar-based HMR can be realized by extracting features by deep learning from radar motion-sensing data. In this paper, three 2-D domains (Time-Doppler, Time-Range, and Range-Doppler) are analyzed as the motion data. The motion classification results using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) shows that multiple domains improve classification accuracy. In addition, we show the motion analysis results with high range resolution including DOA, and show that further accuracy improvement can be expected.

articleTitle: Polarimetric Signature CNN based Complex Permittivity Estimation for Microwave Non-destructive Testing
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Here, we present complex relative permittivity estimation algorithm using fully polarimetric data based convolutional neural network (CNN) approach for microwave nondestructive testing scenario. The three-dimensional FDTD simulation show that our method accurately retains both dielectric constant and conductivity of floor slab buried in concrete media.

articleTitle: Direction and Location Estimation Algorithm with Power Gravity Point for Spectrum Sharing
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A direction and location estimation algorithm is proposed in this paper. In spectrum sharing, it is required to estimate the location of existing systems to avoid interference with them. The power gravity point algorithm estimates transmitter locations with simple data such as location and received power of sensors and equations and therefore, it is considered suitable for spectrum sharing to various wireless systems. On the other hand, since the algorithm assumes an isotropic radiation pattern of antenna for the transmitter, it cannot be applied to a transmitter with directivity. To solve this problem, in this paper, sectorial sub-regions centered on the power gravity point are defined. Calculating the power gravity point of all 360degree sub-regions, the angular locus of the power gravity point is obtained. Using the symmetry of the locus, the direction of the transmitter from the initial power gravity point is estimated. Selecting the sub-region of the direction, the transmitter location is estimated as the power gravity point of the sub-region. Simulation results show that the estimation error of the proposed algorithm is smaller than that of conventional power gravity point algorithms.

articleTitle: Doubly Curved Reflector Antenna Design Trade-Offs for a Hexagonal Lattice of Beams
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a doubly curved reflector antenna fed by a stack of linear arrays is discussed. The design procedure to generate a hexagonal lattice of beams leads to higher spillover losses, resulting in lower aperture efficiency. The impact of oversizing the reflector to reduce spill-over losses is investigated with numerical results reported in Ka-band.

articleTitle: New Low-Cost FDM Technology for Printing Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper a new FDM (fused deposition molding) printing process for the production of electrically conductive structures, e.g. antennas, is presented. In comparison to known processes, this is only done with a simple 3D printer with additional dosing unit for the conductive printing material. The printing process of the thermoplastic carrier material and the conductive adhesive paste takes place almost simultaneously and requires no further thermal treatment. First printing tests of antennas were very successful.

articleTitle: Two-dimensional Autofocus Approach for bistatic SAR Polar Format Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The existing two-dimension (2-D) autofocus algorithms for bistatic system aperture radar (SAR) do not make full use of the structure of phase error knowledge and estimate phase error in a blind manner. They often suffer from low computational efficiency and imprecise parameter. In this paper, an efficient 2-D autofocus algorithm for bistatic SAR is presented. First, the new bistatic PFA (polar format algorithm) interpretation is used to derive the structure of phase error. Then, based on this knowledge, a 2-D autofocus approach is proposed. This algorithm only requires an estimate of azimuth (1-D) phase error, and then the 2-D phase error can be computed from the 1-D phase error. Compared with other existing autofocus approaches, the experimental results demonstrate that both the accuracy of the parameter estimation and the computational efficiency in this algorithm is obviously improved.

articleTitle: Physical-Layer Cell ID Detection Probability Using NR Synchronization Signals for 3GPP TDL Channel Models
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents physical-layer cell identity (PCID) detection probability using synchronization signals for the 5G New Radio (NR) initial access in 3rd generation partnership project (3GPP) tapped delay line (TDL) channel models. Computer simulation results validate the PCID detection probability based on the cumulative distribution of the instantaneous received power level of the synchronization signal for the respective channel models. We also show that the high PCID detection probability is achieved by using the NR synchronization signals in the 3GPP TDL channel models.

articleTitle: An Electrically Small Top-Loaded Mono-Cone Antenna with Ring Slot
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An electrically small top-loaded mono-cone antenna with a ring slot is proposed. By employing the monocone with top-hat, slot, shorting pins, and cylinder elements, the miniaturization is achieved. By connecting the shorting pins from the mono-cone top-hat to the ground plane, the antenna bandwidth at the low frequency limit is expanded. The slot inside the top-hat improves the impedance matching in the high-frequency band. Furthermore, by employing the cylinder elements, the impedance matching at the mid and high frequency bands is improved. The -10 dB reflection coefficient bandwidth of the proposed antenna is ranging from 0.52 GHz to 1.74 GHz.

articleTitle: Base Station Antenna Systems for mm-Waves
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Lower efficiencies of power amplifiers and increased path loss at higher frequencies are two reasons why utilizing millimeter-wave frequencies for future wireless communications systems is challenging. In this paper, two distinct antenna systems are presented which address this challenge by using high antenna gain. This allows lower transmit power levels, compared to conventional phased array antennas, while still providing high effective isotropic radiated power.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Wave Source Localization Method Using UAVs Based on the Maximum Likelihood Estimation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: For temporal and spatial spectrum sharing between primary and secondary wireless communication systems, wave source localization is a promising technique to localize areas that wireless signals are radiated. In order to localize wave sources under NLOS (Non-Line-of-Sight) environments, we have proposed a wave source localization method using UAVs (Unmanned Aerial Vehicles) based on maximum likelihood estimation and evaluate the performance of the proposed method under a situation that DoAs (Direction of Arrivals) of received signals at each UAV follow a von-Mises distribution. In this paper, we evaluate the performance of the proposed method with a more practical simulation environment using a ray-tracing radio propagation simulator.

articleTitle: HAPS to Ground Propagation Model Considering General Terrestrial Path
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: ITU-R ground-to-ground propagation model adaptable to any terrain was extended to predict basic transmission loss of high altitude platform station (HAPS)-to-ground path by considering the reduction of ray bending due to stratosphere. Using the proposed method, an example coverage map of a mobile base station on HAPS was produced highlighting the effects of terrain as well as spherical earth diffraction and troposcattering.

articleTitle: A Low Side-Lobe Slotted Ridge Waveguide Array Manufactured by Resin Injection Molding
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a low side-lobe slotted ridge waveguide array manufactured by resin injection molding. The resin waveguide is divided into two parts, and both are fastened using screws and bosses. The waveguides need to be arranged closely in order to apply them to a dual-polarized phased array antenna. This requires the bosses to be pushed into the waveguide, which causes reflection waves and phase delay in the waveguide and then deteriorates radiation pattern. In this paper, we propose an iris on a ridge in the waveguide to cancel the effects of the bosses. We design an array of 16 subarrays with the proposed structure. The simulated side lobe is -32.7 dB, which validates the effectiveness of the proposed structure.

articleTitle: Optical-Fiber Link Multi-Probe Near-Field Antenna Measurement System using Zero-Biased EA modulator and CWDM Multiplexer
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We have developed multi-probe near-field antenna measurement system using optical-fiber link system. Our developed optical fiber link system consists of a super luminescent diode, zero-biased optical reflection-type electro absorptive modulators (EAM), coarse wavelength division multiplexing (CWDM) multiplexers and photodiodes. Our developed near-field antenna measurement system consists of WR-28 open ended waveguide probes (OEWG), an optical fiber link system and 6-axis 1 m length arm vertical articulated robot. Our system can be applied to multi OEWG probes with EAM. In this paper, we show frequency characteristics of our system and a measured near field frequency responses for a WR-28 standard gain horn antenna using OEWGs up to 30 GHz.

Author Keywords: zero biased optical reflection type electro absorptive modulator

articleTitle: A Wideband Dual-Linearly-Polarized Millimeter Wave Antenna for 5G Terminal Application
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a low-profile and wideband dual-polarized millimeter wave antenna is proposed for 5G applications. The radiator is comprised by a pair of vertically-stacked elliptical patches for broadening the bandwidth, along with eight and four rectangular slots cut on top and bottom patches for size miniaturization. In order to enable dual-polarized operation, two feeding striplines are orthogonally placed for exciting the stacked patches through two H-shaped apertures cut out on the ground plane. The proposed antenna achieves a footprint of 4.5 mm × 4.5 mm, and a total thickness of 1.57 mm. Six shorting pins are introduced in between two feeding apertures for improving the port isolation. The proposed antenna is fabricated and characterized, achieving a measured bandwidth of 21.8% and a low mutual coupling smaller than -41 dB. The superior performance of the proposed antenna can be a promising element candidate for arrays in 5G terminals and base stations.

articleTitle: Generalized Ray-tracing Model for Modified Geodesic Luneburg Lens Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we present an accurate and efficient ray-tracing model for calculating the radiation pattern of rotationally symmetric geodesic lenses. The performance of the ray-tracing model is compared to full-wave simulations, CST and HFSS, through the radiation patterns of a modified geodesic Luneburg lens antenna. The modified geodesic Luneburg lens profile has two parts, one is the original geodesic curve using geometrical optics, and one is a transition for reducing reflections. The radiation pattern from the ray-tracing model has a good agreement with the results from the full-wave simulations. However, the ray-tracing is significantly faster than the full-wave simulators.

articleTitle: Indoor Localization with Machine Learning Based on Interpolated Received Signals of Phased Array
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents indoor localization with machine learning, which estimates the position of a target three-dimensionally based on the interpolated received signals of a phased array. In a fundamental study, retro-directive signals of a small 2-by-2 phased array received from the target are input to a 3-layered neural network (NN) to estimate the location of the target. To reduce the time and cost for the training of this system, especially in the 3D case, the signals from a tag on a coarse grid are interpolated to prepare training data. The higher accuracy of localization with interpolated signals is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Design of a K-band Wideband Circularly Polarized Micro-strip Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The electromagnetic environment faced by modern aircraft is becoming more and more complex, and the sensors on the aircraft are subject to more and more interference and threat. The data link formed by the sensor network among several aircraft can effectively improve the data transmission performance and anti-interference ability. Inter-aircraft data link emphasizes high communication rate, large coverage angle domain, small attitude constraint, low interception rate, high anti-interference and high airborne environmental adaptability. Therefore, it is required that inter-machine data link antenna should have the characteristics of high frequency, large bandwidth, high gain of circular polarization, narrow beam, low side lobe, wave velocity scanning, low profile, light weight, etc. In this paper, a double layer micro-strip antenna coupling fed by strip line U /H slot is presented, which has the above advantages. At the same time, a 5x4 array antenna is designed. The test results show that the standing wave bandwidth less than 1.5 is 24% and the overall height is 14mm, which is very suitable for inter-machine networking data link antenna sensor equipment.

articleTitle: Design and measurement of a linearly dual-polarized dual-band and wideband multi-ring microstrip antenna fed by two L-probes
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents design and measurement of a linearly dual-polarized dual-band and wideband multi-ring microstrip antenna fed by two L-probes. The proposed antenna consists of two circular ring patches and two L-probes arranged in a multi-layered dielectric substrate. By using a thick substrate for the L-probe and arranging two ring patches as radiation elements, the proposed antenna operates wideband and dual-band characteristics. Furthermore, by arranging two L-probes at the orthogonal positions, the proposed antenna can radiate dual linear polarizations. The measured fractional bandwidths corresponding to a reflection coefficient below -10 dB were 21.7% and 10.6% for the first and second modes, respectively. The measured isolation between two ports of the test antennas in the above bandwidths were less than -13 dB.

articleTitle: Angle-of-Arrival-based Outdoor Localization for Spectrum Sharing at 25 GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper evaluated two angle-of-arrival (AoA)-based localization methods, pseudo-linear estimator (PLE) and maximum-likelihood estimator (MLE), at 25 GHz band in an outdoor environment. The transmitter (Tx) was the commercial small power data communication system. The receiver (Rx) was the fan-beam array antenna mounted on the stepping motor. The experiment was conducted in the Tokyo Institute of Technology where the location estimation was done by searching the Rx angle which maximizes the received power. The results showed that both methods had good accuracy if only the line-of-sight (LOS) points were used, and became worsen for non-LOS (NLOS) points, especially for PLE.

articleTitle: Dual Band and Dual Polarized Reflectarray Using Cross Dipole and Patch Elements
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In the fifth generation wireless communication systems, it is expected to use high frequencies such as 39 GHz in addition to 28 GHz. However, radio wave in high frequency bands has a high straight advancing property. As a result, coverage holes exist where communication quality is insufficient in communication area. To overcome this problem, a reflectarray has been reported to reflect the radio waves in a specified direction. In this paper, a dual band and dual polarized reflectarray is proposed. The proposed reflectarray can achieve the 45° reflection at normal incidence for both polarization at 28 GHz and 39 GHz.

articleTitle: 2D Sparse Array Selection via Deep Leaning
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a simulated annealing (SA) assisted deep learning (DL) based 2D sparse array selection approach. A SA-based optimisation method is used to assist in generation and annotation of dataset. The antenna selection problem is formulated as a multi-classification problem, and a convolutional neural network (CNN) is used to solve it. The SA-based dataset generation method enables optimal sensor distribution and reduces computation complexity related with dataset generation. Numerical examples verify the effectiveness of the proposed method in terms of configuration of the realised sparse arrays and DOA estimation performance.

articleTitle: Closely-spaced Four-element MIMO Antenna for 5G Mobile Terminals
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a MIMO antenna operating at 4900MHz band for 5G mobile terminals. The proposed antenna consists of four closely-spaced elements with total size of 35.4×5.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The open ends of two adjacent elements face to each other and the edge-to-edge distance is only 0.8 mm. A lumped inductor is connected between the two open ends to decouple the antenna. The mutual coupling of the adjacent elements can be mitigated by optimizing the inductor. The simulated overlapping -6 dB bandwidth of the four elements is 285 MHz (4760-5045 MHz), with port isolation higher than 11.3 dB.

articleTitle: Circular lattice design for UHF geodesic dome phased array antenna with reduced footprint
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A circular planar array composed of four equilateral triangle patch antennas with a common triangular ground plane is proposed. The array is a building block for a geodesic dome phased array antenna (GDPAA) based on an icosahedron structure, primarily intended for use in the UHF amateur satellite band of 435-438 MHz. Due to the relatively long wavelength of this band, a novel design for a low-cost GDPAA with a reduced footprint is proposed. It is found that if individual elements are placed in a circular lattice, the footprint is reduced and the overall array performance and antenna isolation are improved.

articleTitle: Study on simple performance evaluation for MU-MIMO-OFDMA
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: MU-MIMO-OFDMA, which is a combination of Multi-User Multiple Input Multiple Output (MU-MIMO) and Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiple Access (OFDMA), can achieve high-speed and stable transmission by allocating resources in both the spatial and frequency domains.
