In this paper, we propose a method to easily realize MU-MIMO-OFDMA transmission by setting a threshold value for spatial correlation.

articleTitle: Holographic Antenna with Low Surface Impedance Sensitivity Unit Cell
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a holographic antenna using a single/double inter-digital shape unit cells that have a wide surface impedance range and reduce the surface impedance sensitivity on a high relative permittivity and a thin substrate. The proposed holographic antenna operates in 24 GHz, and the maximum gain of the holographic antenna with the proposed method is gain 8 dBi at 33°. Moreover, the proposed antenna satisfied the low surface impedance sensitivity.

articleTitle: THz links for future mobile systems
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A number of base stations are required to offer global mobile services by use of small cells for high-speed wireless links. The small cells should be connected by networks with various media including optical fibers and fixed wireless links. Required bandwidth for such links would be up to 100 Gb/s. In conventional radio systems, it would be rather difficult to achieve such high-speed transmission. In this paper, we focus on THz links which can offer networks for future mobile networks.

articleTitle: Analysis of Strain Sensor using Millimeter Wave Chipless RFID Tag
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a strain sensor using millimeter wave chipless RFID tag. The chipless RFID is composed of several tags and a reader. The reader reads the data from the resonant frequency of the tag's backscattered wave. The resonance frequency of presented strain sensor tag is depended on tag shape changing by strain. The shape of strain sensor tag is optimized by the finite-difference time-domain method and micro genetic algorithm in order to maximize variations of resonance frequencies. The optimization results show that the desired resonant frequencies and large variations are obtained.

articleTitle: Circular polarization characteristics of dipole antenna using flat elements
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Circular polarization (CP) is a polarization state in which the electric field vector rotates in a plane perpendicular to the wave's direction. This paper proposes a dipole antenna using flat plates for CP. It is necessary to combine the antenna's plurality to generate circularly polarized waves using a dipole antenna structure. The proposed antenna can still generate circularly polarized waves with one pair of a flat plate dipole antenna. The EM simulator completes the parametric study. It was found that LHCP (Left-Hand Circular Polarization) was radiated in both directions of the X-axis, and RHCP (Right-Hand Circular Polarization) was radiated in both directions of the Y-axis. A band with an axial ratio of 3 dB or less was obtained in the range of 6.35 to 9.35 GHz.

articleTitle: Perpendicularly Configured Array Elements for a Shared-aperture S/X Dual-band Radar
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This article proposes the perpendicularly configured array elements in a shared-aperture S/X dual-band radar. The proposed antenna array contains one S-band element and nine X-band elements. The currents in the S and X-band elements have orthogonal directional characteristics, which effectively reduces the mutual coupling effects. In addition, an extended cavity structure is also applied to block the surface current and further reduce the mutual coupling effects. To validate the proposed design, the reflection coefficient and bore-sight gain characteristics are investigated. The results demonstrate that the proposed array has proper characteristics for the shared-aperture S/X band radar systems.

articleTitle: Dynamic Ray Tracing: A 3D Formulation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Ray tracing algorithms can simulate multipath radio propagation in presence of geometric obstacles that can represent buildings, objects or vehicles. When objects or vehicles are moving, which is the case of vehicular environments, it is possible to predict the multipath - and therefore the field - in the near future on the base of the current multipath geometry, assuming constant speeds or accelerations for moving objects, using an analytical extrapolation. A full-3D Dynamic Ray Tracing algorithm is here presented for multiple reflections on moving surfaces.

articleTitle: Basic consideration on non-contact localization for a PIM source in array antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Non-contact PIM measurement has been proposed as a PIM evaluation method for an antenna. By using this method, it is expected that a simple method for locating the PIM source in the array antenna will be realized. This paper presents the calculation results of the observed PIM level in non-contact PIM measurement using a model of a linear array antenna. Then, the localization of the PIM source by non-contact PIM measurement was evaluated.

articleTitle: A study on outdoor to indoor penetration loss characteristics considering vertical and horizontal incident angle at 5 GHz band
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recently, the next generation (5-th generation: 5G) mobile communication systems have been actively investigated all over the world. Various systems exist when considering the microwave bands after the introduction of 5G systems. Hence, the propagation characteristics when considering the interference among the systems is very important. In this paper, we compare the characteristics of loss when radio waves propagate from outdoor to indoor (O2I) through a window at 5 GHz band where many IoT devices are expected to be used. In this report, we show O2I penetration loss characteristics at 5 GHz for different incident angles considering not only vertical but horizontal plane.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Improvement Methods for Monopole Element Printed Quasi-Yagi Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A modified monopole element printed quasi-Yagi antenna (PQYA) for bandwidth (BW) improvement is investigated in this paper. With the rectangular driven monopole element, offset feed, and optimizing other design parameters, an operating frequency range from 1.31 to 2.76 GHz is achieved. The evolution steps of the modified monopole element PQYA are presented, and it is shown that an impedance BW can be improved from 41.68% to 71.88%. To verify the simulations, the prototype of the antenna is fabricated and tested. The experimental results are in good agreement with simulated results.

articleTitle: Blind Signal Separation Using Array Antenna with Modified Optimal-Stepsize CMA
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The OS-CMA used for blind signal separation with array antenna has a problem that the stationary characteristics are not stable, although the convergence is extremely fast. This paper introduces a threshold into the stepsize of OS-CMA to realize the more stable stationary characteristics while maintaining the convergence speed. The computer simulation demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Blind-based demodulation scheme for virtual massive MIMO systems
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In beyond-fifth-generation (B5G) networks, massive multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) systems using a large number of base station antennas have attracted significant attention. As the number of antennas increases, the hardware scale of massive MIMO systems is complicated. In recent years, a virtual massive (VM)-MIMO system which performs MIMO transmission by using virtual antenna arrays creating a single antenna element has been investigated. In this paper, we propose a blind-based demodulation scheme for a VM-MIMO system to cancel the interference with oversampling. In our proposed scheme, as a signal whose level is less than a certain power threshold cannot be used in the high-order modulation scheme with oversampling, we apply filtering wherein signals with the noise power level are removed. Through this procedure, multi-level modulation signals can be utilized in VM-MIMO. Moreover, our simulation evaluations show that the bit error rate improves considerably by using our proposed scheme on the uplink commutation environment including up to ten users.

articleTitle: Retrodirective Array Antenna System for the Microwave Power Transmission
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The long and middle range MPT (microwave power transmission) is very important, which basically uses RF beamforming technology to efficiently provide the power at distance and requires the large dimension of array system to the far end power receiver. In this paper, we design an antenna and phase conjugate circuit for the retrodirective array antenna system. The beam directivity is improved by 0.2dBi, 0.45dBi and 0.3dBi at 0, 120 and 180 degree. Simulation results show that the phase conjugation is well performed. So, the proposed system can be useful for the middle range MPT system. Also, we have studied and discussed the system power efficiency for wireless power transmission and antenna array dimension. A design example shows the primary design of 5% power efficiency for microwave power transmission at the distance of 4 m. when the center frequency is 2.45GHz.

articleTitle: Mixture Database Method in Area Estimation by Finger Printing
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This contribution describe "area estimation" using Finger printing for indoor localization. A method for updating DBs with user-acquired AP information is necessary for the system. There is a problem of lowering the estimation accuracy due to the bias of the updated DBs. To solve this problem, we proposed a method to create a large distribution by mixing multiple databases.

articleTitle: Wideband Isolation Enhancement of Dual-Antenna Array Using Hybrid Decoupling Structures
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A wideband hybrid decoupling structure for MIMO antennas is presented in this paper. The decoupling structure is composed of a suspended array-antenna decoupling surface, which consists of several reflectors and a defected ground structure with two rectangular slots to reduce the mutual coupling. When utilizing the proposed design in the two extremely-closed patch antennas with an edge-to-edge distance of only 1 mm (0.019 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> at 5.65 GHz), the simulated results demonstrate that the isolation better than 20 dB can be achieved over the frequency range of 5.13-6.27 GHz (20%). Besides, the isolation level reaches more than 30 dB over 5.41-6.25 GHz (14.4%). Meanwhile, the efficiency and gain of the antenna are also improved by considerable amounts.

articleTitle: Design of Low Profile Broadband Dual-polarized Microstrip Patch Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Novel vehicle technology has become a hot research topic in the aerospace field in recent years. In order to improve the aerodynamic shape and stealth performance, a conformal antenna must be used. This puts strict requirements on the longitudinal height, volume and weight of the antenna. At the same time, the relevant electronic equipment on the aircraft platform also puts forward higher demands on the antenna for broadband, dual polarization, high gain, and low side lobes. Therefore, the low-profile, miniaturized broadband dual-polarization conformal antenna has become a research hotspot in recent years. This paper presents a form of double-layer patch micro-strip antenna with strip-line fed H-shaped slot coupled feed, which has broadband dual-polarization characteristics. At the same time, an 8x8 array antenna was designed. The test results show that the bandwidth of the standing wave less than 1.5 is 25%, and the overall height is 1.3mm, which is Very suitable for electronic equipment of novel aircraft platform.

articleTitle: A Study on Σ-Δ Directional Antenna Array for Electromagnetic Wave Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A Σ-Δ directional antenna array for electromagnetic wave energy harvesting is proposed in this paper. By applying the Σ-Δ directional antenna array with the 180-degree hybrid circuit, it is possible to convert more electric power from the electromagnetic wave. The results of the consideration by the indoor environment using the ray tracing method are reported that the received electric power by the Σ-Δ directional antenna array is improved more than the single directivity antenna.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Vertically Polarized Endfire Phased Array Antenna for 5G mm-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a low-profile vertically polarized endfire phased array antenna for millimeter-wave mobile device applications. The proposed array antenna is designed based on a conventional folded slot antenna structure by adding C-shaped via configurations and a coupled double-sided parallel stripline (DSPSL). A cost-effective PCB process is utilized to fabricate the proposed array. The proposed array has a reflection coefficient less than -10 dB over 27.9 GHz-28.78 GHz, the maximum gain is 13.3 dBi and the half-power beamwidth in the E-plane (xz-plane) is 56°. In addition, the proposed antenna has maximum beam steering angles of ±30° in the H-plane (xy-plane).

articleTitle: Inter-Mode Interference Caused by Antenna Swinging in OAM Mode Multiplexing
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this study, we estimated the performance of an orbital angular momentum (OAM) mode multiplexing transmission using a uniform circular array when the antenna swung. To compensate for the inter-mode interference caused by antenna swinging, OAM mode de-multiplexing was adaptively controlled by a least mean squares algorithm. Experimental results showed that stable transmission was achieved by the optimum loop bandwidth of the feedback loop in the E-band.

articleTitle: Compact Triple-band Monopole Antenna with Dual Fork-shaped Strips for WLAN/WiMAX Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A miniature single-layer CPW-fed monopole antenna with triple-band operation for wireless local area network (WLAN) and worldwide interoperability for microwave access (WiMAX) application is presented. By inserting a small fork-shaped strip into a bigger modified fork-shaped patch element, the antenna with overall dimensions of only 25×20×0.8 mm3, is capable of generating three distinct operating bands, 2.27 - 2.61, 3.37 - 3.89, and 4.88 - 6.69 GHz covering all the 2.4/5.5/5.8 GHz WLAN bands and the 3.5/5.5 GHz WiMAX bands. Moreover, the antenna shows good monopole-like radiation patterns and stable antenna gains across the three operating bands.

articleTitle: An analysis of increasing the gain of the patch antenna using slots on the ground plane
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A patch antenna is one of the most common directional radiation antennas in mobile communications [1] and [2]. It can be varied in accordance with the combination of reflectors or directors to increase antenna gain and can also be used for making a high gain array antenna. In this paper, we proposed that slots are embedded into a ground plane (GND) to increase the gain of the patch antenna at 3 GHz. Some characteristics including VSWR and far-field radiation pattern are simulated by use of CST MWSTUDIO. Details of the antenna configuration and simulated result are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Absorption evaluation of electromagnetic wave absorbers in practical environments
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In recent years, UHF- radio-frequency identification (RFID) systems are paid to attention as one of technologies which achieve the unattended shop or production field. However, the reliability of indoor telecommunication is adversely affected by multiple reflection interference. In order to actualize those unattended systems, the microwave absorber that suppresses the electromagnetic interference is essential. However, because existing microwave absorbers are not transparent, it blocks the monitoring camera's field of view. Therefore, we developed a transparent microwave absorber, and the evaluation results of the absorption performance are described in this report.

articleTitle: Investigation of noise current on the wire harness in the EV deriving from WPT
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In recent years, wireless power transmission (WPT) to an electric vehicle (EV) has attracted increasing attention. More than several kW is assumed for WPT, so that electromagnetic interference (EMI) is required to be considered. The WPT can also affect the control system and the automotive networks of the EV. Therefore, the noise current induced on the wire harness due to WPT cannot be ignored. The purpose of this paper is to investigate the noise current on the wire harness. As a result of the investigation, we confirmed up to several hundred μA on the wire harness.

articleTitle: Modulation Scheme Estimation of Multiple Signals Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a plural modulation scheme estimation method for using machine learning. The estimation accuracy of the method is numerically verified. As the results, it is shown that the combination of modulation scheme in mixed signals can be estimated by proposed method.

articleTitle: Development of Indoor Device-Free Location Estimation Using Commodity WiFi Device
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In recent years, since the propagation channel characteristics have been effectively used for applications such as motion sensing, position detection, etc. A great deal of attention is attracted to channel sounding methods easy to utilize using low-cost devices. This paper presents a device-free indoor location estimation method using spatio-temporal features of radio propagation channels using the 2.4-GHz band 3-by-3 MIMO channel sounder developed using commodity wireless LANs. The measurement results demonstrated a reasonable performance of the proposed method with small number of antennas.

articleTitle: A Suspended Line to Waveguide Transition for Dual-polarized Slotted Waveguide Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a suspended line to waveguide transition for slotted waveguide array antenna. In the proposed transition, slotted waveguides are fed by waveguide T-junctions. The input port of the T-junction is connected to the suspended lines, which run parallel to the axis of the slotted waveguides, with a slot. The simulated bandwidth with a reflection coefficient less than -20dB is 3.3% for the transition for vertical polarization and 2.3% for the transition for horizontal polarization.

articleTitle: An Extended Co-prime Array with Multiple Discontinuous Period Subarrays
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a new extended co-prime array with multiple discontinuous period subarrays (ECAMdpS) is proposed. Different from the co-prime array with multi-period subarrays (CAMpS), the number of periods for each subarray of ECAMdpS is discontinuous. By selecting the value of period and the number of periods for each subarray properly, the degrees of freedom (DOFs) of ECAMdpS can outperform than CAMpS. The direction of arrival (DOA) estimation performance of ECAMdpS is demonstrated by the simulation results.

articleTitle: Approximate analysis of EM wave scattering from two cracks on a ground plane
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We derive a simple formula of scattering field from two different cracks on conducting ground plane, based on the formulation of the Kobayashi potential method. By using the formula, one can easily and in detail examine the scattering features of empty and material filled case with/without the multiple scattering contributions.

articleTitle: Basic Study on Polarimetric Observation of Ocean Radar
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: As the use of coastal areas expands, the demand for ocean radar is increasing. The radar’s potential is not limited to wave observations, but to acquire other oceanographic information. We deployed an ocean radar on the roof of the Faculty of Engineering, Niigata University. This radar system has a dual-polarization feature to help the multi-purpose use of ocean radars. In this report, we show some initial experiment results of dual-polarization observation including calibration.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional Estimation of Angle of Arrival using Newton–Raphson Method
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes estimation of the three-dimensional angle of arrival for multiple incoming waves using the Newton-Raphson method. The source locations can be estimated when the error function (the difference between the received and estimated array antenna power) is minimized. The results obtained reveal the angles estimated via the proposed method to contain small errors. Thus, those values do not fall into the local minimum solution.

articleTitle: Environment Mapping Technique using Millimeter-Wave Radio Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Aiming at realizing sensing of the surrounding environment for smart homes/smart building applications, device-free localization techniques using radio propagation characteristics have gained interest. To realize such techniques it is often required that the accurate environmental information should be obtained in advance. In this study, the environment mapping method using millimeter-wave (mm-wave) ratio such as WiGig and 5G mobile communication systems was developed. Specifically, this study proposed a multi-dimensional Kirchoff Migration (KM) method using mm-wave systems which improves the performance by utilizing the high-resolution in delay time and angular channel responses.

articleTitle: Ultra Wide Band Antenna for Breast Tumor Detection
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An ultra-wideband antenna is designed for breast tumor detection, which operates at 5Ghz frequency range. From the simulation results, the best return loss of -40.32 dB is obtained at 5.2GHz. Moreover, the large bandwidth obtained is 3.46GHz with respect to -10dB. Antenna is simulated with/without tumor to obtain the E-field, H-field, and SAR values. From the simulations, the E-field value are 12667 v/m for non-tumor and 13270 v/m for tumor. The H-field values are 60.9 A/m for non-tumor and 60.6 A/m for tumor. The SAR values obtained were 0.208 w/kg for non-tumor and 0.206 w/kg for with tumor.

articleTitle: Classification Accuracy Improvement of Traffic Monitoring MW Radar by Velocity Compensation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this study, target classification using machine learning for traffic monitoring systems with millimeter-wave radar has been studied. Time-frequency analysis by STFT is a strong tool for radar data, thereby we can see difference of periodicity in Doppler frequency. However, it is difficult to distinguish targets having weak periodic motion such as bicycles and cars. In traffic monitoring systems, observation time for target classification is also an issue. Since the speed of cars is high, target classification in short observation time is required. In this paper, we propose a mean-velocity compensation to spectrograms in classification by CNN. Effectiveness of velocity compensation in limited observation time is verified by using experimental dataset.

articleTitle: Preliminary Result of a Wide-band Radio Frequency Moisture Sensor for Oil and Gas Pipe Thermal Insulator
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the preliminary measurement result of the wide-band radio frequency (RF) moisture sensor for oil and gas pipe thermal insulator. The thermal insulator with metal jacket such as fiberglass, mineral wool, rock wool, cellulose, polyurethane foam, polyurethane, etc. is employed around pipelines, piping and other equipment to control the temperature during transfer of substance. The corrosion under thermal insulator (CUI) due to salt water is the most dangerous problem when undetected. The indirect method for detecting CUI employs the thermal insulator moisture data. The advantages of the proposed wide-band RF moisture sensor are a wide detection rage compared to the conventional technique and high accuracy. The proposed system consists the voltage control oscillate (VCO) of 1.2 GHz to 2.7 GHz, the power detector, the microcontroller and transmitting (Tx) RF probe and receiving RF probe.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Dual-band Fan-beam Metaline-based Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents an array antenna composed of two circularly polarized (CP) metalines. The array radiates a CP fan-beam within two frequency bands; one frequency band is below the transition frequency of the metaline, and the other is above the transition frequency. The antenna characteristics, including the gain, axial ratio, and VSWR, are analyzed and discussed.

articleTitle: An Optimized Sampling Scheme for Multi-probe Spherical Near-field Measurement
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An optimized sampling scheme for more efficient multi-probe spherical near-field measurement is proposed, which is suitable for measurement systems with an electric scanning mode in theta or phi. By properly decreasing the sampling interval that related to mechanical scanning, the proposed sampling scheme is proved efficient for improving measurement efficiency though theoretic analysis of different sampling schemes employing the spherical near-field to far-field transformation algorithm. The validity of the algorithm is also verified through comparing the transformed results with simulated ones.

articleTitle: Broadband Circuit Analog Absorber Using Low-Cost Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The authors propose a broadband circuit analog absorber using a low-cost frequency selective surface. The center of a Jerusalem cross element was modified to reduce four resistors on each arm to a single resistor. The elements were arranged in a chessboard-like configuration to cancel the cross-polarized reflection generated by the asymmetric shape of the element. The experimental results show the proposed absorber provides 61.1% bandwidth for -10-dB reflection at 6.7 GHz.

articleTitle: Propagation Characteristics and Channel Capacity with Drone Height
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: To cope with the increase in communication traffic, the use of microwaves and millimeter-wave bands has been recently studied for outdoor use. However, the transmission enhancing the high received power has become a new challenge, because the path loss increases in the high frequency band. This study aims to reduce the propagation loss by relaying autonomous unmanned aerial vehicles (Drones). We propose a model based on the Drone height as a parameter and evaluate the channel capacity using the model to demonstrate the effectiveness of Drone relay stations.

articleTitle: Obliquely-Cut Horn Antennas Loading a Half-Cylindrical Conductor for a Widely Tilted Sectoral Beam
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a compact horn antenna loading a half cylindrical conductor for covering a specified wide circular area with a tilted sectoral beam. The proposed antenna can tilt the radiated beam to direction of 30 degrees at 24GHz by making the structure of the horn an asymmetric structure. Furthermore, a dielectric lens is inserted for supporting the cutting conductor. Usefulness of the proposed antenna is verified numerically.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of Optical Leaky wave Antenna Excited by Photonic Bandgap Parabolic reflector with Thin Glass Layer
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents gain enhancement method of optical leaky wave antenna excited by parabolic reflector. This antenna uses Photonic Band Gap (PBG) as parabolic reflector to excite Grating Wave Guide (GWG). PBG reflector does not give the perfect reflection and causes the decrease of gain. We propose the gain enhancement by a new parabolic reflector combining PBG and glass layer.

articleTitle: Women in Science—A Case Study from Husband’s Point of View—
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We consider an example of a female scientist who is leading the large-scale atmospheric radar construction project from the perspective of her husband. It is of course dangerous to draw a general feature from such an example, but it may be a case that can be referred to by female researchers who are active in the engineering field. After briefly reviewing the history of the project and clarifying its special features, we consider the possible role of a husband in such cases.

articleTitle: Active Millimeter-Wave Imaging Using Incoherent Illumination with Multiple Incident Angles
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The active millimeter-wave imaging using incoherent illumination is studied to improve contrast between the objects and human body. The multi-directional illumination are applied to decrease the angle dependence of the image contrast. It is demonstrated the quality of imaging of the object is largely improved by using the proposed imaging method.

articleTitle: Development of UHF-RFID tag antenna for identifying liquid filled containers
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recently, RFID (Radio Frequency IDentiflcation) system is expected to serve as the distribution management system of the alternative to bar-codes. If a tag antenna that can be identified even when attached to the surface of metal or high lossy dielectrics is developed, high precision and automation of various product management can be expected. In this report, the development of the tag antenna for UHF-RFID system that can be attached to containers such as blood samples or liquid medicines is described.

articleTitle: Conformal Subarray Antenna for Circularly Polarized Synthetic Aperture Radar onboard UAV
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a preliminary design of a conformal subarray antenna for circularly polarized synthetic aperture radar (CP-SAR) onboard UAV. The CP-SAR is operated in C-band with the center frequency of 5.3 GHz and bandwidth of 400 MHz. Limitation space inside the fuselage and the CP-SAR signal attenuation issue caused by the fuselage material will be attempted to overcome by installing a conformal CP-SAR antenna wrap-around outside the UAV fuselage. An osculating circle with a radius curvature of 920 mm is used to reference fuselage curvature to bend the antenna. Simulation results show the conformal antenna achieves excellent performance characteristics. The antenna is currently fabricated and will be validated in the next work.

articleTitle: Measurement of Received Polarization Characteristics by a Vehicle-Mounted Antenna in Cellular Communication Environments
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we show a measured result of the polarization characteristics for vehicle-mounted antenna by receiving radio signals of an existing cellular system. We examine the XPD characteristics when the reflections of a vehicle body exist by setting three different antenna positions. We further consider the gain where dual polarizations could be ideally utilized.

articleTitle: Metasurface Bandwidth Enhancement with a Non-Foster Load
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The operational bandwidth of a metasurface is limited by variation of the reflection coefficient phase. Loading metasurface unit cells with a non-Foster circuit allows for remarkable enhancement of the operational bandwidth. Proper design of a negative impedance converter (NIC) to implement necessary non-Foster load is essential for a broadband metasurface design. Recently, we have presented a design methodology for NICs with low conversion error. In this paper, the methodology is applied to design of a non-Foster load to extend the operational bandwidth of a metasurface designed for the center frequency of 2.45 GHz. The bandwidth enhancement from 7% to 38%, i.e. by a factor of 5.4 is demonstrated when using the practical non-Foster load and NIC based on bipolar junction transistors.

articleTitle: VESBR for the Electromagnetic Scattering of Multilayered Dielectric Objects
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Volume equivalent shooting and bouncing ray (VESBR) is a high frequency method, which first introduces volume equivalent sources to consider the contribution of dielectric medium. In previous work, it has been proved its performance in analyzing the scattering of dielectric and composite objects. In this paper, VESBR is extended to analyze the scattering from multilayered dielectric object. Simulation of double layer dielectric medium show that the results of VESBR agree well with those of surface integral equation (SIE). While the computation time and the required memory of VESBR are much less than those of SIE.

articleTitle: Radio Propagation Analysis of Low Base Station Antenna by Mobile Measurement in Urban Street Cell Environment
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In the 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> generation mobile communication system, high frequency bands over 6GHz are used to realize high speed and large capacity communication. Because of high path losses, these bands are considered to use in small cells at low base station antenna. In this paper, measured data with moving using a channel sounder at 20GHz is analyzed for a low base station antenna installed in an urban street cell environment to clarify the radio wave propagation characteristics.

articleTitle: Design of a Wideband Phased Array Antenna with Ultrawide Scanning Angle to 70 Degree
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A wideband phased array antenna (PAA) is designed and numerically demonstrated with ultrawide scanning angle up to 70 degree. A tapered slot antenna (TSA) is chosen as the PAA element which is optimized in a full wave solver. Results shows its capability to provide VSWR≤3 from normal to 70 degree from 2.17GHz to 6.71GHz. To study the broadband radiation patterns at the normal direction, a PAA composed of 9×9 TSA elements is built in the full wave solver. The scanning performances at 6GHz are also studied, with scanning angles from 0 to 70 degree by changing the feeding phases.

articleTitle: Transmit Power Control Method for Centrally Controlled Wireless LANs with MU-MIMO
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a transmit power control method to reduce power consumption and alleviate inter-cell interference for centrally controlled wireless LANs with multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO). The main feature of the proposed method is to control the transmit power of the access points (APs) according to the relationship between the number of allocated users and AP antennas. The effectiveness of the proposed method compared to the conventional fixed transmit power method is demonstrated in terms of power consumption and system throughput via computer simulations.

articleTitle: Prototype Evaluation of Monopulse Beam Steering Circularly Polarized Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a beam steering circularly polarized array antenna which employs input amplitude control based on the monopulse mechanism and perturbation technique. The radiation pattern of the antenna can be controlled by changing the amplitude ratio of two input signals. The proposed antenna is numerically analyzed and designed by using electromagnetic simulation with theoretical discussion. The measured results of a prototype antenna confirm the feasibility of the proposed antenna. Beam tilt angles from 2° to 28° were obtained with axial ratios around 1 dB.

articleTitle: EM-Transparency for Improving Angular Accuracy of a Reactively Loaded MIMO/AOA Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Previously, we have developed a method of eliminating coupling between AOA and MIMO arrays by optimizing reactive loads. In this paper, to investigate the mechanism, a new physical measure, named the CAR (Current Area Ratio), is introduced to show that EM-transparency of the elements is attained due to the cancellation of radiation fields, caused by the out-of-phase currents induced on the elements.

articleTitle: Electric Field Reconstruction of Antenna inside Phantom for Non-invasive SAR Measurement
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper studies electric field reconstruction for antenna inside phantom. The application is aimed for non-invasive SAR measurement of in-body antenna. The method relates electromagnetic currents on the surface enclosing the test subject (antenna and phantom combination) to the scattered external field received by probe. From the surface currents, we were able to reconstruct the internal electric field of phantom with known permittivity, ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> = 45. It is shown that we can obtain good result in lossless sphere case.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Over-The-Air Apparatus for Generating Cluster Environment
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents an appropriate scatterer arrangement that realizes a cluster propagation environment with a Gaussian distribution in azimuth and elevation. Considering the practicability and cost of manufacturing, the size of the instruments needs to be as small as possible. The analytical results show that the arrangement of scatterers can be determined by adjusting the angular spread of the incoming wave with a certain minimum power.

articleTitle: Circularly-Polarized Circular Meandered Microstrip Antennas for WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A meandered quarter-mode of the circle with arc-shaped slots and a probe-feed is proposed to produce CP radiation. Two antennas are presented, in which, one is with two arc-shaped slots and the other is having 3-arc-shaped slots to control the return-loss at the phase-shift variation of two orthogonal-modes. The 10dB Bandwidth of the Antenna-1 (A1) is 1.24GHz (4.52-5.76GHz) and Antenna-2 (A2) is 1.21GHz (4.5-5.71GHz). The 3dB AR Bandwidth of A1 is 200 MHz (4810-5010 MHz) and A2 is 120MHz (4830-4950 MHz). The gain obtained for both antennas is 5dBic. The proposed antennas are fabricated and the simulation analysis is presented.

articleTitle: Quarter-Wave Line Inserted Series- and Shunt-Diodes Rectifier Tolerant of DC Load Resistance Deviation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a brand-new topology of diode rectifier intended for wireless power transfer applications. The key point of our topology is a quarter-wave transmission line that is inserted between two diodes: one in series and the other in shunt. Thanks to the quarter-wave line, the two diodes work in two different modes in accordance with the load resistance's change. This topology remarkably improves the rectifier's tolerance to load resistance deviation. The prototype successfully proves our concept showing that it works for wider than one decade of the load resistance range, which could not be done by conventional rectifiers.

articleTitle: Multi-mode Circular Waveguide Antenna with Orbital Angular Momentum
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Electromagnetic wave that carries orbital angular momentum (OAM) can be expected to have a large channel capacitance at the same frequency. In this paper, a circular waveguide antenna generating circular polarization (CP) and orthogonal two orbital angular momentum modes is presented. This antenna consists of two circular waveguides, an outer one and inner one, which generate OAM of orders l = ±1 modes and circular polarization of l = ±0, respectively. As the result, we have found the possibility of four independent transmission paths at 2.4 GHz.

articleTitle: Elucidation of Impedance Conditions in High-Efficiency Operation RF-DC Conversion Circuits
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An impedance relationship was speculated from the automatic design of the high-efficiency RF-DC conversion circuit. By the measurement, it was found that each of the reactance of the operating impedance of the diode and the input filter are complex conjugates, and the method manufacturing high-efficiency RF-DC conversion circuit was clarified.

articleTitle: Near Field Co-Planar Phase-less Measurement for EIRP Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a simple, quick and compact measurement system to evaluate patch array antenna. In this system, we focus on phase-less, and co-planar measurement. This measurement is effective for EIRP evaluation of 5G user equipment.

Author Keywords: NFFF(Near field to Far field transformation)

articleTitle: Study on Frequency Characteristic for Self-Calibration Method of Systematic Errors for DBF Antenna Using Gating Process
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: National Institute of Information and Communications Technology (NICT) is currently researching and developing an array-fed reflector antenna that flexibly changes the coverage area using a DBF and improves the frequency utilization efficiency using a DC for next-generation communication satellites in the Ka-band. The systematic error calibration of an array feed is very important because the influence of phase errors appears prominently in the characteristics of the antennas. We propose a self-calibration system for an array feed using a pickup antenna and gating process to realize a more accurate systematic error calibration for array-fed reflector antennas. The calibration values for the array feed are obtained from the coupling characteristics using a pickup antenna from which the noise is removed by a gating process. This report shows that the proposed method does not affect the radiation pattern calibration even if the calibration coefficient is calculated from the coupling characteristic of an arbitrary frequency in the operation band.

articleTitle: Disk Loaded Monopole Antenna Installed in Metal Cylinder
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recently, a compact, conformal and metal-mountable antennas for radio-frequency identification (RFID) tags have been studied to manage metal cylinder of various shapes wirelessly. In addition, the radiation characteristics of RFID tag antennas placed inside a metal cylinder have also been investigated. However, the antennas attached to consumable parts inside a metal cylinder has not been considered. This paper presents the radiation characteristics of disk loaded monopole antenna placed in the metal cylinder.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on 2-Element Rectenna Array Using Yagi-Uda Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a rectenna array employing planar Yagi-Uda antennas. The planar Yagi-Uda antenna has endfire radiation and rectenna arrays can be realized by simply stacking the proposed rectennas. Therefore, the proposed rectenna array effectively increases the output DC power by arraying multiple rectennas. In this paper, the performance of a 2-element rectenna array is experimentally evaluated. The maximum output power is obtained when the array spacing is 0.7λ and the optimum load resistance of each single rectenna is almost constant regardless of the array spacing.

articleTitle: Effect of Particle Filter to the Finger Print with wide coordinate interval
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Currently, research is being conducted on location estimation using wireless LAN access points. In this research, we apply a particle filter, which is one of the time series filters, to examine the design method of its parameters and evaluate its accuracy. As a result of adjusting the parameters in the proposed method, the estimation error could be reduced. It was also confirmed that the proposed method can improve the accuracy more than the conventional method even if the DB coordinate interval increases.

articleTitle: Undersea Positioning Using Electromagnetic Wave in Consideration of Sea Wave Effects
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this study, assuming we specify the positions of the divers rescuing in the accidents and support their works, we investigate undersea positioning technology using the electromagnetic waves with low frequency (10 kHz). In this paper, assuming we employ our positioning system in the factual situation, we investigated the effect of sea waves to our positioning system. Also, we show the result of positioning estimation in case of taking the measure to the sea waves.

articleTitle: A Study on Indoor Human Moving Route Estimation using Several Receivers of 920 MHz Band Radio Waves
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: There is a growing need for estimation of human movement route in a room for crime prevention, monitoring of the elderly, the workers’ situation. This study aims to realize human movement route estimation using radio waves, by focusing on the changes in the wave propagation affected by human motion. This paper proposes a method of estimating the human moving route in a room using RSSI (Received Signal Strength Indicator) of 920 MHz band radio waves. We performed empirical evaluations of the proposed system with one transmitter and four receivers.

articleTitle: Array-Fed Dual-Band Transmitarray Antenna with Wide Frequency Ratio
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a novel aperture coupled patch array-fed dual-band transmitarray antenna with frequency ratio of 1.7 (10 GHz and 17 GHz). First, by introducing square loop slot and cross dipole slot, the element demonstrates over 75% phase coverage. Then, two aperture coupled patch array antennas are designed to illuminate the aperture, providing advantages of being low-profile and lightweight. Full-wave simulations show that realized gain of 22.3 dBi and 23.3 dBi, and 1-dB gain bandwidth of 3% and 5.3% are achieved in 10 GHz band and 17 GHz band, respectively.

articleTitle: Experimental Results of n261 Millimeter-Wave Module for Mobile Device
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A millimeter-wave module integrated with PCB is proposed. The placement and stacking of mobile device could provide good robustness. The simulated and measured performance of PCB only case will be studied in this paper.

articleTitle: Cost effective wideband Ka flat lens antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A flat wideband lens antenna operating in Ka band is designed. The design corresponds to the transformation of an hyperbolic lens via quasi-optic transformation into a flat lens. The implementation of the lens is made using 3D printing technology. Simulations accounting for the exact replica of the manufactured lens (including the details of the patterns created by the printer) are made. The experimental results show an excellent agreement with the simulations, including low losses. The presented design is a low cost antenna providing gains above 23 dBi in the whole Ka band.

articleTitle: Low-order linear array for FM passive radar: calibration and beamforming
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An array factor models the ideal response of an antenna array to the far field source. In order to coherently add a far-field signal array factor model must be known. However, the model does not include errors that are encountered in reality. This discrepancy leads to significant loss of coherent gain of the array. This paper describes an array calibration method we used for compensating error in our 4-antenna FM linear array. We show the improvement we got using the error compensation method in direction finding as well as array pattern from real signals.

articleTitle: Frequency Selective Surfaces Using Hexagonal Interwoven Structures
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, an ultra-compact, angular stable, wide-band, and low-profile Frequency Selective Surface based on intertwined structures is presented. The unit cell is created by entwining the arms of a hexagonal structure with its neighbor cells until the structure is tessellated. The Fractional Bandwidth of the proposed structure is 92.45%, which is the highest value found in the literature regarding intertwined structures. A further increase in λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>/P, preserving a similar Fractional Bandwidth of the original unit cell, is obtained by extending the unit cell in the 2.5 dimension. Simulations results show that the lowest dimensions of the unit cell are 0.029λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> x 0.029λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>. The miniaturization capabilities of this design are reflected by the high values of equivalent inductance and capacitance, generated by the geometry of the structure. Two prototypes are manufactured using the photolithography technique, which will be measured and compared with the simulation results. This design is suitable to be used for buildings propagation control and as meta-surface for space limited applications such as RCS reduction for small and irregular objects and ground plane for antennas in mobile terminals.

articleTitle: Review on Wideband and Compact CTS Arrays at Millimeter Waves
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, three state-of-the-art parallel-fed continuous transverse stub (CTS) arrays are presented. They operate at various frequency bands ranging from 20 GHz up to 86 GHz. The multiple capabilities of this architecture, such as side-lobe level reduction, active beam switching, and wideband operation with an ultra-low-profile, are here reviewed. Moreover, the suitability of the antenna concept for multiple fabrication technologies is demonstrated. The performance and key design solutions of three prototypes manufactured using milling techniques, low-temperature co-fired ceramic and printed circuit board technology are showcased.

articleTitle: Physical-Statistical Model for UAV-to-Ground Urban Radio Channels
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A physical-statistical ray-based model is applied to model the UAV-to-ground radio channel in urban areas. The modeling method relies on simple input data, such as input distribution parameters (e.g. mean building height, building height variance). The physical part of the model being based on ray-tracing, it is also applicable over very wide parameter ranges at a very low computation time thanks to a pre-calculation procedure.

articleTitle: Packaged Dish Antenna for Wireless Terahertz Photonic Crystal Waveguide Devices
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A robust packaging structure for all-silicon terahertz photonic crystal waveguide devices is devised. A reflector dish is incorporated, to realize a scalable, wide-aperture antenna for practical wireless applications of terahertz waves.

articleTitle: Performance of interference suppression system in environment where artificial noise is mixed into multiple desired signals
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recently, electromagnetic interference in AM radio receivers associated with noise generated from the power control unit (DC-DC converters) in hybrid vehicles (HVs) has becomes a serious problem. To address this problem, a noise suppression method thorough digital signal processing in an AM radio is proposed in the past research. However, the method is only applicable to single desired signal. In this paper, the reduction performance by the method for multiple desired signals is confirmed.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave and THz links under severe weather condition
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Millimeter-waves and THz-waves can offer high-speed wireless transmission. However, transmission distance would be limited due to atmospheric attenuation and rain attenuation. In addition, mechanical vibration by wind would have impact on link performance, because the wavelengths of carriers are less than a few millimeters. This presentation reviews recent studies on fixed wireless link performance under severe weather condition.

articleTitle: Inverse scattering approach by using cost functional consisting the approximated stored energy with no information on incident field
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An initial-boundary value problem is set up whose solution coincides with that of the original scattering problem in the interior region bounded by the observation surface if and only if a medium inside the observation surface is the same as that of the original one. Based on this initial- boundary value problem, we present an inverse scattering method by using cost functional consisting the approximated stored energy with no information on incident field. A cost functional consisting of the approximated stored energy of the misfit field between the original problem and the boundary value problem with an estimated object is introduced to solve the inverse problem. Preliminary numerical examples are provided to assess the proposed inversion approach.

articleTitle: Design of Hybrid Tapered TEM Horn for Radiated Immunity Test in Close Proximity
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We have designed a wideband TEM horn with a hybrid structure comprising linear and curved tapered plates and optimized it for radiated immunity tests in close proximity as specified in the IEC standard. Analytical results of numerical simulations show that the proposed hybrid tapered TEM horn has wideband radiation characteristics covering a test frequency range of 380 MHz to 6 GHz and generates a homogeneous field while realizing downsizing.

Author Keywords: Radiated immunity test in close proximity

articleTitle: On the Convergence of the Iterative Gauss-Seidel-Based Electric Field Algorithm for the Solution of Antenna Array Mutual Coupling
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recently, a new method for the solution of the antenna array mutual coupling (MC), which is based on the field data of an isolated element and relates to the iterative Gauss-Seidel method, has been proposed. In this paper, we study the convergence of the proposed method by comparing it with the convergence of the classical Gauss-Seidel iteration applied to a method-of-moments (MoM) system. Despite several approximations being used in the field-based method, similar behavior between the two methods has been observed, both in terms of the stability and the rate of the convergence.

articleTitle: Assessment of Television White Space in the Greater Metro Manila Area through Geospatial and Empirical Approaches
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This work provides an assessment of TV white space in the UHF band (470-698 MHz), in the Greater Metro Manila Area (GMMA). Radio propagation simulations were performed using Okumura-Hata and Hata-9999 models. Spectrum measurement was done using a portable spectrum analyzer along a single route from Metropolitan Manila to a nearby province. Assessment of TV white space was done by identifying area with field strength values less than the FCC's Grade B contour threshold. On the other hand, FCME algorithm was used to identify white spaces from the spectrum measurement data. Results show that there are white spaces in the GMMA, especially outside Metropolitan Manila which can be utilized for secondary use.

articleTitle: Efficiency Enhancement of Wireless Power Transfer Localization using Defected Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a defected metasurface for efficiency enhancement of wireless power transfer localization. To examine this study, the WPT system composes of large Tx small Rx and 5x5 metasurface, which is designed at the operating frequency of 13.56 MHz. Simulated results show that the efficiency of WPT with defected metasurface of 38% when the Rx is placed at the corner unit cell metasurface. Such efficiency result equal the uniform metasurface case with Rx at center.

articleTitle: DoA Estimation on A MIMO Handset
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper describes Direction-of-Arrival (DoA) estimation on a Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) enabled handset. A 4-port antenna system is used in a realistic handset and all the electromagnetic effects are taken into consideration, including antenna terminations and the user. The Polynomial Root Finding (PRF) DoA estimation technique for uniform linear arrays is adapted to address the naturally irregular grid of antenna elements in a realistic handset. This adaptation is accomplished in two separate ways; via Manifold Separation Technique (MST) and via Gaussian Processes Regression (GPR). Simulation results show reasonable DoA estimation accuracy even with few calibration data.

articleTitle: A Study on Beam Narrowing and Gain Enhancement of Patch Array Antenna Using FSS
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a study on beam narrowing and gain enhancement of a patch array antenna by loading Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) consisting of periodic arrangement of rectangular dipoles. The dipole element is designed so that its length get shorter towards the end of the antenna to equalize the phase distribution on the aperture surface. Antenna characteristics are evaluated by performing the finite-difference time domain (FDTD) analysis for the case when the main beam direction of the patch array antenna is the broadside and when the main beam direction is tilted from the broadside. From the simulated results, beam narrowing and gain enhancement are confirmed for the above-mentioned cases.

articleTitle: Prediction for Cluttered Building Entry Loss using ITU-R Propagation Models: Sum of the Building Entry Loss and the Clutter Loss
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Lately, in the ITU-R, developing a cluttered building entry loss (BEL) model has been a "hot" issue, although an uncluttered BEL model was already developed and published in its Recommendation ITU-R P.2109. In this paper, by combining with the clutter loss model from the existing ITU-R recommendation, a methodology of deriving sum statistics of cluttered BEL is proposed.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Double-Directional Channel Sounder using COTS RF Transceivers
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: To date various wireless systems using millimeter-wave bands have already been developed. However, the demand for more accurate channel models is still increasing. In this study, a millimeter-wave double-directional channel sounding system using commercial off-the-shelf RF transceivers is presented where an analog beamformer based electrical beam-steering offers a fast double-directional channel acquisition. In addition, this paper developed a high-resolution multi-path parameter estimation algorithm from the multi-dimensional power spectrum. Finally, as validation, the scattering processes were identified by comparing the path parameters extracted from the power spectrum obtained from measurements with the interacting objects in the real environment.

articleTitle: An annular patch circularly polarized antenna in 920-MHz band
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A circularly polarized microstrip patch antenna in 920-MHz band was designed and fabricated. This antenna has an annular-ring patch as the radiating conductor and radiates circular polarization by making two slits on the patch. The simulation and measurement results were shown, and then the effect of a conductor protrusion was analyzed when it was inserted in the center of the ring patch. This antenna is intended for applications in which a conductor protrusion exists inside the ring like a gear wheel.

articleTitle: Scattering Control of Electromagnetic Waves via Space-Modulation Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Controlling the scattering of light or electromagnetic waves are conventionally realized based on the different phases profile of metasurfaces elements. However, this approach is limited to the operating frequency bandwidth and cannot achieve such functionality as frequency beam-scanning. Here, we present a concept of space-modulated metasurface in which the structure is making up with the non-resonated elements. We show that the design can achieve both frequency beam-scanning and fixed-frequency beam-scanning. Also, it provides a large operation bandwidth comparing to the conventional metasurface-based resonating structure. Finally, we fabricate the sample, and the measured responses show reasonable agreement with the simulated results.

articleTitle: A Preliminary Experiment on Relationship between Soil Moisture and Attenuation Constant of 920 MHz Band Radio Waves
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The increases of soil moisture content is a landslide disaster harbinger phenomenon. The attenuation constant of the radio wave increases with the soil moisture content. This study aims to realize the soil moisture content estimation by calculating the attenuation constant based on a measured received signal strength indicator (RSSI) of 920 MHz band radio waves. This paper shows the result of the preliminary experiment of the relationship between the attenuation constant of radio waves and soil moisture content.

articleTitle: Development of high-impedance antenna for energy harvesting in ISM band
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recently, Electromagnetic wave energy harvesting is attracting attention as a means of supplying power to self-contained sensor networks. When the sensor node self-contains power, the total maintenance cost of sensor networks will be reduced. It is thought that the high input impedance antenna is suitable to adjust to rectifier circuits. In this report, the high impedance planar antenna is developed, and evaluated results about its utility are described.

Author Keywords: High impedance planar antenna Twin loop antenna

articleTitle: Directional Loop-Type Antenna Technologies Applied to Satellite and Terrestrial Integrated Mobile Phone Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this article, a brief overview and discussion on some loop-type antenna technologies applied satellite and terrestrial integrated mobile phone applications is presented. By properly applying distinct characteristics of different resonant modes of various loop-type antenna designs as array elements, different application requirements of beamforming array antennas for satellite mobile phones including multi-band operations, dual-polarization or wide beam-scanning coverage could be achieved.

articleTitle: Reconstruction of Dipole Antenna Current Distribution based on Boundary Integral Equations
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this research, reconstruction method for current distribution of dipole antenna is proposed. The reconstruction method for current distribution of antenna is useful, because the radiated electromagnetic field can be estimate by using dipole antenna current. The proposed reconstruct method utilize boundary integral method. The effectiveness of the proposed method is confirmed by comparing with simulation result based on MoM.

articleTitle: Study of Posture Estimation Using MIMO Sensor Based on CSI
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, person postures are estimated by MIMO sensor and the machine learning using channel state information (CSI). MIMO sensors are superior to cameras used in conventional surveillance systems in that they do not invade privacy and can sense even outside the line of sight. CSI are calculated from the data obtained from the sensor measurements, and then the posture classification is performed by the machine learning model based on CSI. The model is trained from the actual measured data and its classification performance is evaluated.

articleTitle: Metamaterial – Based Microwave Band – Stop Filter for Wi – Fi Blocking Window
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, we propose a novel Wi - Fi blocking window based on metamaterial microwave band - stop filter. Made of glass and fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO), the proposed window is transparent for visible light, allows other RF waves to go though significantly while completely blocks the Wi - Fi signal. With such property, this window can be used for confidential purpose.

articleTitle: Distance Dependence of Transmission Characteristics Between Small Dipole Antennas in Tissue Equivalent Liquid Operated in kHz Band
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Introducing a longer water tank with a width of 1200 mm which is filled with tissue equivalent liquid imitating human tissue, small dipole antennas can be faced each other to measure the transmission characteristics between them as a function of distance in the kHz band. Then, it is possible to examine the transmission characteristics at a distance of 200 mm or more, which could not be measured by the water tank used before. It is quantitatively shown that the effect of common mode current can be observed in our measurement setup and eliminated by appropriately applying time domain gating technique.

articleTitle: Design of High-pass Space Filter Using Periodically Perforated Metal Plates and Dielectric Material
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The authors propose the novel space filters that combines two periodically perforated metal plates and the dielectric material. In this study, we confirmed that these structures function as electromagnetic wave transmission control materials by FDTD analysis and experiments in free space.

articleTitle: Wide-band Injection-Locked Frequency Dividers of Concurrent Oscillating RF Stress
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This article studies the over-voltage stress effect on a dual-resonance divide-by-2 injection-locked frequency divider (ILFD). The ILFD consists of two sub-ILFDs coupled by magnetic field and it can operate in three modes with overlapped locking ranges. The outputs of ILFD can be measured at high-band and low-band buffers, the measured data on low-band buffer shows high figure of merit (FOM). Concurrent-oscillating over-voltage bias degrades both FETs in high-band and low-band sub-ILFDs and causes the degradation of the low-and high-band locking ranges. The degradation of the FOM evaluated at high-band buffer is severe, so better operation condition is to measure the output at low-band buffer for microwave applications.

articleTitle: Dispersionless Optical Activity in 3-D Chiral Metamaterial Composed of High-K Dielectric Cube and Metallic Mesh
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a 3-D chiral metamaterial comprising of a high-K dielectric cube and metallic mesh in the microwave region. Our numerical results show that the metamaterial has dispersionless optical activity and an impedance matching to free space, resulting in broad polarization rotation and low reflectance.

articleTitle: Extended Beamforming by Restored Phase Information of Virtual Array Input Signal
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We propose a beamforming and signal demodulation method for the development of two-dimensional (2D) array antennas. The authors have studied an extended beamforming method by using Khatri-Rao (KR) product, however it corresponds only to real-valued signals like BPSK. In this paper, we aim at improving the extended beamforming performance by recovering phase information in demodulation scheme. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated through computer simulation.

articleTitle: Effect of Antenna Pattern of Radar on Vibration Estimation for Infrastructure Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recently, a way of detecting the signs of deterioration of the infrastructures has been needed. Measuring the vibration state of structures by using millimeter-wave radar is one of the useful methods. However, sometimes the radar itself is subject to disturbances such as vibration when measuring structures outdoors. Hence, the way of removing the vibration disturbances by taking the cross-spectrum of the baseband signals obtained by two radars has been proposed. In this paper, we examined the effect of antenna pattern on vibration estimation with the disturbance cancellation method. The simulation result suggests that the estimation error of the vibration amplitude is less than 1% when the half-power beam width of the antenna is smaller than 40°.

articleTitle: DoA Estimation Results in 20-GHz Band Using Compressed Sensing
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The 28-GHz band is used in the 5th generation mobile communication system (5G) [1]. In 5G, the introduction of massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) is being considered, and in an environment with large propagation loss such as that of millimeter waves, massive MIMO can realize beamforming according to the position of the terminal [1]. Therefore, it is important to understand the direction of arrival in the millimeter wave band. In this study, we conducted an experiment using a 48-element circular array in the 20 GHz band in the urban area of Niigata City, and also performed ray tracing assuming the same environment. In addition, we show the direction of arrival (DoA) estimation results using iterative reduction threshold algorithm (ISTA), which is based on compressed sensing. It is shown that the main path can be estimated by using ISTA even with approximately 5 elements.

articleTitle: Experimental Validation for Temperature Rise in Human Tissue Due to Implanted Metal Plates with Screw Holes Using Translucent Solid Phantom
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduced numerical estimations for SAR enhancement in human tissue due to metal plate implants with screw holes. To investigate the impact of the metal implants, we numerically evaluate SAR of human head phantom with complicated shaped metal implants. From the simulation results, SAR enhancement due to the implanted metallic plates was clearly observed at specific frequency. We also achieved temperature increase measurements using translucent solid phantoms in order to confirm validation of the numerical results.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Antenna Arrays for Integrated Space and Terrestrial Networks
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Integrated space and terrestrial networks are expected to be a key technology for beyond 5G communications systems. One main challenge posed for the antennas is the array performance deterioration caused by orientation changes of various elements mounted to conformal platforms. To overcome this challenge, a reconfigurable antenna element that can switch among four linear polarizations is reported and applied to a conformal array. An efficient array synthesis algorithm is utilized to attain high-gain, low-sidelobes, and low-cross-polarization characteristics. A linear conformal array is presented to verify the effectiveness of the developed algorithm.

articleTitle: IM Evaluation of Electronic Devices using Circular Polarized Sensing Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we consider a method measure nonlinear noise in electronic devices by exposing to electromagnetic waves. First, we consider polarization dependence of IM by linearly polarized wave. Secondly, we investigate the method of measuring by circular polarized wave.

articleTitle: Study of Antenna Misalignment Effects on Path Loss for a Liver-implant Channel
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: With the promising use of ultra-wideband (UWB) technology for wireless implantable devices in many future medical applications, channel behaviors inside the human body under various circumstances need to be extensively evaluated. This paper investigates the characteristics of UWB channel for liver-implant, considering the effect of antenna misalignment for the in-body to off-body communication scenario. A heterogeneous digital male body model was utilized in the numerical study and path loss data was obtained and analyzed. The results demonstrate that antenna misalignment leads to an increase in the path loss by about 6 dB.

articleTitle: Correlation Control of Random Variables for Setting the Number of Paths in Monte-Carlo Simulation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a method of setting the number of paths in Monte-Carlo simulation for large-scale MIMO antennas, in which random variables are generated using a linear combination of stationary and uncorrelated random numbers. The proposed method gives a Monte-Carlo simulation in a more realistic propagation environment with a predetermined number of paths.

articleTitle: A Design Concept of Grid-loaded Step Reflector Antenna with Coaxial-Mode Excitation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A reflector antenna excited by TM01 circular waveguide mode is being studied. A reflector antenna with steps was proposed. Since this antenna cancels out half of the polarized components, the polarization loss increases, theoretically by 3dB. Therefore, we propose a desgin to improve the gain by loading a metal grid on the reflector surface, as compared to the conventional antenna design.

articleTitle: EM-Decoupled Orthogonal Dipole Rotating Electric Fields in Synchronization with Propeller
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: To eliminate the EM-coupling between an antenna and a propeller, this paper presents an orthogonal dipole array with weighted signals combining in such a way that its electric fields can rotates in synchronization with propellers of a flying car. Instantaneous weight functions are developed so that the direction of electric field vector is perpendicular to that of propeller. Analytical results show that a large antenna gain is achieved regardless of the rotation angle of propeller.

articleTitle: Incident Angle Reconfigurable Metasurface by Mechanically Extending Diffraction Grating Period
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
