abstract: To solve the problem of shadow area in wireless network, a metasurface is expected to anomalously reflect the wave from base station to user in non-line-of-sight (NLOS) area. However, the sensitivity between an incident and reflection angles makes more inflexibility for reflector installation. Therefore, the technique to maintain the reflection angle of reflector, as the incident angle changed, is studied by separating supercell of metasurface. From both of simulation and experimental results, the designed 28 GHz metasurface can maintain a constant reflection angle at 45° while the incident angle is varied up to 0° - 10° without re-designing process.

articleTitle: Realization of Optimized Cylindrical Cloak Using Multi-Layer Ceramic Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the realization of the optimized cylindrical cloak. The unit cell is designed by locating a multi-layer ceramic capacitor (MLCC) between two dielectric substrates. By using two types of MLCC with capacitances of 3.6 pF and 3.9 pF, and loading a dielectric ring instead of the MLCCs to the 8th layer, it confirms that the reflection scattering of the optimized cylindrical cloak using MLCCs can be reduced in comparison with that of the cylindrical cloak using MLCCs based on the parameters of Schurig cloak.

articleTitle: Electrooptic sensing for antenna characterization and propagation investigation at THz band
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We show the two applications of an electrooptic sensing which is based on a nonpolarimetric frequency down conversion technique at terahertz frequency band. We demonstrate the near-field measurement and far-field characterization of a Cassegrain antenna at 300 GHz. We also demonstrate the visualization of a wave packet propagation in a free space at 120 GHz.

articleTitle: Wideband Halo Antenna with Four Parasitic Elements
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a Halo antenna with four parasitic elements is proposed as a horizontally polarized wideband antenna. The characteristics of the proposed antenna are analyzed through simulation. The results demonstrate that the antenna offers a small diameter and wideband performance. The relative bandwidth of the antenna is 12.1%, respectively. In addition, its radiation patterns are omnidirectional.

articleTitle: A study of propagation loss in micro-cell environments using measurement data at 2.2 GHz band
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The next generation (5th generation: 5G) of mobile communication systems have been investigated all over the world. Even after introduction of 5G, there are many terminals up to 4G. However, the concepts of controlling the interference effect of managed wireless nodes and maximizing the amount of communication in the entire network have been proposed. In this paper, the propagation loss characteristics are evaluated where a large number of Internet-of-Things (IoT) terminals are assumed. In this paper, we propose a simple propagation model in the 2.2 GHz band which considers the interference from the IoT terminals, based on the results of measurements in an urban environment.

articleTitle: Research of a metamaterial microfluidic sensor based on FANO resonance
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The combination of the metamaterials and microfluidic technology has provided a new research direction for higher sensitivity sensors. In this paper, an asymmetric metamaterial structure based on FANO resonance has been proposed. That structure is very sensitive to the small change of the dielectric constant. The simulation result shows that the resonant frequency moves 56 MHz averagely when the dielectric constant changes by 0.2. The measurement result is in good agreement with the simulation result in terms of the resonance frequency. That sensor has high sensitivity and great potential for chemical and biochemical detection in the future.

articleTitle: Stereolithography and Direct Metal Laser Sintering Applied to mm-Wave Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This document shows additive manufacturing as an advantageous option for manufacturing and design of components based on gap waveguide. 3D printing increases the degree of freedom in structural design because its complexity has no impact on the cost of production. This makes 3D printing an ideal manufacturing method for small devices with intricate details. The article compares two manufacturing techniques: stereolithography (SLA), which is based on copper-plated plastic, and direct metal laser sintering (DMLS), which generates an all-metal part. At 94 GHz, good results have only been obtained with SLA because of the better surface finish.

articleTitle: Study on Backward Transient Scattered Electric Fields from a Coated Metal Cylinder
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We calculate backward transient scattered electric fields from a coated metal cylinder, which is covered with a homogeneous medium layer. A time-domain asymptotic-numerical solution (TD-ANS) is used for computations in a backward transient scattered electric field by a coated metal cylinder. An analysis method using the TD-ANS provides a basis of nondestructive testing for corrosion degree of rebar in steel reinforced concrete structures. By comparing with a reference solution, we examine an interpretation method of response waveforms of backward transient scattered electric fields by using the TD-ANS.

articleTitle: Design of a Wideband Wing-shaped Small Printed Dipole Antenna for High-Power Jamming Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a wideband wing-shaped printed dipole antenna for high-power jamming systems. The proposed antenna is composed of a printed wing-shaped dipole radiator on a Duroid substrate, rectangular slots, a parasitic loop element, and matching posts to improve the impedance characteristics with a miniaturized physical antenna size. The proposed antenna has a fractional bandwidth of 67% with a center frequency of 4.5 GHz. The results show that the antenna is suitable for jamming systems with wideband characteristics.

articleTitle: RF Power Scavenger
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the process of designing and building of energy harvesting device to collect "free" RF ambient energy is presented. This experiment was conducted for a bachelor's degree Final Year Project at the University of Glasgow. The Power Scavenger device consists of a microstrip wideband antenna, a full wave rectifier and a capacitor as unit storage. The antenna has an omnidirectional radiation pattern in the horizontal plane and an -10-dB impedance bandwidth from 900 MHz to 2250 MHz. Measured results indicate energy harvesting up to 70 mV.

articleTitle: An Acceleration Method of Conformal Array Pattern Calculation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposed a fast calculation method that can speed up the synthesis of conformal array pattern. It firstly adjusts the beam pointing of the array unit based on the Euler rotation principle. Second, it uses the unit pattern simulated data as the sample of array. Finally, the far field data of each unit is linearly superimposed to obtain the whole conformal array pattern. The calculation results show that, the similarity between the proposed algorithm and the CST software can reach more than 95%, and the operation time of the CST software is 7.6 times of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: A Gridless Method for Microwave Coincidence Imaging Based on Atomic Norm Minimization
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Microwave coincidence imaging (MCI) has great potential in the staring and forward-looking imaging realms. However, the existing grid-based imaging methods usually suffer from grid mismatch problem which would significantly degrade the imaging performance. In this paper, a gridless MCI imaging method based on the atomic norm minimization (ANM) is proposed to offer a resolution to the grid mismatch problem, while maintaining the super-resolution ability of MCI.

articleTitle: Phase Adjustment Algorithm for Deformation Compensation of Nonflat Reflectarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper investigates an on-orbit calibration method for a nonflat reflectarray antenna. This paper proposes the antenna calibration method that uses a shape measurement device. The analysis in this paper shows that, with the proposed calibration method, the gain reduction due to shape deformations can be effectively ameliorated.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Q factor of Antennas in Lossy Medium
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the analytical expressions of Q factor of antennas in lossy medium are derived for two models. In model 1, the lossy medium is regarded as a part of the antenna, to emphasize he radiation loss. In model 2, the antenna is located inside a spherically layered lossy medium, to demonstrate the effect of both radiation loss and conductive loss. The analytical expressions are evaluated numerically and the results are compared with the results presented in previous researches.

articleTitle: Matching Circuit Design of Planer Frequency Dispersive Phase Shifter for Base Station Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A frequency-dispersive phase shifter has been proposed to improve communication capacity by increasing the tilt angle of the low-frequency band in multiband base station antennas for mobile communications. This paper describes the results of the design of the matching circuit on the electromagnetic field simulator. The matching circuit configuration is investigated by using random search to match with the transmission line, which has been a problem in the proposed phase shifter.

articleTitle: A Planar Retrodirective Array using Dual-mode Dielectric Resonator Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A planar retrodirective array was constructed by dual-mode dielectric resonator antennas. Each port of antennas was effectively connected by the periodic boundary condition. The pattern of the response wave was investigated by changing the apex and azimuth angle of the incident wave. As a result, the retrodirective operation was obtained for all angles of incidence.

articleTitle: High-Q Characterization of MW-Band Dielectric Resonator Rectenna Using an Equivalent Circuit
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper investigates the voltage amplification phenomenon by deriving equivalent circuit parameters for a coaxial dielectric resonator, where the equivalent circuit parameters are compared with the measured results. Furthermore, experimental studies on improving the radio frequency (RF)-direct current (DC) conversion efficiency using a λ/4-coaxial dielectric resonator with a higher Q factor are presented. The results show that the RF-DC conversion efficiency is improved by 13% at -10 dBm, as compared to that for a conventional dielectric resonator with a lower Q factor.

articleTitle: Reflection Characteristics of Metamaterial Electromagnetic Wave Absorbers and Its Relative Permittivity and Relative Permeability Evaluations
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Electromagnetic (EM) wave absorbers are frequently used in various places to remove undesired EM waves. Recently, the use of materials as EM wave absorbers has been reported. In this study, the authors evaluated the reflection characteristics of proposed metamaterial EM wave absorbers composed of a periodically metallic pattern arrangement structure and a dielectric material. Next, the relative permittivity and relative permeability characteristics of proposed metamaterial EM wave absorbers considered by using the S-parameter method.

articleTitle: Influence of concrete on patch antennas installed on utility poles
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In order to install a lot of 5G base stations, there is a method of installing them on utility poles. In this paper, antennas installed on utility poles (concrete poles) for 5G base stations are investigated numerically and experimentally. First, the influence of concrete and a reinforced bar embedded in concrete on the antenna characteristics are simulated using the FDTD method. Simulation results show that the influence of concrete and the reinforcing bars embedded in it are very small. We also measure the input characteristics and radiation pattern of the patch antenna on concrete to show the validity of the simulations.

articleTitle: Propagation Model and Scale Model Experiment of Light Domain for Clutter Loss in Urban Areas
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We predicted the clutter loss between a base station high up in the sky and a terrestrial mobile station in urban areas. In order to clarify the elevation angle characteristics of clutter loss at 100 GHz, the physical model using assumption of diffuse reflection on an building wall surface was proposed. In addition, a scale model experiment using visible light is conducted, and the validity of the proposal model is verified. A clutter loss at 100 GHz is predicted using the proposal model of light domain.

articleTitle: Rain Attenuation Characteristics due to Typhoon Wind Velocities in Satellite Communications Links
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Rain attenuation characteristics due to typhoon passage are discussed using the satellite signal observations conducted in Osaka, from 1988 to 2019. The ratio of hourly rain attenuation to rainfall rate is largely enhanced as the typhoon passes the east side of the station, while it becomes smaller in the case of west side passage. Compared with the ground wind velocities of nearby AMeDAS, the equivalent path lengths of rain attenuation become larger as the wind directions approach the opposite of the satellite azimuth angle, while they become smaller as the wind directions near the satellite azimuth angle.

articleTitle: Propagation Model in Corridor LOS Condition Based on ABG Approach
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper reports results of measurement campaign from 2 to 67 GHz in corridor LOS environment and proposes a propagation model based on ABG approach. From the comparison between measurement and predicted results by the proposed model, it is clarified that our model can be estimated basic transmission loss with sufficient accuracy.

articleTitle: Investigation of Hyperparameters for DOA Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In estimating the direction of arrival (DOA) of a radio wave using array antennas, the correlation matrix calculated from the received signals at each antenna element is generally used. In recent years, applied researches such as DOA estimation and radio propagation estimation using machine learning have been conducted. In this paper, a method for estimating the DOA using machine learning is proposed, and clarify the influence of each hyperparameter on the estimation accuracy.

articleTitle: A Multi-Groove Loaded Rectangular Aperture Horn Antenna for Orthogonal Polarized Elliptical Beam
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We have proposed a rectangular aperture horn antenna with low crossed polarization and orthogonal polarization which has the same beam shape. This paper reports on a structure that controls modes independently for each polarization in order to shorten the axial length of rectangular-aperture horn antenna with multi-grooves. The optimization of the structure has been performed to obtain a specified -10 dB beam widths. The axial length of the proposed antenna is about one-half the length of the previously developed horn.

articleTitle: A study on an online acceleration of automatic design of RF-DC conversion circuit using neural networks
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The design method of RF-DC conversion circuits for wireless power transmission is discussed. The extent to which circuit properties can be estimated using convolutional neural networks is discussed in this study. In order to use an automatic design method for circuit design, it is a problem that it takes time for electromagnetic field analysis. It is shown that the proposed method may make it possible to design circuits in a realistic time.

articleTitle: Improved Performance of Microwave Staring Correlated Imaging by Coherent Integration
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The imaging performance of Microwave Staring Correlated Imaging (MSCI) is determined by the property of sensing matrix and the noise condition of the imaging system. In this paper, coherent integration is introduced into MSCI to improve the imaging performance by enhancing signal noise ratio (SNR) with a predetermined sensing matrix. Via coherent integration of target echo and incoherent integration of additive noise, the upper-bound of the imaging error can be reduced according to matrix perturbation theory. Numerical imaging results validate the improvement of imaging performance, indicating a new sensing matrix construction method for MSCI.

articleTitle: Over-The-Air Apparatus for Large-Scale MIMO Antennas to Create the Full-Rank Channel Matrix
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents an Over-The-Air evaluation method for large-scale MIMO antennas to create the full-rank channel matrix. In this proposed method, the scatterers are virtually arranged in such a way that they have the same effect as that of randomly-arranged scatterers. This method allows us to measure the full-rank channel matrix using a limited number of scatterers. This method is useful for assessing a high MIMO channel capacity of large-scale MIMO antenna.

articleTitle: The Trend of Research and Development and International Standardization of Radio Communication Systems using Millimeter-waves in Railway
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In railways, train radio systems have long been introduced as a means of communication between running trains and the ground. However, current train radio systems mainly use voice communication, and the amount of information that can be transmitted are limited. Therefore, researches are being carried out to realize the broadband ground-to-train radio communication using millimeter-waves. This paper reports that the trends of research and development toward the utilization of millimeter-waves in railways, the current status of international standardization activities, and future prospects.

articleTitle: Optical High-Gain Leaky-Wave Antenna by Using a Waffle-Iron Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper describes a comparison of optical leaky-waveguide antennas, i.e., grating waveguide (GWG), waffle waveguide (WWG), and waffle-iron waveguide (WIWG), using both simulations and measurements. We simulate the antenna characteristics and experimentally confirm the high antenna gain.

articleTitle: Collinear Super Turnstile Antennas for 5G Sub-6 Base Station
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In the fifth-generation (5G) wireless communications, due to the advantages such as wide range and low cost, sub-6 frequency band is widely used. It is a challenge to develop the antennas for sub-6 base stations which are wide band, high gain and compact. In this paper, a center-fed collinear antenna array with a compact size is developed based on the super turnstile antenna. The antenna array works at 4.7 GHz, omni radiation pattern is obtained with the average gain of 8 dBi at a wide bandwidth of about 13%.

articleTitle: Localization of Near-field Sources Using Uniform Circular Array and Blind Calibration Method
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper deals with the near-field source localization using a uniform circular array (UCA). The blind array calibration method is also applied to the source localization using UCA with mutual coupling between elements. The computer simulation shows the effectiveness of the calibration in the near-field source localization with UCA.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Hologram with Ultrathin Huygens’ Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Huygens<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">'</sup> metasurfaces, which can tailor both electric and magnetic dipole resonances, have been draw widespread concern. Here, a three-dimensional Huygens' metasurface holographic imaging with enhanced quality is designed whose thickness is only 0.033λ. The presented Huygens<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">'</sup> metasurface hologram may provide inspirations for the design of high-resolution imaging, ultrathin imaging device, security, and data storage.

articleTitle: Hydrodynamic Approach for Deep-nanometer Scale Topologies: Analysis of Metallic Shell
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In order to describe light-matter interaction at deep-nanometer scale, which is governed by nonclassical phenomena, a semiclassical hydrodynamic model with additional boundary conditions has been introduced. This model investigates the motion of the charged gas in metals, characterized by nonlocal material parameters. Based on different treatments of the nonlocality, several hydrodynamic models have been proposed. This work employs the hard wall hydrodynamic model (HW-HDM) and the quantum hydrodynamic model (Q-HDM). The study is performed for the mode structure (natural modes) of a spherical metallic nanoshell, supplemented by the plane wave response of the system. It is shown that the main transverse resonances of HW-HDM and Q-HDM experience nearly identical blueshifts in comparison to the classical resonances. The corresponding longitudinal resonances show noticeable spectrum shifts.

articleTitle: SA antenna-based DOA measurements for LTE base station environments
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This report shows that arrival waves of different base stations can be discriminated by a simple DOA (Direction of Arrival) measurement method based on synthetic aperture (SA) antennas that offers high accuracy. Specifically, demodulation and channel estimation for LTE are added to an existing DOA measurement method. An experiment confirms that the angle and level difference of arrival waves for each base station can be accurately determined.

articleTitle: Radiation Characteristics of Electromagnetically Coupled Embroidered Patch Antennas with Reduced Amount of Conductive Yarn
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper describes the simulated radiation characteristics of electromagnetically coupled embroidered patch antennas with anisotropic conductivities for the radiating patch element. The FDTD simulation was conducted with several anisotropic conductivities for the patch element. Simulated results agree well with the measured results. The additional gain reduction is less than 0.2 dB, even with a 75% reduction of conductive yarn for the patch element. The simulated gain difference between the embroidered antenna with the low stitch density and copper reference antenna was about 3.0 dB and agreed well with the measured result.

articleTitle: Bi-directional Updating Algorithm for ROI and Dielectric Profile in CSI Framework for Microwave Subsurface Imaging
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a bi-directional updating algorithm between radar image and inverse scattering reconstructions, namely, complex permittivity profile, under the contrast source inversion (CSI) scheme, for microwave non-destructive testing scenario. To implement the above scheme, the sequential optimization process of the region of interest (ROI) and dielectric profile is newly introduced in terms of the ROI and dielectric profile buried in concrete media. The FDTD numerical test, assuming typical NDT model, demonstrates that our proposed method considerably updates the reconstruction performance in CSI framework.

articleTitle: ALOS-PALSAR Quad Pol Data and Image Archive for Monitoring the Earth Environment
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Precise monitoring of the earth cover and its historical archive are very important for preserving the healthy earth environment. Since the majority of quad pol data sets acquired with ALOS-PALSAR have been saved unprocessed, National Institute of Advanced Science and Technology have completed full-processing and opened a website on which everyone can search, view and download the global data. These numerous data sets including SLC as well as ortho-rectified scattering power decomposition images can be utilized freely for checking the long-term temporal variation of the land cover. They will serve as a good reference for advanced microwave remote sensing.

articleTitle: Schemes to Reduce No Estimates and Database Update Errors for Finger Print Area Localization
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We are investigating the finger print method using wireless LAN access points (APs) to estimate user location. We focused on the APs coincidence rate (APCR) and database update as a way to prevent the loss of estimation accuracy. The APCR is a method to prevent estimation errors by narrowing down the candidate estimation positions. However, depending on the conditions, there is an issue that causes of no estimates. Updating a database using user-measured data presents the issue of update errors. In this paper, we have proposed and verified these two issues.

articleTitle: Standardization Activities on Foreign Object and Debris Detection System for Airport
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The Foreign Object and Debris (FOD) must be removed to keep the safe operation of airports. Some of FOD Detection Systems (FODDS) are in service. This paper describes the development of international standards for FODDS.

articleTitle: Evaluation of direction of arrival and XPR by hexahedral antennas based on 920-MHz band measured data
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The propagation characteristics in an urban macrocell environment was measured using a hexahedral antenna with V and H polarization on each face as a basic study in an environment where numerous IoT terminals exist in the 5G communication. The direction of arrival was obtained from the 920-MHz propagation data. The polarization characteristics were evaluated by XPR obtained from the received power values of the antennas arranged orthogonally.

articleTitle: Analysis of cluster characteristics in SHF band using ISTA and K-means++ algorithms
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In the super high frequency (SHF) band used in the 5th-generation mobile communication system (5G system), the propagation characteristics are different from those in conventional propagation models, such as i.i.d. Rayleigh fading. Therefore, a new propagation model is necessary to evaluate 5G systems. We previously proposed a propagation model for the SHF band that regards the incoming radio wave mass as a cluster. However, the evaluation of parameters such as the number of clusters are found to be insufficient. Herein, we clarify the cluster characteristics of the SHF band by clustering simulation results and actual measurement results using the iterative shrinkage thresholding algorithm (ISTA) and k-means++ algorithm.

articleTitle: Looking Back on My Past – Finding Assets by Words from Others –
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The author has been engaged in research and development of wireless access protocols and has been contributing to the standardization activities in IEEE802. In this paper, while introducing her field of expertise, she looks back on her past how she got there. Some of her findings may give some hints to young female engineers to think of their career paths.

articleTitle: A reduction of measurement points in cylindrical near field measurement by complex interpolation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a method of reduction of measurement points in cylindrical near field using spline interpolation in complex domain to measure near field in high speed by using multi probe system.

articleTitle: Fading Analysis for BANs in Cylindrical Rooms with Metallic Walls
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A fast fading analysis for Body Area Networks operating at 2.45 GHz in cylindrical rooms with metallic walls is presented in the paper. A model was developed, based on geometrical ray bouncing. By using an empirically validated simulator, it is shown that it is enough to analyse up to 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> order reflections. Additionally, it is shown that the normalised radius (to the wavelength) of the cylindrical room does not have a significant influence on fast fading characteristics. The obtained values for the Rice factor, being negative or very close to 0 dB, show that in this kind of environments fast fading can be characterised by the Rayleigh Distribution.

articleTitle: Frequency Control of a Varactor-Loaded Dual-Band Single-layer Shorted Microstrip Antenna Fed by an L-probe with Reduced Cross Polarization
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a frequency-tunable varactor-loaded dual-band single-layer shorted microstrip antenna (MSA) fed by an L-probe with reduced cross polarization. The proposed antenna consists of two L-shaped patches on both sides of a feeding L-probe arranged on a dielectric substrate. In order to miniaturize the antenna, the two patches with approximately a quarter wavelength in length are shorted at the opposite side to the L-probe with a via hole. A varactor diode is mounted on each shorted patch in the vicinity of the via hole. The resonant frequencies of the two patches can be controlled by the DC bias voltages applied to the varactor diodes independently. In order to reduce cross polarization radiated from the L-shaped patches, a varactor-loaded frequency-tunable dual-band shorted MSA with modified L-shaped patches is proposed. Although the fractional frequency-tunable ranges of the two patches are almost unchanged in comparison with the conventional MSA with L-shaped patches, measured cross-polarization of the proposed MSA with the modified L-shaped patches is improved by around 5 to 10 dB in the broadside direction.

articleTitle: Service Area expansion by Adaptive Array in BRT Communications
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, introduction of Adaptive Array in BRT (Bus Rapid Transmit) Communications where the trial of autonomous driving is examined. As a result of examination, service area is expanded, and the effectiveness of Adaptive Array is demonstrated.

articleTitle: FDTD Analysis of Dipole Antenna on Multilayer Dielectric Slab
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The FDTD method, which is one of the electromagnetic field analysis methods, has a problem that the time step width becomes small and the analysis cost increases due to the CFL condition when an attempt is made to accurately discretize and analyze a structure that is thinner than the wavelength. There is a subcell method as an analysis method for avoiding this problem, but few examples have been analyzed for a thin multilayer medium. Therefore, the purpose of this research is to reduce the cost of the analysis of multi-layer media that is thinner than the wavelength. In this paper, we analyze the effectiveness of this method by analyzing the antenna on a multilayer dielectric slab using the subcell method.

articleTitle: Development of an Antarctic Atmospheric Radar
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We briefly review the system outline and technical developments for the Antarctic atmospheric radar constructed at Syowa Station (69°S, 40°E). The radar has achieved equivalent sensitivity to that of the MU radar in Japan while reducing its power consumption to less than one thirds of that. Newly developed algorithms for adaptive clutter rejection and beam de-broadening are introduced to alleviate difficulties imposed by the environmental and the operational conditions unique to this facility.

articleTitle: Deforestation Detection in Tropical Forests using Scattering Power Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Tropical forests play an important role for healthy Earth environment. Polarimetric Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) has a great potential for forest monitoring because of its penetration capability and retrieval of polarimetric information. This study evaluates the capability of deforestation detection in tropical forests using the six-component scattering power decomposition and quad polarization SAR data. We could clearly distinguish whether an area is a natural forest or not by taking an appropriate window size for ensemble average. The deforestation detection performance achieved an accuracy exceeding the kappa coefficient of 90%.

articleTitle: Uniplanar Broadband Balun Design for Sub-THz Antenna On-Wafer Characterization
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A uniplanar broadband balun is designed on SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Si substrate at sub-THz through this work. The structure is proposed for CPW to CPS transition establishing efficient on-wafer characterization environment for balanced antenna structures over the D-band. The balun is composed of a CPW linearly tapered into CPS and a broadband open termination of one side ground of CPW. The designed structure is analyzed and optimized through HFSS simulation. The designed model showed a bandwidth ratio of 55% at 140 GHz with insertion and return loss of 1 dB and 17 dB respectively. The results of the back-to-back structure are also presented.

articleTitle: Iteration-Free Phase Retrieval Method Using Phaseless Single-Plane Near-Field
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes an iteration-free phase retrieval method using single-plane near-field amplitude distribution. The proposed method numerically creates a two amplitude groups from a single plane amplitude distribution by linear interpolation. The two amplitude groups are related to virtually defined aperture surface using propagation matrices by the field equivalence principle. The phase distribution on the measurement plane is retrieved using the singular vector of the propagation matrix scaled by the two amplitude groups. By the numerical analysis, we indicate that the near-field phase distribution can be accurately reconstructed by the proposed method with the reconstruction error within 10%.

articleTitle: Impact of Signal Correlation in 2D Imaging with Khatri-Rao Product Expansion Array
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The main purpose of our research is to build a security system that checks the possession of dangerous materials using millimeter-wave radar with a small number of elements and observation points, and to realize 3D imaging. As a study to perform high-definition imaging with a small number of antenna elements, we applied virtual array processing of Khatri-Rao (KR) products. However, the virtual array processing of KR products assumes uncorrelated wave incidence in principle [2]. Therefore, in this paper, we showed how the correlation affects 2D imaging by KR processing when the correlation wave arrives. The results show that the imaging quality depends on not only the magnitude of correlation coefficient but also phase of it.

articleTitle: Compact Double-Wing Cavity Gap Waveguide Twist for E-Band Antenna Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Millimeter-wave waveguide twists are needed in 5G antenna systems. Due to the small dimensions at mmWave regime, the manufacture of conventional waveguide twists becomes a big challenge. A new waveguide twist by employing the gap waveguide technology and double-wing cavities is proposed in this paper, which does not require conductive contact between step sections so that the wielding or soldering is avoided. This new technology reduces the number of the steps for the twists significantly with a wide frequency band and a low cost. A prototype of the three-section double-wing cavity gap waveguide 90° twist at E-band is manufactured and measured. The measured results agree well with the simulations.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Shinkansen Antenna for Overhead-Line Voltage Detection and Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The rooftop antenna of the leading car on the Tokaido Shinkansen, which is a high-speed railway line in Japan, has two functions; 1) detection of the overhead-line voltage in 60 Hz and 2) wireless communication in the VHF band. In this paper, we propose a miniaturized antenna configuration to reduce aerodynamic noise caused by the antenna. When the detection rod that detects the overhead-line voltage is shortened, the performance of overhead-line voltage detection deteriorates, but the deterioration is minimized by making the antenna substrate area as large as possible within the antenna radome. Moreover, in the VHF band, the wideband characteristic is attained and the antenna gain becomes higher than the conventional antenna by using a folded monopole structure and a parallel resonant circuit. The effectiveness of the proposed antenna is confirmed by simulations.

articleTitle: Radiation Phase Control of a Single-Layer Ring Microstrip Antenna Fed by an L-Probe with a Variable Reactance Circuit
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a single-layer ring microstrip antenna (MSA) fed by an L-probe with a variable reactance circuit for a beam adjustable microstrip antenna arrays (BA-MSAA). The BA-MSAA consists of a central patch element fed by a feeding line and two parasitic patches with a variable reactance circuit (VRC) adjacent to the center patch. Radiation patterns of the BA-MSAA are controlled electronically by reactance values of the VRCs. In order to enhance the beam-shaping performance of the BA-MSAA, it is necessary to feed the all patches and to control the radiation phases of the fed patches independently. For this purpose, a single-layer ring MSA fed by an L-probe with a VRC is presented in this paper. The prototype MSA with the VRC is designed at 5 GHz. The radiation phase of the prototype MSA can be controlled in the range of about 80 degrees when the normalized reactance of the VRC is varied from -2.0 to 2.0.

articleTitle: Aperture Efficiency Improvement by Reflectionless Metasurfaces for Large-Aperture Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We design an impedance-matched reflectionless metasurface to manipulate the aperture phase of an X-band large-aperture slot array antenna. By proposing a design procedure for large-area metasurfaces in practical applications with preparing a database that relates the propagation characteristics of unit cells with their physical structures, we design a large-area non-periodic reflectionless metasurface consisting of 200×34 unit cells. A gain enhancement due to an aperture efficiency improvement by the metasurface is experimentally demonstrated at 9.41 GHz.

articleTitle: Development of 3D Cross-Layer Simulators
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Propagation characteristics are primarily used as evaluation indices for wireless communication quality. However, the evaluation of solely the propagation characteristics cannot help determine the performance of an entire communication system that entails the upper layer. Further, owing to various limitations, cross-layer evaluation across layers was difficult to realize thus far. Therefore, this paper proposes a three-dimensional cross-layer simulator that can evaluate the performance of a communication system that entails the physical layer. In addition, we confirmed the effectiveness of the performance evaluation in IEEE 802.11g and 11ax using the proposed simulator.

articleTitle: Heartbeat Measurement Results by a VHF-Band Antenna with an Adaptive Matching Control Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Non-contact detection using a Doppler sensor has been studied for heartbeat measurement. However, Doppler sensors are affected by reflected waves from surrounding objects, making accurate acquisition of heartbeats difficult. To solve this problem, we have proposed the heartbeat sensor using of the small loop antenna with low radiation efficiency. When it is placed near subject's heart, the antenna input impedance change according to surroundings. In this paper, we show an adaptive control algorithm of a variable matching circuit according to changes in the surroundings of the antenna. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by measurements for multiple persons.

articleTitle: Non-contact PIM-measurement for Array Antenna using Open-Stub Extension
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method of Non-contact PIM measurement for array antenna by substituting open-stub extension for low-PIM-termination. DUT(Device Under Test) is excited by the PIM tester placed outside and induced PIM is also detected by it. Since null of the current standing wave should be avoided, it is recommended that tests with open-stubs should be carried out. 2-element array antenna is considered as DUT with PIM source in one element. Under above condition, we propose method that requires only one stub with a certain length. Quarter-wavelength stub is practical in the proposed non-contact PIM-measurement method.

articleTitle: Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) Calculations in the Abdomen of the Human Body Caused by Smartphone at Various Tilt Angles
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recently, various electromagnetic (EM) applications have become common, and humans are frequently exposed to EM waves. Therefore, the effect of EM waves on the human body should be evaluated. In this study, we focused on the specific absorption rate (SAR) due to the EM waves emitted from a smartphone, developed high-resolution numerical smartphone models, and calculated SARs under various conditions.

articleTitle: Radio Frequency Interference Detection for Multi-Receiver Synthetic Aperture Radar Based on Interferometric Analysis of Raw Data
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We propose a novel radio frequency interference (RFI) detection method for multi-receiver SAR systems. Some RFIs are difficult to be distinguished from the scattered radar echoes and thus, the focused SAR image contains some colored noise derived from RFI. Some SAR platforms apply a multi-receiver SAR system. In such a system, RFI signal is kept identical between the receivers while the ideal signals are non-identical because they are the summation of thousands of backscattered echoes. We developed an interferometric analysis method for separating RFI polluted bands from the SAR raw data based on the idea above.

articleTitle: Observation of the UHF Television Duct over the Japan Sea
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In Ishikawa of Japan, terrestrial UHF television (TV) broadcasting waves are sometimes received between spring and the early fall from Korea and Shimane of Japan far from the horizon. We have observed these wave intensities since May 2007 at Tsubata in Ishikawa. This abnormal propagation seems to be the duct propagation to be caused by several climatic conditions, that is, sunshine hour, air temperature, sea surface temperature and air pressure. In this paper, we show outline of the observation, and show climatic conditions on the duct occurrence from the observation for 10 years from 2008 to 2017.

articleTitle: Flexible Views without Being Held Back by Fixed Ideas is the Mother of Invention
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Flexible Views are most important way of thinking. If you do not forget it, you can challenge anything developing not only technologies but also societies at Antenna and Propagation. Why do you need to think about the sex and age of people who invented excellent technologies? Quality of technologies is an only thing you need to pay attention. In this paper, I would like to discuss the importance of the flexible view based on my experiences as a woman in engineering and my knowledge about design of planar antenna at millimeter waves.

articleTitle: Radio environment measurement over the urban area for UAV communications
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper describes the UAV airspace's radio environment's evaluation results in the 920MHz and 2.4GHz band at the urban and the bay area. The radio environment measurement has been set up at a multistory building in Tokyo's metropolitan area (Shinjuku) and a giant Ferris Wheel in the bay area. The measurement results show that the urban area radio environment was distinct from the bay area. Especially, the CDF of 2.4 GHz band shows time-dependent at Shinjuku Building. This result found that Wireless LAN use is a significant factor in the 2.4 GHz band.

articleTitle: New Gap Capacitive Structure for Broadening Left-handed Region in Composite Right/Left Handed Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes composed right/left-handed transmission lines (CRLH-TL) having new capacitive gaps introducing many projections in an interdigital-capacitor part for broadening the left-handed region. As a result, it is made clear from the numerical investigation that the CRLH-TL with the proposed interdigital capacitive gap succeeds to have broad bandwidth in the left handed region.

articleTitle: Analysis of Incoming Wave Characteristics for V2V Communication in an Urban Environment
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We are currently developing a 4 × 4 multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna system for ad-hoc connected car applications. To evaluate the proposed MIMO antenna, we performed a ray tracing simulation of a radio propagation environment for vehicle-to-vehicle communication in an urban environment. The results revealed that the 4 × 4 MIMO channel capacity based on the characteristics of the analyzed radio propagation environment varies depending on the SNR.

articleTitle: Implementation of Beamforming a Circularly Polarized Radiation Pattern on 3D Random Arrays
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, a circularly polarized beamforming technique is demonstrated on 3D random arrays to preliminarily emulate a wireless phased array morphing in the air. Sixteen linearly polarized patch antennas acted as swarming radiators, and each antenna was positioned randomly in a 3D volume. The experiment was conducted in an anechoic chamber to alleviate multipath effects, and the measured results were benchmarked using simulations to verify the fidelity of the beamforming algorithm.

articleTitle: N-type Metacurl Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An N-type metacurl antenna, which is composed of circularly polarized n-type cells, is presented. The radiation mechanism is qualitatively analyzed using electric current bands. It is found that the gain for a left-handed circularly polarized wave reaches a maximum value at a frequency where the propagation phase constant is negative; however, the gain for a right-handed circularly polarized wave becomes zero at a frequency where the propagation phase constant is positive. Quantitative analysis using a finite integral method confirms this fact and reveals other antenna characteristics.

articleTitle: Frequency-Dependent FDTD Analyses of Terahertz Plasmonic Devices
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The properties of surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) have recently been utilized even at terahertz (THz) frequencies. In this article, the frequency-dependent finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method is applied to the analysis of terahertz plasmonic devices. We first mention the modeling of an InSb material that can support SPPs and present the FDTD equation based on the simple trapezoidal recursive convolution (TRC) technique. Next, the TRC-FDTD method is applied to investigating a waveguide-based TM-pass polarizer with InSb layers. Numerical results show that an extinction ratio of 30 dB is obtained with a device length of less than 500 μm.

articleTitle: Two-dimensional ARMA for FDTD Radiation Pattern Analysis
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method has been widely employed for analyzing various electromagnetic problems, including low-frequency problems. It provides accurate results in most cases, however, relatively long calculation time is required for slow convergence problems, such as array antennas. For this reason, the autoregressive moving average (ARMA) model has been applied to FDTD radiation pattern analysis because the radiation patterns calculation requires multi-dimensional (time and space) data. In this paper, we applied two-dimensional ARMA to FDTD radiation pattern analysis to reduce the calculation time. We confirm effectiveness of the method by calculating the radiation pattern of Yagi-Uda antenna.

articleTitle: Angle-insensitive Bifunctional Resonator Based on Periodic Structure
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An angle-insensitive bifunctional resonator composed of a compound silver grating is proposed. The resonator exhibits different response characteristics for TE and TM polarization, thus enabling two functions, corresponding to high-sensitivity sensor and low Q-factor absorber. For TE polarization, the Q-factor, refractive index sensitivity, and figure of merit of the resonator can reach 283.4, 2577.6 nm/RIU, and 181.5 RIU-1, respectively, due to the excitation of cavity mode resonance. For TM polarization, the resonator can be regarded as an absorber with high absorptivity (> 97%) based on magnetic resonance. This simple structure provides a good paradigm for designing high-performance multi-functional devices.

articleTitle: Study on Forward Transient Scattering by a Metal Cylinder Covered with a Homogeneous Medium
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We calculate forward transient scattering by a metal cylinder covered with a homogeneous medium (coated metal cylinder). A time-domain asymptotic-numerical solution (TD-ANS) is used for computations in a forward transient scattered electric field by a coated metal cylinder. An analysis method using the TD-ANS provides a basis of nondestructive testing for corrosion degree of rebar in steel reinforced concrete structures. We confirm the validity of the TD-ANS by comparing with a reference solution. We also discuss an interpretation method of the forward transient scattered electric field using the TD-ANS.

articleTitle: A Single-Layer ± 45° Dual-Polarized Array Antenna Based on Phase Control Approach
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A single-layer ± 45° dual-polarized directional array antenna based on phase control approach for millimeter-wave applications is proposed in this paper. Based on the series-fed dual circularly polarized array, the ± 45° polarized radiation is achieved by exciting the two ports of the array simultaneously and adjusting the feeding phase difference of the two ports. Since the two ports of the series-fed array are excited simultaneously, the beam direction of the array does not deflect with frequency changes. In addition, the entire antenna array is printed on a single-layer substrate. The array achieves dual-polarized radiation from 29.5 to 30.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Frequency Domain Iterative Cancellation of Periodic Noise
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes frequency domain iterative cancellation for suppressing a periodic noise. The proposed cancellation alleviates a periodic noise in the desired frequency band by using an interference canceller with a replica of the noise. The proposed iterative canceller achieves superior replica estimation even when the signals in all the frequency bands are collapsed by the periodic noise. The performance of the proposed iterative cancellation is evaluated in terms of the signal power to noise power ratio(SNR) by computer simulations. The proposed cancellation obtains a gain of 25 dB even when the carrier power to noise power ratio(CNR) is about 0 dB by iterating the cancellation 2 times, while the no-iterative cancellation achieves only a gain of 4 dB.

articleTitle: Circularly Symmetric Photonic Bandgap Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel photonic bandgap (PBG) antenna with a circularly symmetric structure is proposed, and analyzed using the body-of-revolution FDTD method. The PBG antenna is composed of a stack of dielectric layers and is fed from a cylindrical metallic waveguide. A gain of 32.8 dB is obtained with an aperture efficiency of 48.3%.

articleTitle: Reflectarray Antenna Changing Beam Direction by Polarization
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Reflectarray antenna applies the reflection phase control function of a metal loaded frequency selective reflector (FSR) to the reflector antenna. If the shape and arrangement of the elements are appropriately designed, it is possible to control the reflection phases of vertical (V) and horizontal (H) polarization with a single reflectarray. In this report, a highly accurate reflectarray is investigated that uses three linear elements. The results of the analysis demonstrate that the mutual coupling between the H and V components reduces and the effect of manufacturing error is minimized. Consequently, it is inferred that the beam could be emitted in different directions for each polarization.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Enhancement of a Folded Monopole Antenna with an Iron Tower
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper discusses bandwidth enhancement of a folded monopole antenna using an iron tower (FMAIT). First, the impedance of the FMAIT with one wire is analyzed by electromagnetic (EM) and circuit simulations. It is shown that the bandwidth can be expanded by reducing the step-up ratio in an equivalent circuit of the FMAIT. Then, the FMAIT with three driven-wires is proposed to reduce the step-up ratio. It is verified by EM simulation that the bandwidth enhancement can be achieved by separating wires from each other.

articleTitle: Dual-polarized Antenna Loaded with Ferrite Cores for Decoupling in Multi-band Multi-array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel method of suppressing the resonant coupling in multi-band multi-array antennas is proposed. It is proved by a dual-band dual-polarized antenna array which is configured as a lower-band (LB) element operating from 690 to 960 MHz and two columns of HB elements operating from 1690 to 2690 MHz. The proposed method is achieved by loading ferrite cores on the cables of the higher-band (HB) elements. With the ferrite cores, the LB common-mode currents distributed on the cables of HB elements are eliminated, and then the distorted LB radiation patterns are evidently restored.

articleTitle: TOF Estimation of Multipath Waves Using PN Correlation Method with M-FOCUSS
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper applies M-FOCUSS, which is a method of compressed sensing technologies, to the delay profile of multipath waves obtained by the PN correlation method with multi-antenna system. The computer simulation using the proposed method demonstrates the improvement of TOF estimation accuracy and separation performance of the multipath waves.

articleTitle: 300 GHz link enabled by Yagi-Uda antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the use of a Yagi-Uda antenna on polymer substrate for 300 GHz data communications. The antenna is described and characterized in terms of radiation pattern in the 300 GHz band. Then, it is used and validated within a communication link. Using amplitude shift keying modulation at 10 Gbps and without any signal post-processing nor off-line detection, error-free performance is achieved.

articleTitle: Design of the radio fence of the EISCAT_3D radar for human safety using Method of Moment and Geometrical Theory of Diffraction
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The current status is reported about the design work on the radio fence around the transmitting site of the EISCAT_3D radar for human safety. The Method of Moment (MoM) is used to compute the current distribution on antenna elements and near electric field strength outside of the fence. Techniques to reduce computation costs are explained with initial results, followed by the future plan to combine the MoM and Geometrical Theory of Diffraction for simulations on very large models that contain the whole antenna array and fence.

articleTitle: Study of FDD downlink beamforming method suitable for WPT in real environment
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The wireless power transmission (WPT) system realizes high power supply in the microwave band. The WPT system needs a function to transmit power while detecting and avoiding other systems (W-LAN) which uses adjacent transmitting channels. In this paper, we propose a method to detect other systems using 802.11ac based preamble signals assuming W-LAN. We measure signals in an actual indoor environment, and performance computer simulations using the propagation channels using the W-LAN system. The effect of the proposed method in the real environment is verified.

articleTitle: Mode Group Selection Method for Inter-mode Interference Suppression in OAM Multiplexing
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a mode group selection method for orbital angular momentum (OAM) multiplexing to suppress inter-mode interference (IMI) owing to the misalignment of the beam axis. We have proposed an IMI suppression method employing even-numbered OAM modes, and its effectiveness has been successfully confirmed. Odd-numbered OAM modes are robust and used in addition to even-numbered modes to improve the robustness against the IMI, and the appropriate mode group is selected based on the system capacity. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated in terms of system capacity via computer simulations.

articleTitle: Near-field Aperture Distribution Measurement of 8×2-element 60-GHz-Band Circularly Polarized Post-Wall Waveguide Dipole Loaded Slot Arrays
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An 8×2-element 60-GHz-band circularly polarized post-wall waveguide dipole loaded slot array has been characterized by near-field antenna measurement. The antenna is composed of two substrate layers and one has feeding waveguides and slots and the other has dipole arrays. This antenna is fabricated by printed circuit technology. The near-field antenna measurement shows that the non-uniform amplitude and phase distribution decrease directivity and bandwidth of the directivity.

articleTitle: Far field estimation by current distribution reconstruction from 5-sided box near field
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents how to reconstruct the current distribution of the antenna using a near field of the 5-sided box. It is difficult to measure the phase of the near field in the high frequency band. The proposed method is an inverse problem using near field amplitude and can estimate the far field accurately, by using initial phase information. The information is determined by phase delay due to the distance between the feeding point and measurement point, considering antiphase of z plane of the box.

articleTitle: Novel Broadband Corrugated Lens Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recently the wireless surveillance system has been regarded highly. In order to realize the sensitive wireless surveillance system, its antenna has to perform the broadband and high gain characteristics. As the simple method, it can be realized to combine the parabolic reflector and the broadband primary antenna which has the wide and constant beam width through the wide frequency band. This time, we have tried to develop the broadband and wide beam width antennas composed of the corrugated lens and the ridged antenna as the primary antenna for the parabolic reflector. This paper introduces its configuration and the good simulated results as follows.

articleTitle: Highly-Integrated Pattern Switchable MIMO Antennas for 5G Notebook Computer Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Highly-integrated 2-port MIMO antennas with variable radiation patterns for 5G notebook computer applications are presented. It is demonstrated that switchable and diverse radiation patterns for conjoined dual coupled-fed loop antennas can be achieved successfully by properly designing parasitical and switch-integrated current-dragging resonant structures. The proposed MIMO antennas are expected to have higher adaptive capability within different practical multipath channel environments.

articleTitle: Theoretical error analysis on geolocation unknown emitters using TDOA of three geostationary satellites
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In satellite communication, there is a severe problem of interference from unknown emitters to the geostationary satellites. This problem is called uplink interference. We consider the problem of geolocation method based on time difference of arrival (TDOA) between 3 adjacent geostationary satellites. In this paper, we derive theoretical error equation, and then clarify the relationship between the location of the target and the geolocation accuracy.

articleTitle: General Chair's Welcome Message
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Presents the introductory welcome message from the conference proceedings. May include the conference officers' congratulations to all involved with the conference event and publication of the proceedings record.

articleTitle: Program at a Glance
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Provides a schedule of conference events and a listing of which papers were presented in each session.

articleTitle: Author Index
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Presents an index of the authors whose articles are published in the conference proceedings record.

articleTitle: Directive Antenna Design at 2.4 GHz on Foot Surface for Wanderer Location Identification
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A directional patch array antenna was designed for wanderer location identification. The antenna was used for foot-mounted BLE beacons at 2.4 GHz band. Its directional performance was evaluated by simulation and it was found that the antenna can sweep diagonally upward from 7° to 35°.

articleTitle: A Broadband Dual-Slant Polarized Metal Vivaldi Antenna for a High-Power Jammer
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a dual-slant polarization metal Vivaldi antenna with a broadband characteristic for a high-power jammer application. The single element of the proposed antenna consists of radiating flares and feeding cavity parts. This single element is then extended to a periodic structure slanted with 45° for a dual-polarization property. For the periodic structure, the VSWR values are under 1.6 from 2 GHz to 6 GHz. In addition, the bore-sight gains of the periodic structure are over -2.5 dBi in the entire operating frequency band. Then, we expand the proposed antenna to a dual-slant polarized 8×8 array antenna.

articleTitle: Orthogonal-Polarization-Reuse-Antenna (OPRA) Evaluation at Cellular Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We investigated the performance of Orthogonal Polarization Reuse Antenna (OPAR) in a cellular LOS environment. OPAR is a technology that reuses multiple orthogonal polarization in the space domain. OPRA's average channel capacity increases by about 30% compared to 3-sector dual-polarization antenna. We confirmed that the use of OPAR increase the channel capacity by mitigating interference in overlapped zorn compare to 3-sector with a dual-polarization antenna.

articleTitle: Direction Finding by Time-Modulated Circular Array with Amplitude Comparison
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a novel direction finding method using the power spectrum characteristics in parallel with the amplitude comparison is proposed in time-modulated circular array (TMCA). The direction of arrival (DoA) of the incident signal in azimuthal angular range of 360° is estimated by the TMCA with high accuracy. In addition, angular ambiguity is reduced through the amplitude comparison without additional hardware. As a result of the direction finding performance by proposed method is provided with a four-element TMCA.

articleTitle: Leaf-Shaped Bowtie Slot Antenna Array for Application in Beam Scanning
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a circular 4×4 Butler Matrix based on microstrip line is designed and applied to a 4-element linear array of leaf-shaped bowtie slot antenna. This antenna structure is designed to operate within 27GHz to 29GHz. The circular butler matrix is used in order to eliminate crossover element. On the top of antenna array, a dielectric superstrate with high dielectric constant is used to improve impedance bandwidth and gain. Those antenna characteristics are evaluated by using Finite Different Time Domain (FDTD) method. From the simulated results, -10dB impedance bandwidth is within 27GHz to 28.5GHz and the antenna can scan the beam within 9° to -13° along E-plane.

articleTitle: Balanced Non-contact Connector for PIM Measurement
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A non-contact connector for a balanced PIM measurement system is proposed. This paper shows that proposed connector operates at three frequencies in PIM band and whose frequencies are able to be tuned independently.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on Dual-Band Differential Rectenna with Stacked Antenna Configuration
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a novel dual-band differential rectenna is proposed and its performance is experimentally evaluated. The proposed rectenna has a simple structure in which 2.45- and 5.8-GHz band microstrip antennas are stacked. The conversion efficiency under 0.29-W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> power density was 63.6% and 31.1% at 2.5 and 5.95 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Prediction of 28 GHz Propagation Characteristics in an Indoor Office Environment Based on Large-scale Computer Simulations
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper predicts 28 GHz millimeter-wave propagation characteristics in an indoor office environment using large-scale numerical simulations based on the FDTD technique. Analyzing the path loss model parameters, it is confirmed that many reflections from the walls and furniture appear in the indoor environment. Additionally, comparing the electric field distributions with the path loss characteristics in some areas of the room, it is shown that the both agree mostly with each other although the unique distributions of electric field differing from the path loss model are caused by the interactions between the direct wave and the multipath waves in the limited areas near the TX antenna, the walls and furniture.

articleTitle: Development of Advanced HTS Onboard Ka-band Antennas for Engineering Test Satellite 9
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We have developed the advanced onboard antennas for High Throughput Satellite (HTS). They are three types of the antennas utilizing Ka-band frequencies to aim in-orbit verification by the Japanese Engineering Test Satellite 9 (ETS-9). First antenna is the fixed multi-beam antenna (Fixed MBA) employing the miniaturized and integrated feeder unit to enable dense allocation of multi beams for improvement of spectrum efficiency. Second antenna is the Digital Beam Forming antenna (DBF-ANT) to enable flexible beam shape. Third antenna is the common communications system antenna (CCS-ANT) transmitting broad beam which has beacon transmission function etc.

articleTitle: Observations on Near-Field Evaluation of 5G Signal Quality
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: 4G and earlier base stations have been tested by direct-wire connection from the antenna connector to the measuring instrument. OTA measurements are being introduced for 5G, especially FR2, due to the increased number of antennas. There are higher expectations for near-field measurement (NFM) than far-field measurement (FFM) due to its advantages, such as smaller footprint and lower propagation losses. This paper demonstrates the possibility of measuring both power and EVM performance using NFM.

articleTitle: 4×4 Magneto-Electric Dipole Array with Single-Layer Corporate-Feed Ridge Gap Waveguide for mmWave Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents simulations results of a 4×4 magneto-electric dipole (MED) array antenna fed by a single- layer corporate-feed ridge gap waveguide (RGW) for millimeter wave applications. The designed antenna model consists of two unconnected metal layers: the top radiating layer and the bottom corporate-feed RGW layer. Hence, the antenna profile can be lowered since no intermediate cavity layer is required. The MED radiating element shows a larger impedance bandwidth compared to the conventional single layer array antenna. The S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> ≤ -10 dB bandwidth of the simulated antenna is from 24 - 29 GHz, resulting in a 18.9% impedance bandwidth. The realized antenna gain is greater than approximately 19.6 dBi.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Semicircular Disc Patch Antenna Designed with Sector-Shaped Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A miniaturized semicircular disc patch antenna is designed which is loaded with sector-shaped mushroom metamaterials. Full wave simulations reveal that a semicircular disc patch with size of 0.234λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> ×0.117λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> enables the antenna to resonate at 3.511GHz. The antenna bandwidth is 2.3% and the peak gain is about 5.6dBi. The proposed miniaturized semicircular disc patch antenna can meet the needs of 5G mobile communications at 3.5GHz band.

articleTitle: Millimeter Wave Microstrip Antenna with CSRR for 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper describes the comparison between microstrip antenna and microstrip antenna with CSRR for millimeter wave application. The proposed approach utilized 3 different structures which are a single element, 1×8 array, and 4×4 array. CSRR is applied to the design to increase the number of radiating frequencies. The main advantages of the proposed method are the compact size of the antenna, reduced size, and dual band performance from the antennas. From the simulation work, it is discovered that antennas with CSRR structure has dual band performance and reduced size of antenna patch and substrate.

articleTitle: A Reflection-Type Phase Shifter Using Quasi-Transmission-Line Variable Reactors and Impedance Transforming Hybrid Coupler
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a reflection type phase shifter composed of quasi-transmission-line variable reactors and an impedance transforming hybrid coupler. We clarify how the low loss variation and the wide-relative phase shift is obtained by adjusting the parameters of these parts. Calculation results reveal that there is the trend that the characteristic impedance of the coupler and the electrical length of the transmission line are small values for the low loss variation and the wide-relative phase shift, respectively.

articleTitle: Design Multi-band of LTE-Advanced Antenna with Multi-coupling Path Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The proposed multi-band of LTE (long term evolution) -Advanced Pro antenna by 4-resonant path consists of multi band folding and two non-feeding elements at 800MHz, 2.1GHz, 1.7GHz and 700MHz. The experimental achieves LTE-A Pro target efficiency and gain after optimized parameters, cabling loss, cabling length and multi-coupling path for US (United States) band and EU (European Union) band for laptop PC and mobile device applications.

articleTitle: Bent loop Inverted F antenna for TWS Bluetooth earphones
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, bent loop Inverted F antenna (IFA) for True Wireless Stereo (TWS) Bluetooth (BT) earphones is proposed. The proposed antenna is made by loop IFA shape to satisfy BT bandwidth. The bandwidth of BT is 83.5MHz, and proposed antenna's bandwidth is 84.5 MHz in S11<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6dB</sub>. To meet center frequency for BT, the proposed antenna is the bent loop shape. The center frequency is 2.45GHz (BT band). Proposed antenna shows sufficient bandwidth for BT.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Dual-Polarized MIMO Antenna for 700 MHz and Sub-6 GHz 5G Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a dual-band dual-polarized MIMO antenna for 5G systems. To perform this study, a dual-band two-port antenna is designed for operation in 700 MHz (lower band, LB) and between 2.0 and 4.0 GHz (upper band, UB). The UB radiator consists of two crossed double-loop dipoles and the LB bent-dipole element is connected outside the UB element. Simulated and measured results show that the bandwidths of 16% (0.69-0.81 GHz) and 67% (2.0-4.0 GHz), with isolation better than 20 dB, without the additional decoupling structure. The proposed antenna is a good candidate for 5G indoor base station antenna.

articleTitle: Simulation Results of Satellite AIS when Utilizing Khatri-Rao (KR) Product Array Processing
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Future ship detection by satellite will require the provision of more value-added observations in addition to constellation services. Such SAT-SAR missions as ALOS-2 have the satellite AIS. These sub missions need to be more sophisticated within limited constraints. This paper describes KR product array processing to digital beam forming (DBF) using a sparse array AIS antenna.
