It also presents the highperformance of a ship's signal detection with simulated signal collision using a ship position model.

articleTitle: Examination of behavior estimation by MIMO sensor that can respond to the difference in distance
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, machine learning using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is applied to a radio wave sensor that utilizes the time correlation of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) propagation channel fluctuations, and the basic characteristics of different behavior estimation are shown. Furthermore, the effectiveness of MIMO sensors with vertical arrays is shown.

articleTitle: Improvement of Transmission Efficiency by using Annular Array Metamaterial for Magnetic Coupling Wireless Power Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recently, the magnetic coupling wireless power transfer technology has been attracting a lot of attention and is expected to have a wide range of applications in the electrical equipment around us. On the other hand, there have been reports on the application of metamaterials for the purpose of improving antenna gain and suppressing mutual coupling between antennas, and this study aim applying this technique to the magnetic coupling wireless power transfer system. In this paper, a magnetic wall by meta material suitable for a magnetic coupling wireless transfer system is proposed and its effect is demonstrated experimentally.

articleTitle: Service Area Expansion by Polarization MIMO Gap-filler in Terrestrial TV Broadcasting
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, effects of the relay station install location and the retransmission beam width on the service area expansion performance of a polarized MIMO gap-filler in a terrestrial broadcasting environment is examined. Numerical results show that the distribution of buildings is important to design the relay station parameter.

articleTitle: Ground Reflection Power Measurements of Thin High-Voltage Power Lines Using 76 GHz Helicopter Forward-Looking Low-Transmitting Power Millimeter-Wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The reflection power from 12.6 mm diameter high-voltage power lines located between two islands was evaluated using a 76 GHz helicopter forward-looking low transmitting power millimeter-wave radar. Firstly, the specifications of the radar system are discussed. Then, reflection power measurements are carried out with a distance of 370 m between the radar and the high-voltage power lines. Both the specular reflection and Bragg scattering are measured with different incident angles. In addition, it is confirmed that a maximum 30 dB signal-to-noise ratio is obtained.

articleTitle: Study of 21-GHz-band Rain Attenuation Based on Annual Observations of Broadcasting Satellite Signals
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We have been conducting research and development of 21-GHz-band satellite broadcasting using the BSAT-4a broadcasting satellite. We have studied the rain attenuation characteristics of the 21-GHz band using annual observations of signals from the BSAT-4a at Tokyo, Japan. We discuss the differences between the measurements and the predictions of the ITU-R model with a measured rainfall rate.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable T-shaped Slot Antenna Using Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a circular polarization (CP) reconfigurable T-shaped slot antenna. Characteristic mode analysis (CMA) is carried out to understand the physical mechanism of a stand-alone T-shaped conductor laminate, from which modal current distribution over the conducting plane suggests how the circular polarization can be fulfilled. Furthermore, by using a pair of PIN diodes, the antenna is capable of switching its polarization from right hand circular polarization (RHCP) to left hand circular polarization (LHCP) and vice versa. The antenna targets at the 2.4-GHz band. The simulated overlapped -10-dB reflection coefficient and 3-dB axial-ratio bandwidths is 4.5%.

articleTitle: Impact of Wall Blockage on LOS User Association Strategy in Indoor Small Cell Networks
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Interior wall blockage affects the performance of indoor cellular networks but has not been sufficiently studied. In this paper, by incorporating the attenuation caused by wall blockages into to the path loss model, we develop a tractable approach to analyse the performance of indoor cellular networks under the influence of interior wall blockages. Then, the proposed analytical approach is applied to study the downlink coverage probability of line-of-sight (LOS) user association strategy. The analytical results are validated by Monte Carlo simulations in comparison with those obtained under the existing wall blockage model that assumes impenetrable walls.

articleTitle: Near-Field Test Challenges of High Frequency Digital Phased Array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A hemispherical near-field test system that allows for the AUT to remain stationary is described. Typical structural test data is presented to illustrate the applicability of this type of test system for high frequency (mmWave) cases. Digital data rates for a typical AUT are also presented and it is shown to become restrictive in terms of the maximum throughput achievable during testing.

articleTitle: Novel Simulation Approach to Microstrip Antenna Integrated with Nonlinear Circuit
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this study, a new simulation method is applied to microstrip antennas integrating nonlinear devices. The simulation method is a combination of electromagnetic simulation and harmonic-balance circuit simulation. In this simulation, far field characteristics of the antenna can be obtained. A multiplier integrated circularly polarized microstrip antenna is analyzed as an example and the effect of the proposed method is highlighted.

articleTitle: The Analysis of the Octave-Band Self-Complementary Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We investigate antennas that could use enough bandwidth to achieve high resolution in FMCW radar. In analyzing the antenna, we first analyzed it with GAP feeding structure by Finite Element Method. This antenna is self-complementary which is designed for wide bandwidth. The design frequency band is 40.0-80.0 GHz, and the analysis center frequency is 60.0 GHz. The reflection characteristics (S11) could be suppressed to approximately -10 dB or less. Furthermore, we success the bore-sight beam gain suppressing to ± 0.83dBi at design frequency band between 40 to 80GHz.

articleTitle: Improved Drone Detection in FMCW Radar using SPC Technique (invited talk)
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces the stationary point concentration (SPC) technique, one of the state-of-the-art techniques for detecting small drones with frequency modulated continuous wave radars. A novel approach of the SPC technique is explained, and representative experimental results are shown. Finally, the promising potentials of the SPC technique are discussed.

articleTitle: Design of a Dual-band Shared-aperture Radar Array Using Printed Dual-loop Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a shared-aperture S/X dual-band radar array using printed dual-loop antennas. The proposed array consists of one S-band element and nine X-band elements, where the coupled-fed dual-loop structure is applied for broadband matching characteristics. The proposed X and S array elements are then stacked to share a limited size aperture. Thicknesses of all layers including the air gap are optimized so that the S-band element has electromagnetic (EM) transparent characteristics in the X-band. To verify the feasibility of the proposed array, the reflection coefficient and bore-sight gain are investigated in the S/X-band.

articleTitle: Accurate Estimation of Analog Circuit Parameters by CMA-ES Method
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a method to accurately estimate analog circuit parameters from observed amplitude characteristics. In analog circuits, it is not always possible to obtain the expected characteristics due to the existence of errors between the design value and the actual value of circuit parameters. It requires a huge amount of resources to measure all the actual values of those parameters. We propose a method to accurately estimate those values using the Covariance Matrix Adaptive Evolution Strategy (CMA-ES), and evaluate its performance in comparison with some other methods.

articleTitle: Dual-band Coplanar SSPP Endfire Radiating Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band coplanar SSPP antenna is reported. This antenna shows end fire radiation at the two resonant frequencies viz. 5.38 GHz and 6.23 GHz. The efficiency of the antenna is observed to be more than 80% for both frequency bands. The gain of the antenna is approximately 2.8 dBi for 5.38 GHz and 4.8 dBi for 6.23 GHz. Antenna gain at the 6.23 GHz is enhanced by employing I-shaped resonators. The characteristic mode analysis of the SSPP antenna is also carried out and reported here for the first time.

articleTitle: A Filter-Technique Aided Design of 60-GHz Band Planar Single-feed Dual-polarized Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A new dual-polarized microstrip antenna fed by a resonator-integrated feeding network is proposed for millimeter-wave wireless harness application. The dual-polarized radiation is provided by two orthogonally arranged antennas, so the radiation Q factor can be controlled for bandwidth design. Furthermore, a specified bandwidth is achieved by tap-line couplings between resonators and antenna, of which the design is aided by a filter technique. Thus, a high-profile structure and small-gap couplings employed in conventional works are not needed in the proposed antenna. A 60-GHz band dual-polarized antenna with 3-GHz bandwidth are designed and tested, thereby showing the effectiveness of the proposed structure.

articleTitle: Electrically Small Huygens Dipole Array for 5G Wireless Power Transfer Enabled IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A 1 × 4 antenna array facilitated by an innovative electrically small Huygens dipole element is reported. The entire array is ultra-thin, being realized on a single PCB substrate. Each of the Huygens linearly-polarized (HLP) dipole elements is the result of a careful integration of one pair of metamaterial-inspired electrically small structures, i.e., an Egyptian axe dipole (EAD) and a capacitively loaded loop (CLL) near-field resonant parasitic (NFRP) element. The EAD acts as the electric dipole radiator; the CLL works as the magnetic dipole radiator. They are oriented orthogonal to each other and are in-phase to radiate identical cardioid-shaped Huygens patterns in both the E- and H-planes. The consequent 1 × 4 Huygens array operates at 2.45 GHz with a high 8.9 dBi peak realized gain. It has a narrow E-plane 3-dB beamwidth, 28°, and a very broad H-plane beamwidth, 153°. The developed linear HLP-based array is particularly useful for far-field wireless power transfer (WPT) enabled IoT applications that require broad area coverage.

articleTitle: 10-Gbit/s Data Transmission over Dielectric Sheet for 120-GHz-band Sheet LAN
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We investigated 120-GHz-band sheet LAN that enables the connection to LAN simply by placing portable devices on the sheet and can achieve 10-Gbit/s data transmission. We designed dielectric sheets and waveguide-to-dielectric sheet transition, and evaluated their transmission losses. The transmission loss over 100-mm-long dielectric sheet was about -6 dB at the 120 GHz band. We have succeeded in 10-Gbit/s data transmission over the dielectric sheet using 120-GHz wireless signal.

articleTitle: A 2-layer 45° -Slant-Polarised Phased Array Antenna with Baffles Based on Gap Waveguide Technology for mmWave 5G Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A 45° slant-polarised gap waveguide phased array antenna designed with focus on mmWave 5G is presented. Baffles are used to reduce grating lobes. The total efficiency of the array is greater than -0.7 dB, and the average broadside gain is 24.2 dBi in the band from 26.5-29.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of High-Isolation Fragment-Type 5G Base Station Antennas with MOEA/D-GO
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A simple base station antenna is proposed by using two bow-tie dipoles orthogonally printed on different sides of PCB and fed with straight coaxial cables. High isolation and return loss are enhanced by optimization searching for the best distribution of fragment-type structures. A simple scheme for joint optimization is applied by introducing a compound design matrix for MOEA/D-GO, which describes both the fragment-type and the key canonical structures in one design matrix. For demonstration, an antenna is designed for China's 5G band of 3.3-3.6 GHz, which achieves return loss of 20 dB and isolation of 40 dB.

articleTitle: Ray-Tracing Analysis of 60 GHz Band Propagation in Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In the future, the importance of in-vehicle sensors will increase. The usage of wireless communications is considered to save the number of electric wires for connecting the sensors. In this paper, we show ray-tracing simulation and experimental measurement in passenger vehicle. From the comparison between simulation and measurement, it was seen that the angular path loss distributions were very similar even if the path loss of the reflected paths in measurement were about 20 dB or more larger than those of the corresponding paths in the simulation.

articleTitle: A design of dual-band dipole antenna with reflector and FSR using genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A 2 GHz / 3.5 GHz dual-band vertically polarized dipole antenna equipped a reflector and frequency selective reflector (FSR) is considered in this study. The problem to design the antenna is that there are many structural parameters for designing the antenna. This paper reports the results of finding the structural parameters that satisfy the antenna performance required for mobile base station antennas by applying a genetic algorithm.

articleTitle: Equation for Estimation of Radio Link Budget for NMHA in Human Fat Tissue Phantom
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recently, Wireless Capsule Endoscopy (WCE) is used widely in human body medical diagnosis. Normal Mode Helical Antenna (NMHA) is suitable as the antenna for this application because of its small size and high efficiency. In this paper, NMHA performance inside a phantom of human fat tissue is calculated using FEKO simulator software. Frequency used is 402 MHz. The antenna used as the receiver is a half-wave dipole antenna. The equation proposed to estimate radio link budget for NMHA has considered few parameters which are the amount of power transmitter, transmitter and receiver gain, distance between transmitter and receiver and losses such as dielectric loss, free space loss and reflection loss. The calculated power received is compared with the power received and S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub> obtained from simulation.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of Millimeter-Wave Multi-Path Propagation in Passenger Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper reports the measurement campaign and identification results of the millimeter-wave multi-path propagation characteristics at 61.5 GHz band in a passenger vehicle environment. Four measurement scenarios were assumed, and the propagation characteristics of the dominant paths in each were identified. From the results, it can be seen that the dominant paths are distributed along the line-of-sight (LoS) direction, but it could also be seen that some other communication links of which power are ranged from 10 to 15 dB smaller than that of the LoS component are available.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on Resolution Enhancement in Height for Automotive MW-3D-SAR
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Automatic driving systems of automobile have been extensively studied. In particular, automotive millimeter-wave (MW) radar is drawing attention. So far, we have studied on SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) technique for automobile to make 2D-map images. Obviously objects surrounding automobile also contain height information, hence 3D imaging will help us to discriminate object information. In this paper, we will realize 3-D imaging of an object by observing with a vertically-placed array antenna, and examine the height estimation performance of several Direction-of-Arrival estimation technique.

articleTitle: 20 GHz Bandwidth 3.84 dBi Gain InP On-chip Antenna for 300GHz Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A broadband antenna that can be used for a phased array in the 300-GHz band applicable to ultra-high speed wireless transmission system such as Beyond 5G or 6G is proposed. The antenna is composed of a split ring resonator and a patch antenna and has broadband radiation characteristics. Its small size of 1/3-wavelength means it is promising for use in a phased array. The antenna is fabricated on a 60-μm-thick InP substrate and the return characteristics and gain are evaluated. Comparison of experimental and simulated results confirm the operating bandwidth of 20 GHz (290 - 310 GHz) and there is good agreement of the two gain results in the normal direction with an average error of 0.86 dBi. Also the average peak gain of the simulated result is 3.84 dBi at the operating frequency band. The results confirmed the broadband and good gain characteristics of the antenna.

articleTitle: Plasmon Analysis for Metallic Nanocylinders Using Hydrodynamic Drude Model
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Plasmon analysis for metallic nano structure is performed by the finite-difference frequency-domain method. Dispersion of metal is represented by the hydrodynamic Drude model which can consider the non-local effect for electrons. We will clarify characteristics of plasmons when metallic nanocylinders are arranged.

articleTitle: 1×8 Slotted Array Antenna with Fan-Beam Characteristics for 28 GHz 5G Mobile Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A quasi-Yagi slotted array antenna with fan-beam characteristics for 28 GHz 5G mobile applications is proposed. The antenna is composed of a 1×8 slot antenna array with directors to enhance the half-power beamwidth (HPBW). The proposed antenna has a fan-beam radiation pattern with a simulated HPBW of 256.72° and a peak gain of 11.16 dBi. In addition, the proposed antenna covers ±48° using a beam steering mechanism. Mutual coupling reduction is achieved by inserting slits between the adjacent slot radiators on the ground plane.

articleTitle: Polarization-Sense Reconfigurable Circular Polarized Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A single fed circular polarized microstrip patch antenna excited through near field coupling is proposed. L-shape near-field feed line is used to feed the microstrip patch antenna as it is useful to control the direction of the current, and change the polarization sense of the circularly polarized wave. By using near field coupling technique, the size of the microstrip patch antenna is reduced to be less than a half-wavelength of the guided wave. Along with the size reduction, slits must be inserted into the antenna to achieve good axial ratio. Its length has been optimized numerically to generate axial ratio that cover 2.4 GHz ISM band. Experiment results shows that the proposed antenna possesses an axial ratio bandwidth of 4.1% and 10-dB return loss covers 2.35 to 2.54 GHz. The proposed antenna is eligible for a communication network that uses right- and left-handed circularly polarized wave spatially.

Author Keywords: near field coupling microstrip patch antenna

articleTitle: Application of An Efficient Method of Moments to Numerical Analysis of 1-bit Transmitarrays
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An efficient method of moments for numerical analysis of antennas with variable load impedance is presented. The presented method is a kind of domain decomposition method. A loaded full-matrix equation is decomposed into block matrix equations corresponding to unloaded and loaded parts, respectively. These block matrix equations are solved sequentially using an unloaded full-admittance matrix and currents of the antennas are obtained. The presented method is computationally efficient because matrix inversion of a loaded full-impedance matrix, which is computationally expensive, is unnecessary. The presented method is rigorous because its algorithm includes no approximation. The presented method is applied to numerical analysis of 1-bit transmitarrays and its performance is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Applications of Photonics Technology for Wireless Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We briefly introduce some results of research and development projects performed by ETRI on the RoF technology and THz wireless delivery systems.

articleTitle: A Balanced Filtering Crossover for Two Paths with Different Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a planar balanced filtering crossover with third-order bandpass response. Two paths of the crossover are designed to have different passband frequencies. The balanced crossover is designed to have good differential-mode bandpass response and good common-mode rejection for each path. In addition, good isolation between the two paths are also considered in the design process. The proposed microstrip crossover has been fabricated on RO4003C substrate. Simulated and measured results reveal the bandpass response for each path. 30-dB isolation and common-mode rejection are realized.

articleTitle: Recent Development of Substrate Edge Antennas and Arrays for Millimeter-Wave Communication
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Electromagnetic (EM) emission from substrate edges is increasing significantly when the communication systems move from the first generation to the fifth generation using millimeter waves. It is reasonable and very interesting to utilize the substrate edge to design antennas. For example, H-plane horn antennas are implemented in commercial substrates using the substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology. H-plane SIW horns have the advantages of low profile, good gain, and little EM interactions due to the closed structure. In addition, radiation from the substrate edges also can be in leaky waves, which features simple feedings, good impedance matching and high gain. Substrate edge antennas (SEAs) are easy to form arrays with multiple beams or steering beams, and also very suitable to be employed together with packaging technologies. SEAs and the arrays are very promising in the next generation communication systems, like in handset terminals.

articleTitle: OAM-based Imaging with Cylinder-shaped Arrays
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recent years, the electromagnetic (EM) wave carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM) has been applied for radar imaging. The dual relationship between the OAM index and the azimuthal angle can be used to reconstruct target's profiles in the azimuthal dimension. In this paper, the OAM-based imaging is studied to reconstruct the three-dimensional information by exploiting the tomographic technique. The wavefront and intensity distributions of the generated OAM beams are analyzed firstly. Subsequently, the imaging model of the proposed imaging scheme is derived. And, the imaging approach is developed to obtain the target's position in range, azimuth and elevation dimensions. Simulation results show good agreement with theoretical analyses. This work can advance the development of three-dimensional imaging technology based on OAM beams.

articleTitle: Periodic Fluctuations in Channel Capacity due to the Rotation of Propeller in Flying Cars MIMO
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: One of the most distinguishing characteristics in MIMO communication for flying cars, as compared with ordinary ground-based car radios, is the periodic fluctuations in channel responses due to the rotation of propeller. This paper presents effects of propeller on inter-flying cars MIMO communication. The analytical results show that the propeller gives two kinds of effects; changes in the channel gain due to shadowing and variations of the correlation due to path differences, yielding periodic instantaneous responses of MIMO channel capacity in association with the rotation of propeller.

articleTitle: Displacement Measurement by Using Millimeter Wave Interferometric-SAR
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) is a technology that virtually realizes a large-aperture antenna by radar movement. SAR enable us to monitor a wide range. In addition, Repeat-pass observation by SAR enable us to detect small displacement of the target. This is InSAR (Interferometric SAR). We also propose quasi Differential InSAR to prevent the temporal decorrelation of InSAR. In this paper, we consider the performance of InSAR and quasi Differential InSAR for slope fluctuation observation and compare them by using simulation.

articleTitle: Performance of Single-Carrier LOS-MIMO Using FDE in 3GPP TDL Channel Models
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In the future cellular systems based on heterogeneous networks (HetNets), the application of line-of-sight (LOS)-multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) to backhaul or fronthaul between a macro cell and small cells is promising from the viewpoint of low-cost deployment. For this purpose, this paper presents the bit error rate (BER) performance of single-carrier 2 ×2 LOS-MIMO using frequency domain equalization (FDE) in the 3rd generation partnership project (3GPP) tapped delay line (TDL) channel models. Computer simulation results show the effectiveness of LOS-MIMO using FDE in the 3GPP TDL based LOS channel models.

articleTitle: Design of Omni-Directional radiation antenna by using two antennas with orthogonal polarizations
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An omni-directional radiation antenna combined with two antennas with orthogonal polarizations is proposed in this paper. Different with the general "omni-directional" antennas, this proposed antenna has no obvious null both in azimuth plane and elevation plane. Two antennas are placed on the opposite sides of the platform and each antenna cover half of the space. Because the two antennas are with orthogonal polarizations, there is little interference for the two antennas, especially at the border of the two half spaces. The antennas with the platform are designed with the platform. The simulated results show that the gain is higher than -5dB for both azimuth and elevation planes. An antenna prototype was fabricated and measured. The measured radiation patterns are agreeable with the simulated ones.

articleTitle: Near Field Leaky-Wave Focusing Antenna Using Inhomogeneous Rectangular Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The near field leaky-wave focusing antenna using the inhomogeneous rectangular waveguide is proposed and a design method is presented. The height of the waveguide broad wall is inhomogeneous to obtain focusing effect at a desired position. Simulation results and measured results at Ka-band are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed design method.

articleTitle: Coaxially Fed Monopole Antenna with Choke Structure Composed of Zeroth-Order Resonator
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the coaxially fed monopole antenna with choke structure. A composite right/left-handed (CRLH) transmission line (TL) is proposed for a choke structure. By using the zeroth-order resonator for the choke structure, the relative bandwidth of 2.4% and the choke length of 0.06 wavelength of the proposed antenna are achieved.

articleTitle: 256 × 256 Large-Scale Pancake MIMO Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The prime objective of this paper is to achieve a considerable reduction in the occupied area of a 256 × 256 large-scale MIMO antenna. A novel approach that can provide a low correlation between subarrays is presented, from which we discuss the procedure for carrying out the miniaturization of large-scale MIMO arrays, aiming at accomplishing several hundreds of gigabits capacity over the full azimuth.

articleTitle: A Dual-band J-type Meander Antenna for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In recent years, small antennas have been developed for portable devices such as smartphones and tablet PC devices. As the development of electronic devices progresses toward IoT, miniaturization of antennas with high performance are required rapidly. Sharing of a terminal for multiple frequencies is demanded to use several wireless systems. In this project, we study on a J-type antenna that enables dual frequency sharing and conduct research on miniaturization. After simulations of fundamental J-type antennas were examined to understand the principle of dual frequency sharing, miniaturization of the J-type antenna was conducted with meander elements. In this report, we research the miniaturization of the J-type antenna for the purpose of sharing in the 5G frequency bands. After the dual-band J-type meander antenna is simulated, characteristics of the antenna are clarified in measurement.

articleTitle: Design of a Triple-band and Wideband Multi-Ring Microstrip Antenna fed by an L-probe
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents design of a triple-band and wideband multi-ring microstrip antenna (MR-MSA) fed by an L-probe. The proposed antenna consists of two ring patches, a square patch, and an L-probe to excite the patches arranged at different layers of a quadruple-layered dielectric substrate. The design frequencies are 3.5 GHz, 4.75 GHz, and 7.5 GHz. The two ring patches and the one square patch for the lower middle, and higher bands are placed at the first to third layers of the substrate from the top, respectively. The L-probe is situated at the bottom layer on the ground plane. By using a thick substrate for the L-probe and optimizing the other dimensions, triple-band and wideband performance can be obtained. In this paper, the triple-band and wideband MR-MSA for the three target frequencies aforementioned is designed by using numerical simulation with Zeland IE3D. A PTFE substrate with a relative dielectric constant of 2.6 is used for the designed MR-MSA. By choosing 4.8 mm thickness for the bottom layer of the substrate and 7.8 mm overall height of the MR-MSA, fractional bandwidths of less than -10 reflection are predicted to be 11.3%, 4.6%, and 4.5% for the first to third bands, respectively.

articleTitle: Basic Shape Classification of Buried Object Using Pattern Matching in Ultrawideband Radar Image
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes the pattern matching technique to the signal pattern of windowed B-scan data to classify the object cross-section shape. The technique applies the dynamic time wrapping to adaptively measure the similarity of the object under test and the reference object. As studied case, we consider a metallic object with three basic shapes: circle, square, and triangle. To check the generality and performance of the proposed technique, we conduct the simulations and experimental studies with an ultra-wideband impulse radar. According to the results, the proposed technique is feasible enough, and it is applicable over the wide possible environments.

articleTitle: Compact High Efficiency Terahertz Filtering Antenna with Low Cross-Polarization Based on the Mixed-Mode Cavity
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper investigates a D-band high-efficiency filtering antenna with low cross-polarization, which consists of a mixed-mode cavity, a TE440-mode cavity and a slot array. The mixed-mode cavity is deployed for achieving filtering power dividing. Hence, a compact size and high radiation efficiency are achieved for terahertz antenna applications. For verification, a 140-GHz 4×4 filtering slot array is fabricated and measured. The measured gain varies from 17.4 to 18.51 dBi within 16.72 FBW (125.7-148.63 GHz), and the peak aperture and radiation efficiencies are about 77.25% and 96.46%. In addition, the suppression level in stopband is higher than 39 dB.

articleTitle: Estimation of electromagnetic far-field from near-field using machine learning
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this development, we proposed a method to use machine learning to estimate a far-field from a near-field. A signal source and wires randomly arranged on the substrate are used as a radiation source. The near and far-fields emitted from the substrate are calculated by electromagnetic field simulation to produce the data necessary for machine learning. We used XGBoost for machine learning. The Route Mean Square Percentage Error (RMSPE) of the far-field strength of the estimated and test data was calculated and was less than 7.1 % at 1-6 GHz.

articleTitle: Empirical Formulas for Performance Prediction of Concrete Embedded Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: To mitigate the space occupation and aesthetic problems of indoor dense small cell deployment, a microstrip antenna with multiple layer configuration operating at 3.5 GHz is embedded in concrete all for indoor communication. The impact of embedding depth and concrete dielectric constant on antenna gain and input reactance are investigated, and simple empirical formulas are obtained based on full-wave simulation. The results in present work provide a good guidance to antenna designers and architects for concrete embedded antenna deployment and communication-friendly building materials selection.

articleTitle: Connecting Networks for Two-Dimensional Butler Matrices With Improved Aggregate Gain
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The concept of connecting networks for two-dimensional beamforming networks is introduced. It enables to generate a triangular lattice of beams providing an improvement in aggregate gain over conventional Butler matrices. The connecting network is used to rearrange the output ports of a two-dimensional beamformer to produce a planar array with the desired properties. A key feature of the design is the use of a twist matrix which enables to maintain wideband performance. The concept is demonstrated with numerical results at 22 GHz.

articleTitle: EBG Inspired Pattern and Polarization Reconfigurable Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the use of electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structure in the pattern and polarization reconfigurable antenna for beam-steering configurations. The proposed antenna consists a group of EBG structure to control the pattern reconfigurability. While two triangular slits are introduces on the square patches to give polarization reconfigurability. The PIN diode is used as the switching method. A maximum +15° and -15° of beam steering is achieved at both linear and circular polarization.

articleTitle: Hemispherical Pattern Double-Cross Dipole Antenna for a Fixed-site Ground Station
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes the design of a double-cross dipole antenna for a low-earth orbit satellite ground station. A fixed-site ground station needs to receive signals at all time while satellites pass through the territorial airspace. The proposed antenna has a radiation pattern as the hemispherical, so it can receive signals from all directions. It has a reflection coefficient of -30.51 dB at 137.1 MHz with a maximum gain of 2.7 dBi. The testing signal reception of the fixed-site ground station using the proposed antenna, the receiver can decode and display images from NOAA-19 satellite for further analysis of satellite images.

articleTitle: A Compact Multiband Circularly Polarized Antenna Exploiting Meander Geometry
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A compact triple-band circularly polarized (CP) planar monopole antenna is presented for wireless communication. The proposed antenna design consists of a meander geometry and two orthogonal stubs in the top layer, whereas a vertical slot is etched in the partial ground plane. The geometry exhibits 10-dB impedance bandwidth of 450 MHz (3.83-4.28 GHz), 560 MHz (5.41-5.97 GHz), and 830 MHz (6.47-7.3 GHz) at three different resonant frequencies. The 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth obtained around these resonances are 4.29%, 4.03%, and 3.52% with respect to 4.1 GHz, 5.8 GHz, and 6.7 GHz, respectively. In addition, the proposed antenna exhibits an improved miniaturized performance having an overall size of 0.35λ × 0.39λ, where λ is the free space wavelength at the lowest CP frequency. Moreover, the antenna has a simple topology, broadside radiation, and moderate gain. The proposed structure has been fabricated and its measured responses are in good agreement with the simulated results.

articleTitle: All-metal Broadband Circularly Polarized Feed Antenna Applied to Millimeter Wave Imaging System
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In order to eliminate the tail shadow caused by unstable structure like substrate integrated circularly polarized antenna, an antipodal exponential-logarithmic slot antenna (ALETSA) is improved to achieve an ultra-wideband circular polarization, low side lobe level, low loss and wide beam at W band and F band. The improved ALETSA is directly fed by a standard rectangular waveguide and loaded with rectangular slots. The relative working bandwidth reaches more than 77.7%. The optimized AELTSA realizes that return loss is below -17 dB, side lobe lower than -18 dB and the axial ratio lower than 3 dB from 70 to 140 GHz.

articleTitle: Experimental evaluation of series resonance scheme for 2 × 2 MIMO IPT
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In an inductive power transfer (IPT) consisting of one transmitter and one receiver, series resonant capacitors are inserted on both sides to achieve high power transfer efficiency and load-independent output current. However, when IPT is carried from multiple transmitters to multiple receivers, the load currents vary with the load resistances due to impact of cross talk among the coils. As an initial attempt to address this problem, we proposed 2 × 2 series resonant scheme to mitigate cross talk and achieve constant load currents for IPT system with two transmitters and two receivers. Effectiveness of our proposal is confirmed by experiments.

articleTitle: Design of a Miniaturized Log Periodic Dipole Antenna Using a T-loaded Structure with Dual-Polarization for Electronic Warfare Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a miniaturized log periodic dipole antenna (LPDA) with dual-polarization for electronic warfare applications. The broadband and high bore-sight gain characteristics are obtained by adjusting the lengths and spacings of the arms. The T-loaded structure is also employed at the end of each arm in order to miniaturize the antenna size. The proposed dual-polarized LPDA has a bore-sight gain of more than 3 dBi from 2 GHz to 6 GHz, where the maximum of 5.9 dBi is obtained at 4.2 GHz. The single log periodic antenna is then extended to an 8×8 slant array.

articleTitle: Feasibility study of the bandwidth expansion for MACKEY S1 type with a short-circuit board
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A meta-surface inspired antenna chip developed by the KIT EOE Laboratory (MACKEY), which integrates a dipole antenna and an artificial magnetic conductor, has been developed [1]. We devised the MACKEY S1 type with one short-circuited side and demonstrated that it could be made smaller [2]. This paper presents a study on the widening bandwidth of the S1 type.

articleTitle: Focusing Lens Design to Achieve Small Focal Spot Size in Human Body
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In microwave hyperthermia, a focusing structure is designed to concentrate microwave at specific region inside human body. It is very important to find out the minimum spot size of the focused point. In this paper, a focusing lens to focus microwave inside human body at 2.45 GHz is designed and the calculation method is validated using Method of Moment (MoM). Small spot size of 1.54 cm is achieved.

articleTitle: Wide-angle Ultra-Wideband PolSAR Imaging Simulation of Canonical Targets
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: By adopting an ultra-wide bandwidth and exploiting a wide-angle synthetic aperture, SAR can achieve high spatial resolutions in the range and azimuth directions, respectively. Incorporate with polarimetry diversity, which allows to explore the polarimetric scattering mechanism of the illuminated targets. Integrated these characteristics aforementioned, wide-angle ultra-wideband polarimetric synthetic aperture radar with canonical targets have been investigated numerically and experimentally. To further validate the simulated results, the corresponding experiment with a dihedral was conducted by a GB-SAR system in the field, which exhibit good agreement with the simulated results.

articleTitle: Digital GoB-based Beamforming for 5G Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: 5G is the next mobile generation and it is expected to bring massive changes in our society. Various technologies are being studied to be used with the future communication systems, two of them being the use of massive MIMO with beamforming techniques. Particularly, GoB beamforming is a digital beamforming method that has been investigated to be used with 5G systems. This paper evaluates the performance of a 5G communication system that makes use of massive MIMO embedded with GoB beamforming, in terms of BER and throughput.

articleTitle: Review of S-band and X-band Antennas and Filters for both Maritime and Space applications
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The paper presents review of development SIW antennas and filters for both CubeSats and maritime solutions. Several examples of sector antennas for S-band were presented. Some improvements in gain of antenna arrays were discussed. The examples of X-band filters and diplexers were describe. Some differences in solutions for both bands were discussed. The influence of the substrate parameters used was presented.

articleTitle: Compact Dual-Band Dual-Polarized Filtering Antenna for 5G Base Station Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a novel ±45° dual-band and dual-polarized antenna for 5G sub-6 GHz base station applications. The proposed dual-band antenna consists of an upper-band (4.8−5 GHz) cross-dipole embedded into a lower-band (3.4−3.6 GHz) magneto-electric (ME) dipole. Without using extra filtering circuit, filtering response can be realized in the upper-band and lower-band antennas. Therefore, mutual coupling between the two antennas can be suppressed intrinsically and the cross-band port-to-port isolation is higher than 25 dB. The proposed antenna is a good candidate for 5G multi-band base station applications.

articleTitle: Experimental and Theoretical Studies on Communicable Distance for Medical Telemeters between Hospitals Located with a Distance of 1,300 Meters
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In Japan, medical telemeters managing patients' biological information via electromagnetic waves have been widely used. However, electromagnetic interferences caused by the electromagnetic waves emitted from telemeters in distant hospitals are an issue of major concern. In this study, we focused on two hospitals which are located 1,300 meters apart and had previously experienced interferences. We thus measured the electromagnetic waves emitted from a telemeter installed in one of those hospitals. Based on the estimation from theoretical equations in which loss of the electromagnetic waves due to the structural objects between the two hospitals taken into account, we found that it is possible to detect electro-magnetic waves even at a distance of 121.6 meters. We then deduce that extraordinary propagation due to such as tropospheric reflections might cause the interferences (electromagnetic wave propagation) emitted from medical telemeters even at a distance of 1,300 meters.

articleTitle: High-performance UWB mmWave Smart Bowtie Array Antenna Technology for 5G Access and backhauling Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Smart Bowtie array antenna technology is a recently developed one, aiming to provide UWB solutions to antennas in 5G mmWave access and backhauling systems. This technology enables the simultaneous multiple beams with large beam scan angles and tracking ability, with high gain and high antenna efficiency over an ultra-wideband (UWB) at low manufacturing cost. This paper will presents several designs to show the features and characteristics of the technology.

articleTitle: Higher symmetries in holey structures applied to gap waveguide technology: fundamentals and considerations
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The use of higher symmetries in periodic structures has made possible the development of new designs of microwave components with enhanced properties. Significant potential of this new way of making periodic structures can also be applied in design of electromagnetic band-gap (EBG) structures. This can simplify the manufacturing of components in gap waveguide technology, but at the same time it is necessary to respect some limitations and challenging design aspects. In this work, we will discuss the properties of EBG glide-symmetrical holey structures and how to apply them in the realization of gap waveguide technology.

articleTitle: Spreading Factor Allocation using the Standard Deviation Classification Method
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes the standard deviation (SD) classification method to improve the long range wide area network (LoRaWAN) resource allocation. The proposed method distributes spreading factors (SFs) by considering means and standard deviations of receive signal strength indicator (RSSI) values of the end devices. The simulation is performed for a rural environment whose signal propagation characteristics are governed by the Hata-Okumura propagation model. It is shown that the SD classification method distributes more SFs to the end devices and clearly offers higher data extraction rate (DER) than that of the original adaptive data rate (ADR) scheme.

articleTitle: A Self-Decoupled Antenna Pair Using Shared Radiator With Orthogonal Modes
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a novel self-decoupled antenna pair using a shared radiator is proposed for mobile terminals. Two orthogonal modes, a dipole mode and a monopole mode, can be excited simultaneously at the same radiator so that it can achieve inherent high isolation and low spatial correlation. A single-band demonstrational example is analyzed to reveal the working mechanism. The simulated results show that the isolation is better than 60 dB throughout the whole band. Moreover, a dual-band extension can be obtained by just adding another two branches, which largely reduces the complexity of design and implementation for dual-band applications.

articleTitle: Estimation of Total Interference Power by Clustering Multiple Wireless Nodes
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: For effective computation of the interference in an environment with multiple nodes, we propose a scheme clustering multiple interference nodes and estimating the total interference power of the cluster. The total interference power is obtained by adding a margin to a reference interference power calculated using geographic information of a limited number of representative nodes. The margin is empirically set to avoid under-estimation of the interference power at an outage probability. Through simulations of the total interference power in a street canyon environment, we evaluated the excess amount of the estimated total interference power in several methods to calculate the reference interference power. As a result, we show that the amount of the excessively estimated power can be reduced by selecting an appropriate way to calculate the reference interference power.

articleTitle: Design and Evaluation of ESPAR Antenna using Hexagonal Microstrip Patch with Hole
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the electronically steerable parasitic array radiator (ESPAR) antenna using hexagonal microstrip patch with hole has been designed, and S-parameter and beam pattern have been evaluated. As simulation results, it is confirmed that the designed antenna can perform beamforming with single radio frequency (RF) chain. It is also confirmed that the designed antenna can support the maximum beam gain from about 6 dBi to about 7 dBi and operating bandwidth of 160 MHz.

articleTitle: Human Blockage Loss Characteristics at 5 GHz Bands in A Crowded Stadium
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper reports on human blockage loss characteristics based on the measurement results in a crowded stadium environment. The measurements were taken at the Japan National Stadium, which will be used at the opening ceremonies of the Tokyo 2020 Olympics and Paralympics. We measured the received signal strength (RSSI) with smartphones (UEs) using the Wi-Fi signal from various access points (APs) installed throughout the stadium for actual service. The measurement data were acquired in the unoccupied state before the event and in the crowded state after the event started. We analyzed the human blockage loss characteristics and found that while the human blockage loss does not depend on the distance between the AP-UEs, it does differ depending on the location, and follows a normal distribution with a median value of 7.2 dB and standard deviation of 5.5 dB.

articleTitle: Robust Source Number Estimation Based on FMCW Radar with Multiple Initial Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We propose a new method to estimate the number of the sources for super-resolution DOA (Direction of Arrival) estimator with FMCW (Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave) -MIMO (Multi-Input Multi-Output) radar. The main idea is using the principle that the phase of the intermediate signals depend on the initial frequency of transmitted signals. We confirmed that the new method can distinguish the true DOA and the spurious when the number of sources is larger than the number of true sources.

articleTitle: Gain enhancement and miniaturization of UWB antenna using metamaterial-based FSS
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a compact, low profile ultra-wideband antenna. The proposed antenna consists of a simple rectangular shape placed at a distance h = 10 mm in front of a frequency selective surface. The antenna has a reflection coefficient lower than 10 dB from 3.4 to 11.3 GHz, and a maximum gain of 7.29 dBi at 5 GHz where the gain is increased by 5 dBi over the antenna without FSS. The overall size of the design is 50 mm × 45 mm × 10 mm. Measured results show good agreement with simulated ones.

articleTitle: Anti-Collision of RFID Tags with Blind DS-CDMA Using ICA
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We proposed an anti-collision technique for RFID uplink signals that requires only one antenna and one query using DS-CDMA blind inverse spreading technique. In order to avoid interference, the tag generates a random code for each query and spreads the data. In order to decode the signal spread with an unknown code, blind inverse diffusion is performed using independent component analysis. This eliminates the need for multiple queries and does not require complex control between reader and tag. Blind inverse spreading does not require special hardware and the protocol can be extremely simple, making it possible to create reliable and fast tags and readers at lower cost.

articleTitle: Design of Deployable Center-Fed Reflectarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper a deployable center-fed reflectarray antenna for mobile satellite communication systems is proposed. The proposed antenna consists of a main-substrate, four sub-substrates, and a backfire antenna. It can be easily installed by attaching the backfire antenna and deploying the folded sub-substrates. In this study, the proposed antenna is designed, and its characteristics are analyzed. The results show that the antenna can satisfy a target gain by adjusting the deployment angle of the sub-substrates.

articleTitle: Wideband H-Slot Antenna Fed by Substrate Integrated Gap Waveguide for mmWave Arrays
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a wideband slot antenna design based on the substrate integrated gap waveguide technology for millimetre wave applications. The proposed antenna is realized using the H-shaped slot (H-slot) to improve impedance bandwdith. Simulation results show that the proposed antenna has an impedance bandwidth at S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> ≤-15 dB from 24-29.5 GHz resulting in a 20.5% fractional bandwidth. Hence, the designed slot antenna can potentially be used as the radiating element of an array antenna for fixed-beam point-to-point applications.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of FBP and CS Methods on Microwave Tomography
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the investigation and comparative analysis of image reconstruction performance on microwave tomography, namely filtered back projection (FBP) and compressive sensing (CS). The investigation is carried out by processing a picture of tree trunk object with a pixel size of 128 × 128. Performance comparison are assessed using mean square error (MSE) and structural similarity index measure (SSIM) parameters. The result of image reconstruction using CS method has better MSE and SSIM with the value of 0.001 and 0.837, respectively, for smaller image pixel, while the result of using FBP method has SSIM value of 0.901.

articleTitle: Influence of Beam Spot Size in Measurement of Pulse Waves at Multiple Parts of the Human Body Using Millimeter-wave Array Radar
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study evaluates the accuracy of measurements of cardiac pulse wave propagation using a 79-GHz millimeter-wave ultra-wideband multiple-input multiple-output array radar. The radar echoes from multiple parts of the human body were extracted using an array beamforming technique. The phase of each echo was converted to the skin displacement and its waveform was carefully compared with the waveform obtained using laser displacement sensors, which was used as a reference for evaluation of accuracy. Because the beam spot sizes of the radar and laser sensors were different, we applied smoothing to the waveform measured using the laser sensor, to make the effective beam spot size equivalent to the spot size of the array radar beam. We then quantitatively analyzed the relationship between body displacement waveforms measured using the array radar and laser sensors.

articleTitle: Design of Broadband Handset Antenna Based On Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a broadband mobile handset antenna with a metal bezel is analyzed by utilizing the theory of characteristic modes (TCM). Through the design of monopole and T-shaped structures, four different characteristic modes of the antenna are excited, and the dual-frequency characteristic of the antenna is realized. At the same time, by loading an inductive element on the monopole, the high-order mode frequency of the monopole is shifted to the lower-frequency, which will expand the bandwidth of the antenna. The simulated results exhibit -6dB bandwidths of the proposed antenna are 820-960 MHz and 1500-2940 MHz.

articleTitle: Sparse Synthesis Aperture Imaging using Multistatic Coprime Scheme
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a mmWave-based imaging method which applies multistatic radar and coprime measurements, to reduce the number of antenna and the amount of data. It replaces every monostatic radar by a pair of separated transmitter and receiver along with phase corrections. A plurality of receivers can simultaneously receive the reflection when a transmitter emits signals. Our proposal is testified by an equivalent experiment and the results indicate that the multistatic coprime measurement is implementable and can reduce the number of antenna to about 0.3% of the standard SAR (using half-wavelength measurements).

articleTitle: Robust Source Number Estimation using Annihilating Filter and Downsampling Scheme
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This papers presents an accurate source number estimation method for MIMO radars. We propose the novel source number estimation method that utilizing SVD for detecting the desired signals. To accelerate the performance, applying downsampling preprocessing by removing undesired components. Estimation performance of the proposed method is evaluated through computer simulation.

articleTitle: An on-chip antenna with an area of 0.9 square millimeters for RFID applications in the 5.8 GHz – 24 GHz range
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A millimeter-sized on-chip antenna is presented. The antenna is composed of two loops, and the impedance of the antenna can be adapted by modifying the shape of one loop without altering antenna gain. The proposed antenna was matched to different rectifier circuits at the 5.8 GHz and 24 GHz frequencies, and achieved a gain of -23.7 dBi and -13.3 dBi respectively. The antenna was tested at 5.8 GHz in conjunction with a low-power RFID circuit and enough power was supplied for the circuit to function at a distance of 7 cm from the power supply.

articleTitle: Theoretical Analysis of Position Report Verification using Distance-based Localization
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Position verification is a technique used to check the validity of a position report sent from a mobile station (MS) to a base station (BS), with the aim of detecting spoofing. For example, the MS-BS distance measured by an independent means can be used. Position verification is different from traditional localization in various aspects. However, localization also can be used for position verification when enough measurements are available. To find the best approach, position verification with and without localization should be compared. As part of the effort, the test statistic of position verification with localization is derived in this paper.

articleTitle: BLOS Propagation Measurements in Gdansk Bay
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The article presents the results of measurement radio communication subsystem. The radio links operating in 0.4-0.45 GHz and 2-2.5 GHz ranges in sea environment were described. The results were compared with propagation models for horizon, over (OTH) and beyond line of sight BLOS sea link.

articleTitle: A Transparent Antenna For Hybrid Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel transparent metasurface antenna (metantenna) based on ITO material is proposed in this paper, which has good optical transmittance while realizing RF energy harvesting. This shows that it has the potential of Solar/RF hybrid energy harvesting. The proposed metantenna based on an aperture-coupled structure, of which the slotted ground and metasurface structure are etched with ITO (1Ω/sq). A impedance bandwidth of 43.6% from 1.40 GHz to 2.18 GHz is obtained to cover 2G and 3G wireless communication bands. At the same time, an antenna array was designed to verify its ability to harvest RF energy.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Large-Scale MIMO Antenna Using the Double-Ring Structure
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a miniaturized large-scale MIMO antenna for mobile stations. The use of double-ring structure comprising the inner and outer 64 × 64 MIMO arrays provides a compact 128 × 128 MIMO array due to an efficient array arrangement under the two-dimensional spatial constraint condition. A simple EM model comprising three elements is proposed, and a theoretical investigation is performed to determine the optimum radius of the inner array.
